title: Agent pods authenticate to LiteLLM with the MASTER ADMIN KEY, so the per-project budget door is not in force
description:
CONFIRMED BY DIRECT COMPARISON, 2026-09-06: the key in /city/agents/triage/agent.toml is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the LiteLLM MASTER ADMIN KEY, and is NOT the project's virtual key.

  agent key == master admin key      YES
  agent key == project virtual key   NO

HOW IT HAPPENS. The controller's bootstrap reads the admin key --
LITELLM_KEY=$(cat .../secrets/litellm/adminKey) in workload-gonk-controller.yaml
-- and writes it into every agent.toml as GONK_LITELLM_KEY. The entrypoint then
materialises GONK_LITELLM_KEY into /tmp/gonk/llkey, and opencode's provider
config points its apiKey at that file. So every agent session authenticates to
the proxy as the PROXY ADMIN.

CONSEQUENCE 1 -- THE BUDGET DOOR IS NOT IN FORCE, and this is what makes
gonk-1zm's fix inert on the path that matters. The meter provisions a per-project
virtual key with a real max_budget (verified: $25 = 0 + 50M * 5e-7 for the e2e
project) and keysinks it to gonk-key-<project>-<hash>. NOTHING USES IT. The admin
key has no alias and no budget, so agent spend accrues against a key that cannot
run out. Synthetic pricing is now correct AND unreachable by agent traffic: I
proved the rate works only by calling with the project key by hand.

CONSEQUENCE 2 -- PRIVILEGE. The LiteLLM master key can list, create, update and
delete EVERY virtual key on that proxy, including other workloads' (OpenClaw
shares it) and including the keys gonk itself relies on for metering. gonk-e9m
establishes that issue text can obtain a shell in the agent pod. That puts
untrusted issue text one step away from the proxy's admin credential, on a pod
whose whole security story is "holds no credentials it does not need".

THE FIX is to hand the agent the PROJECT'S virtual key rather than the admin key.
The plumbing already exists and is already used for the prompt: the meter
keysinks the key to a secret, and the per-session channel is GC_ALIAS. What is
missing is the delivery -- agent.toml's static GONK_LITELLM_KEY is a PER-INSTALL
channel, and a project key is PER-PROJECT, so it cannot ride that channel at all.
Options, in rough order of preference:
  1. Deliver the key with the prompt. The pod already fetches a per-session row
     from the meter by alias (gonk-mzd); the key ref belongs in that row. The
     meter already models KeyRef and deliberately never puts the key itself in an
     API response, so this needs a decision about whether the prompt route may
     carry it or whether the pod should read the keysinked secret.
  2. Mount the keysinked secret into the session pod, which means the pod spec
     must vary per project -- Gas City's k8s provider composes it, so this may be
     an upstream ask.
  3. Keep the static channel but make it a NON-ADMIN key with no budget, which
     fixes the privilege half and leaves the budget half broken. A stopgap, and
     it should be labelled as one.

UNTIL THEN, state the invariant honestly: gonk has per-project budget ACCOUNTING
(the meter attributes spend from /spend/logs metadata) but not per-project budget
ENFORCEMENT at the door. The reservation gate in the meter remains the primary
control, which is what spec 9 always said -- but the LiteLLM ceiling that was
supposed to be the backstop is not currently a backstop for agent traffic.

title: BLOCKER: the GitLab registry volume is 100% full, so no image can be pushed at all
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while trying to deploy the rig checkout work. THIS BLOCKS EVERY DEPLOY, not just gonk's.

SYMPTOM. All 8 image jobs in pipeline 2124 failed. lint and test passed; the failure is at the push:
    error checking push permissions ... POST http://gitlab-registry.gitlab.svc.cluster.local:5000/v2/agentic/gonk-project/gonk-intake/blobs/uploads/:
    UNKNOWN: map[DriverName:filesystem Enclosed:map[Err:28 Op:mkdir Path:/var/lib/registry/.../_uploads/...]]
Err:28 is ENOSPC. The message says 'check push permissions', which is misleading -- authentication is fine, the disk is full.

MEASURED in the registry pod (gitlab-registry-5cc785db66-nw56k):
    /dev/longhorn/pvc-daae18b0...  296G size  296G used  0 avail  100%  /var/lib/registry
    blobs/        295G
    repositories/ 684M
    (gonk's kaniko cache: 9.6M -- not the cause)

DIAGNOSIS. 295G of blobs against 684M of manifests/tags is the signature of UNREFERENCED BLOBS: layers no longer pointed at by any manifest. A Docker registry never reclaims those on its own -- deleting a tag only unlinks the manifest, and the blobs stay forever until an explicit garbage collection runs. Every CI rebuild pushes fresh layers, so this grows monotonically and was always going to reach the ceiling.

NOT a gonk-specific problem, and gonk is unlikely to be the main consumer: gonk's whole repository tree is a fraction of the 684M, while the 295G is shared across everything the registry has ever held.

OPTIONS, owner's call -- shared infrastructure, so I did not act:
 1. GARBAGE COLLECT.  reclaims unreferenced blobs and is the purpose-built remedy. It should run with the registry READ-ONLY or quiesced: a blob being uploaded by an in-flight push can otherwise be collected between its upload and its manifest write. Expect it to reclaim most of the 295G. Add  to also drop manifests no tag points at.
 2. EXPAND THE PVC. storageclass longhorn has ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION=true, so 300Gi can be raised in place. Buys time, does not stop the growth.
 3. BOTH, which is the honest answer: GC now, then a scheduled GC so this does not recur silently.

WORTH ADDING REGARDLESS: an alert on registry volume usage. This failed as an opaque 'check push permissions' error on 8 parallel jobs, and nothing anywhere said 'the disk is full' -- the same silent-failure signature as gonk-zp3 and friends, just in the infrastructure layer.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-12: the OPTIONS block in the description above lost two command strings to shell expansion when it was filed. The intended text is:

 1. GARBAGE COLLECT. Run the registry's own garbage-collect against its config (registry garbage-collect /etc/docker/registry/config.yml) -- it reclaims unreferenced blobs and is the purpose-built remedy. It should run with the registry READ-ONLY or quiesced: a blob being uploaded by an in-flight push can otherwise be collected between its upload and its manifest write. Expect it to reclaim most of the 295G. The --delete-untagged flag additionally drops manifests no tag points at.
 2. EXPAND THE PVC. storageclass longhorn has ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION=true, so 300Gi can be raised in place. Buys time, does not stop the growth.
 3. BOTH, which is the honest answer: GC now, then a scheduled GC so this does not recur silently.
RESOLVED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-17. Measured in the registry pod: 296G size, 101G used, 195G avail, 35% on /var/lib/registry. The 295G of unreferenced blobs is gone -- roughly 195G reclaimed, against the 179G predicted by gonk-1t4's attribution, the remainder being non-gonk repos. Two things did it: gonk-1t4's tag prune (921 tags) and the registry-side garbage collect run on the gitops side (steve/gitops bead gitops-4uk4, closed).

NOT closing this as 'went away' -- the reclaim was executed deliberately and the numbers reconcile. The recurrence half is already carried by gonk-07f (cleanup policy on gonk-project plus an alert on the registry volume), which is where the 'stop it happening silently again' work belongs. This bead was the incident, gonk-07f is the guard.

Was blocking gonk-3so (Phase 1 implementation agent) as a P0 for five days after the condition had actually cleared.
close_reason: Registry reclaimed: 101G/296G, 35% used, 195G free (verified in-pod 2026-08-17). Recurrence guard is gonk-07f.

title: LiteLLM key update re-sends the alias and is rejected as a duplicate of itself, so every re-registered project sticks in key-missing
description:
ROOT CAUSE OF THE TRIAGE OUTAGE, found 2026-08-10 while diagnosing gonk-zp3.

internal/meter/litellm/admin_http.go updateByAlias resolved the key's hashed token id and then POSTed /key/update with the ORIGINAL request body -- which still carried key_alias. LiteLLM's alias-uniqueness check does not exclude the key being updated, so re-asserting a key's own alias is rejected as a duplicate of ITSELF:

  400 Key with alias 'gonk-agentic-gonk-e2e-1784441480' already exists.
      Unique key aliases across all keys are required.

Verified against the live LiteLLM v1.92.0: the identical /key/update with key_alias omitted returns 200.

THE CHAIN: /key/generate 400s 'already exists' (correct, the key does exist) -> updateByAlias -> /key/update WITH alias -> 400 -> EnsureKey returns an error -> meter records StateKeyMissing -> intake answers every webhook 200 and drops it with reason=state_key-missing -> gonk-dispatch NEVER FIRES -> no session, no triage, no artifact. Confirmed live: gonk_intake_dispatch_dropped_total{reason="state_key-missing"} 1 for the Issue Hook of a freshly filed issue, and zero gonk-dispatch order.fired events in the city log.

WHY IT LOOKED INTERMITTENT: it only bites a project whose key ALREADY exists in LiteLLM, i.e. one being RE-registered. homelab/talos-toolkit stayed active purely because its config hash never changed, so reconcileProject short-circuits and never re-registers. agentic/gonk-e2e-1784441480 lost its stored key_ref and so re-registers every pass and fails every pass.

WHY NOBODY SAW IT: service.go swallowed keyErr entirely -- the comment literally said 'Fail closed, but not loud'. No log, no event, no metric carrying the reason. Working it out from outside took a packet-for-packet replay of the meter's calls against live LiteLLM.

WHY THE TESTS PASSED: the fake in admin_http_test.go accepted ANY /key/update body, so it encoded the assumed contract rather than the real one and agreed with the adapter forever. Same trap as the 202 contract (see memory when-a-gascity-api-answers-202).

FIXED: updateByAlias clears reqBody.KeyAlias before /key/update; the fake now rejects a body containing key_alias exactly as real v1.92.0 does (mutation-tested: restoring the alias fails the test); service.go now WARNs with project, alias and error; cmd/gonk-meter calls slog.SetDefault so that record lands in the pod log.
close_reason: Closed

title: gonk stack down on arm64: hand-pushed amd64-only images overwrote CI multi-arch indexes
description:
The whole gonk stack has been down for ~6 days. controller (1593 restarts) and meter (1100 restarts) are on orac04 (arm64) and die with 'exec format error'; intake is Running-but-never-Ready on johnny because it cannot reach the dead meter.

ROOT CAUSE: all four unsuffixed image tags for v0.1.0-80f906b34717 are SINGLE-PLATFORM amd64 manifests (no 'manifests' array). CI pipeline 1935 built correct amd64+arm64 legs and published correct OCI indexes at 02:16-02:37 UTC on 2026-08-04. The unsuffixed tags' image configs are stamped 05:06-05:16 UTC -- ~3h later -- i.e. a by-hand 'make push' from an amd64 box overwrote all four CI indexes with amd64-only images. Flux was then pointed at those tags.

The per-arch tags (-amd64/-arm64) are INTACT and CORRECT: running :v0.1.0-80f906b34717-arm64 on orac04 works (NODEARCH=aarch64, ELF e_machine=0xb7).

FIX: roll forward. Fix the lint error blocking HEAD's pipeline, let CI build multi-arch images for HEAD, bump the four gitops tags to the new SHA (a new tag also forces a fresh pull, working around imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent).

Blocks: nothing in gonk works until this is done.
close_reason: Fixed by rolling forward to v0.1.0-38d5cb3c883e (CI pipeline 2008), verified from OUTSIDE CI to be a real multi-arch index for all four images: distinct child per platform, each child's config reporting the matching architecture. Proven executing on orac04 (arm64): controller NODEARCH=aarch64 with /bin/sh ELF e_machine=0xb7 and gonk-gate --version reporting v0.1.0-38d5cb3c883e; agent likewise; meter and intake both EXECUTE (they reach their own flag/config validation instead of 'exec format error'). All three deployments 1/1 Ready. Root cause was a by-hand 'make push' overwriting four correct CI indexes -- follow-up gonk-9ub. The verification gap that let it stay green is homelab/ci-templates!4.

title: gonk NEVER closes an agent session; every dispatch leaks a 500m/1Gi pod until the cluster cannot schedule
description:
FOUND while diagnosing gonk-pev, 2026-08-03, live on orac. This is the cause of gonk-pev,
not a side finding.

THE FACT: there is no CloseSession, DeleteSession, suspend or prune call anywhere in gonk.
  grep -rn "CloseSession|DeleteSession|StopSession" --include=*.go cmd pkg  ->  nothing
The broker creates a session per dispatch (POST /v0/city/{city}/sessions), gonk-sweep reads
its transcript, classifies the outcome, applies the effects batch -- and then leaves the
session running forever. Gas City does not reap it either: sleep_after_idle is unset on
every agent in the pack, so the session beads carry
  effective_sleep_after_idle=off, sleep_policy_source=legacy_off, sleep_capability=timed_only
and the pod stays "active" indefinitely.

THE COST: each session pod requests 500m CPU / 1Gi memory. As of today ns gonk holds 13 of
them = 6.5 CPU / 13Gi. Eleven are triage sessions from 2026-08-01 whose LAST ACTIVE is two
days ago. The three schedulable nodes are at johnny mem 98%, orac04 mem 91%, venus cpu 96%
of requests, so EVERY new session pod is now Pending/FailedScheduling -- including the
control-dispatcher, which has been in a create-wait60s-timeout-recreate loop for 2h45m,
and including the broker-created scaffold session in gonk-pev.

WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT: same shape as every bug in sessions 5 and 6. A leaked
session is a silent success. The dispatch succeeds, the triage comment posts, the sweep
classifies, the suite stays green -- and the only symptom appears days later, in a
different trigger, as a delivery timeout. The test to write first is the one that asks
what it would look like if teardown silently did nothing.

WHAT TO BUILD (design, not settled):
1. gonk-sweep closes the session it has just classified. Sweep is already the component
   that decides a session is finished and has its outcome; it is the only place that knows
   teardown is safe. `gc session close` / the API equivalent. This is the real fix, because
   it is deterministic and does not wait on a timer.
2. sleep_after_idle on every model agent in the pack as the SAFETY NET, for sessions sweep
   never reaches (infra failure, sweep down, an outcome it cannot classify). Never as the
   primary mechanism -- a timer-based reap makes the leak slower, not absent.
3. A reaper for sessions with no live bead at all, so a leak can never again accumulate
   silently to the point of wedging the scheduler.
4. The test: a dispatch that completes must leave ZERO sessions behind. Assert on the
   session list after the sweep, not on the sweep's return value.

BLAST RADIUS: this gates everything. No trigger can run reliably while the cluster cannot
schedule an agent pod, so gonk-pev, the scaffold onboarding path, and any e2e proof are all
downstream of this.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 (session 7), TDD. All gates green: gofmt, go vet, go test ./...

THE TEST FIRST (cmd/gonk-gate/session_teardown_test.go). Six assertions, all on
gcapitest.Server.LiveSessions() -- what is left STANDING -- never on an exit code or a
recorded call. "runSweep returned 0" was true the entire time it was leaking.
  - round trip: dispatch -> work -> sweep -> judged -> applied leaves ZERO live sessions,
    AND the session is still live mid-turn (an early teardown destroys the unwritten batch)
  - every terminal ladder branch: done / escalate / retry (a re-sling opens a NEW
    attempt-suffixed session, so a leak there costs one pod PER RUNG -- which is why the
    live cluster held both i16.a1 and i16.a2, i17.a1 and i17.a2, and so on)
  - delivery failure closes the session dispatch could never talk to (the gonk-pev case)
  - a close FAILURE does not fail the sweep or strand the bead, but is logged loudly
All six failed red for the right reason before any production code changed.

THE FIX. pkg/gcapi.CloseSession -> POST /v0/city/{city}/session/{id}/close, signed.
Worth noting: unlike create and submit this route is SYNCHRONOUS upstream
(humaHandleSessionClose calls handle.CloseDetailed inline), so its 200 is a real receipt,
not a 202. This is the one session mutation this codebase may believe. 404 == success:
already gone is the desired state.

Three call sites, chosen by asking where a session can outlive the thing that would close it:
  - sweep.go closeSession(): after the outcome is reported, on done/escalate/retry. An
    unknown Next deliberately leaves the session ALIVE -- we did not understand the answer,
    so we have not established the work is over.
  - broker_inject.go abandonSession(): on delivery failure AND on the Store.Put failure.
    Both matter because the bead never reaches StateRunning on those paths, so gonk-sweep
    will NEVER see that alias. Those are invisible leaks, not merely long-lived pods.

A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PLAN. Item 2 (sleep_after_idle as the safety net) is WRONG
and was not shipped. IdleSince is populated from info.DetachedAt only
(cmd/gc/compute_awake_bridge.go:142), i.e. ATTACHMENT-based idleness. gonk's sessions are
headless and never attach, so DetachedAt is empty -- confirmed against the live beads, every
leaked session carried detached_at: "". The idle branch (compute_awake_set.go:467) requires
!IdleSince.IsZero(), so it can never fire for us. Adding the config line would have been a
safety net that does nothing and looks like safety: the same silent-success shape as the bug.
Item 3 (an orphan reaper) is therefore the ONLY net that works, and it is filed separately.

RESIDUAL LEAK, deliberately left: a dispatch process that DIES between create and any of the
three call sites (pod killed, order timeout) still strands its session. Much narrower than
before, and it is exactly what the reaper covers.
close_reason: Three teardown call sites implemented and tested (sweep terminal outcomes, dispatch delivery failure, dispatch store failure); six red-first tests asserting LiveSessions. Residual case (dispatch process dies mid-flight) split to gonk-4d7 along with the sleep_after_idle correction.

title: gonk images are amd64-only but the cluster is mixed-arch; any reschedule to an arm64 node breaks the deploy
description:
OUTAGE 2026-07-31 ~02:23 UTC. gonk-meter is in CrashLoopBackOff with 'exec /usr/local/bin/gonk-meter: exec format error'.

CAUSE: orac is a mixed-architecture cluster --
  johnny  amd64   (kaniko builds run here, so images are amd64)
  venus   amd64
  bailey  arm64
  orac01-04 arm64
5 of 7 nodes are arm64. The gonk images are built single-arch amd64 by the homelab kaniko template on johnny. The chart exposes intake/meter/controller nodeSelector, tolerations and affinity (chart/gonk/values.yaml:94,121,252) but ALL default to {} -- nothing constrains gonk workloads to amd64. The deployment has only ever worked because the scheduler happened to place pods on johnny/venus.

TRIGGER: the chart version embeds the git SHA (gonk-0.1.0+<sha>), so ANY commit to main causes Flux to cut a new chart release and recreate pods -- rolling the dice on architecture each time. Commit 5dcd286 (a beads/gitignore-only commit) was enough. gonk-meter landed on orac04 (arm64) and could not exec.

CASCADE: helm upgrade timed out waiting for gonk-meter + gonk-intake to become Ready; Flux's automatic rollback to gonk.v5 timed out for the same reason; the release is now stuck STATUS=pending-rollback at revision 8. gonk-intake is 0/1 Ready, controller has restarted 5x. dolt is unaffected because dolthub/dolt-sql-server is a multi-arch upstream image.

FIX, two options:
 (a) Constrain scheduling: set nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/arch: amd64} for intake/meter/controller. Cheapest, honest about what the images actually are. Correct home is arguably the Flux HelmRelease values in the gitops repo (deployment-specific), not the chart defaults -- pinning arch in the chart would become wrong the day images go multi-arch.
 (b) Build multi-arch images (kaniko --customPlatform / buildx equivalent, or a manifest list). Bigger job, owned by homelab/ci-templates (project 65), but it is the durable answer on a 5-of-7 arm64 cluster.

Recommend (a) now to restore service, (b) as the real fix.
design: Note the interaction with the chart's Recreate strategy and the etcd-write-sensitive upgrade caveat already recorded on gonk-dxo. Also note that a stuck pending-rollback release blocks further Flux reconciliation, so restoring service needs the release unwedged (helm rollback to a good revision, or a forced upgrade) IN ADDITION to the scheduling constraint -- a nodeSelector alone will not un-stick revision 8.
acceptance_criteria: gonk-intake, gonk-meter and gonk-controller are Running and Ready, the HelmRelease reports READY=True, and a pod-delete test confirms rescheduling cannot land a gonk workload on an arm64 node.
close_reason:
RESOLVED and verified live. The outage is over: ns gonk runs v0.1.0-d0443ac159e7 on multi-arch images, HelmRelease Ready=True UpgradeSucceeded, all four pods Running with 0 restarts, meter healthy. The wedged pending-rollback release cleared itself once working images existed -- no manual helm rollback was needed.

Durable fix was multi-arch images (gonk-owi.1) rather than pinning gonk to the 2 amd64 nodes, so a reschedule onto any of orac's 5 arm64 nodes is now survivable and no nodeSelector is required. Unblocked by homelab/ci-templates!1 and !2 (rootless native per-arch kaniko legs + crane manifest merge).

title: SPIKE S1: inject+return channel without pod bd
description: Plan Task 0.2. Pod has no working bd/gc (S0). EXIT: recorded inject mechanism (gc session new vs formula), return mechanism (gc session peek/logs reads agent's final JSON batch), correlation key (session id vs work-bead id), proven live round-trip: known prompt in -> known batch JSON out. Blocks C1/C2/C4/C5.
close_reason: Channel resolved: inject via gc session new --json (session-id correlation); return via gc session logs --json (structured transcript, sentinel-fenced batch); pod needs no bd/gc. Dead bd-return (S0) replaced. Live round-trip confirm folded into Phase 3 C2a.

title: [bug] gonk-gate envArg uppercased param names -> every dispatch arg empty, no formula ever poured
description: cmd/gonk-gate/main.go's envArg read GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<UPPERCASE(name)>, but Gas City sets GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<name> with the [order.params] key verbatim (internal/webhookmatch/extract.go ExecEnvVars is a plain map copy over declared param names). Every gonk param is lower_snake_case, so every arg read back empty and gonk-dispatch failed with 'unknown trigger; pouring nothing' trigger="" -- after meter had already been asked, so it burned a budget decision and poured nothing.
design: Read the verbatim name first; keep the uppercase spelling as a fallback so a future Gas City that normalizes keys still works.
close_reason: Fix already present in main.go (envArg reads verbatim name first, uppercase fallback); added regression tests TestEnvArg* this session (commit).

title: gonk-meter LiteLLM adapter broken against real v1.92.0: spend poller (v2 date format + response envelope + pagination) and admin update-by-alias (/key/info)
description:
Found by Plan 06 L2 (test/component: first contact between internal/meter/litellm and a REAL LiteLLM ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.92.0). Two independent, reproducible, FATAL defects. The adapters were written against docs + httptest mocks (which returned the WRONG shape), so both slipped through Plan 03.

=== BUG A (spend poller, FATAL) -- internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_http.go ===
Meter can NEVER ingest spend against real v1.92.0 => never synced => Ready() never true => every budgeted /decide defers forever.
1. fetchPage sends start_date/end_date as time.RFC3339 ("2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"). Real /spend/logs/v2 rejects it: HTTP 400 {"message":"Invalid date format: 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z. Expected: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'"}. FIX: format as "2006-01-02" (or "2006-01-02 15:04:05").
2. Since() does json.Unmarshal(body,&entries) with entries []logEntry, but v2 returns an OBJECT {"data":[...],"total","page","page_size","total_pages"}, NOT a bare array. Even with dates fixed, unmarshal fails. FIX: decode {"data":[]logEntry, total, page, total_pages}.
3. Pagination reads header.Get("X-Next-Page") (absent in v2). Real pagination is body fields page/total_pages. Only page 1 is ever read -> silent drop past page_size. FIX: loop while page < total_pages.
Root cause the tests missed it: internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_test.go mock returns a bare `[ {...} ]` array and ignores the query dates entirely.

=== BUG B (admin update-by-alias, breaks re-provisioning) -- internal/meter/litellm/admin_http.go ===
EnsureKey is idempotent-by-alias: /key/generate on an existing alias returns 400 "Key with alias 'X' already exists" (alreadyExists() matches), then updateByAlias() runs:
1. GET /key/info?key_alias=<alias> returns 404 {"message":"Key not found in database"}. v1.92.0 /key/info accepts ONLY ?key=<token>, NOT ?key_alias=. => EnsureKey errors on the SECOND ensure for any project (every budget change / ReconcileKeys tick / re-register).
2. /key/info shape is nested: {"key":..., "info":{"key_alias":...,"max_budget":...}} -- decodeKeyResponse reads TOP-LEVEL key_alias (would be empty). 
FIX: look the token up another way (LiteLLM has /key/list?key_alias=; or GET /key/info?key=<token> once the token is known; or store the token). Parse the nested .info shape.

=== VERIFIED GOOD (no change needed) ===
- HARD DOOR CLOSES: $1.00 key on glm ($2/1M), 100k tok/call = $0.20; call 6 refused HTTP 429 budget_exceeded "Current cost: 1.0, Max budget: 1.0". Zero overshoot.
- budget_duration "1mo" IS a UTC CALENDAR month: key created 2026-07-19, budget_reset_at 2026-08-01T00:00:00+00:00. (P3-2 OK, not rolling-30-days.)
- /model/info returns input_cost_per_token matching configured prices (qwen 2.5e-07, glm 2e-06, sonnet 6e-06) -> synthetic prices agree, catalog drift checkable (P3-4/P3-8).
- Dedicated proxy-admin key SUFFICES (P3-6): a plain generated key gets 401 on /key/generate & /spend/logs/v2, but a key issued to a /user/new user_role=proxy_admin does all admin calls -> master key NOT required.
- metadata NOT forwarded upstream (stub saw only [messages,model]) -> stub log is a VOLUME check only, attribution must come from v2 spend_logs_metadata.
- /key/delete {"key_aliases":[...]} works, returns {"deleted_keys":[...]}, token refused (401) IMMEDIATELY after.
- Also observed: detailed LiteLLM_SpendLogs table write lag is large/unreliable in single-node podman (rows often not visible within 100s even at proxy_batch_write_at:1; after a proxy restart, completions produced no rows in-window) while the key-level budget counter is immediate. P3-3 (spend-log lag vs max_spend_staleness) must be measured through the real code path AFTER Bug A is fixed.

Evidence + full reproduction in docs/spikes/litellm-verified.md. Blocks Plan 06 Task 5 (L2 suite cannot go green until the adapter speaks v2).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified against real LiteLLM v1.92.0 + adversarially reviewed (no credential blanking), merged to main (bef6684). Spend poller reads /spend/logs/v2 (YYYY-MM-DD dates, {data,...} envelope, page/total_pages); updateByAlias resolves via /key/list then /key/update; service.go preserves the stored KeyRef on empty token. Mocks rewritten to the real v2 contract. Follow-ups: gonk-4nk, gonk-0qi.

title: Every onboarded project bricks: ReserveIfFits applies cost gate to zero-cost local rungs
description: P0 money-path defect found by Plan 06 L1 (test/integration wiring real intake+meter). The onboarding default ships monthly_cost_usd:0 + ladder:[qwen-local] (local, zero-cost rung; spec 5.3). pkg/rung/decide.go:246 correctly SKIPS the cost gate for zero-cost rungs (if spec.EstCostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost). But internal/meter/store/memory.go:146 AND postgres.go:428 apply the cost check UNCONDITIONALLY (if !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)||...), and pkg/budget/remaining.go:119 FitsCost returns false whenever MonthlyCostUSD<=0 regardless of est. So ReserveIfFits asks FitsCost(0) against a $0 ceiling -> false -> rejects a reservation that holds ZERO real dollars, even though Decide just said 'run'. Result: POST /v1/policy/decide returns defer/monthly-cost-exhausted for every freshly-onboarded project -- dead on arrival. Affects BOTH store backends (postgres is the real ledger). Latent because no meter test registered a $0-cost budget with a local ladder. FIX: mirror Decide's gate in both ReserveIfFits impls -> if (r.CostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)) || !rem.FitsMonthTokens(r.Tokens) || !rem.FitsTaskTokens(r.Tokens). A zero-cost reservation holds no real dollars so it must always clear the cost leg (token gates still enforce the token budget via synthetic pricing). Add a storetest guard: 'zero-cost local rung reserves under a $0 cost budget'. Money-path -> adversarial review before merge.
close_reason: Fixed + adversarially reviewed + merged to main (8bf5381). Both stores skip the cost leg for zero-cost rungs; verified on real Postgres (fail-before/pass-after, priced rungs still rejected, overspend race 0/10, idempotency intact). Optional future hardening: validateFiniteMoney could also reject CostUSD<0 (unreachable in prod).

title: e2e: assert LiteLLM pricing agrees with the rung catalog, and that the budget door actually closes
description:
opercfg.go states the requirement and admits nothing checks it: "The operator MUST configure the same number in LiteLLM's model list. That agreement is unverifiable from here; Plan 06 checks it." Plan 06 has not written it, and gonk-1zm showed why it matters -- the pricing was simply ABSENT from LiteLLM for months and nothing noticed, so the USD door never closed on any local rung while every manifest read as though it did.

Nothing in the gonk repo can see the gitops values, so this belongs in the e2e harness, which can reach both.

WHAT IT SHOULD ASSERT, in rough order of value:

1. PRICE AGREEMENT. For every rung with kind=local in the operator config,
   LiteLLM's model_list entry for that rung's `model` carries
   input_cost_per_token == output_cost_per_token == synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens / 1e6.
   Catch three distinct failures: missing entirely (the gonk-1zm case), wrong
   value (drift after someone edits one side), and split input/output rates
   (which silently desynchronise LiteLLM's spend from opercfg.PricePerToken(),
   since gonk models ONE price per token).

2. CLOUD RUNGS MUST NOT CARRY A SYNTHETIC PRICE. opercfg forbids it -- a cloud
   rung's price is real and lives in LiteLLM's own config, and declaring a
   synthetic one would be a lie. Assert the config-side rule too, not just the
   proxy side.

3. THE DOOR ACTUALLY CLOSES. The strongest form, and the one that would have
   caught gonk-8gb as well: make a metered call ON THE PROJECT'S VIRTUAL KEY and
   assert spend moves by tokens * pricePerToken. Verified by hand on 2026-09-06:
   25 tokens at 2.5e-07 produced exactly 0.0000062500. A test that asserts the
   ARITHMETIC rather than "spend > 0" catches a wrong rate, not just a missing one.

4. THE AGENT USES THE METERED KEY. gonk-8gb: agents currently authenticate with
   the MASTER ADMIN key, so the virtual key's max_budget is never consulted. The
   check is that the key an agent session presents has a key_alias matching
   gonk-<project> and a non-zero max_budget -- i.e. that it is a scoped key at
   all. This is the assertion that would have caught the budget door being
   nominal.

A TRAP TO ENCODE IN THE TEST rather than rediscover: the gonk-litellm secret is
the MASTER key the meter uses to PROVISION keys, not a project key. A call made
with it bills a key with no alias and no budget, and the project's spend stays 0
while everything looks configured. The project key lives in the keysink secret,
gonk-key-<project>-<hash>, per GONK_KEYSINK_PREFIX. I lost time to exactly this.
notes:
DONE, 2026-09-06, as test/live (build tag: live). Three checks, all passing against the real deployment, and each proved to FIRE on the state it exists to catch.

WHY A NEW PACKAGE RATHER THAN EXTENDING test/component. There was ALREADY a TestSyntheticPricesAgreeBetweenTheRungCatalogAndLiteLLM, and it is a good test -- it proves the agreement rule is enforceable and that the code reads both sides correctly. It could not have caught gonk-1zm because BOTH SIDES ARE FIXTURES: newWorld boots its own LiteLLM and its own catalog. The real proxy carried no prices at all for months while the real operator config declared them, and every hermetic test stayed green. A drift check has to read what is DEPLOYED.

SOURCE OF TRUTH IS THE CLUSTER, NOT THE REPO. The operator config comes from the deployed ConfigMap and the prices from the running proxy's /model/info. What a file in git says is not evidence about what is serving traffic, and the gap between those two is the entire subject.

THE CHECKS:
  1. TestDeployedPricesMatchTheDeployedRungCatalog -- for every local rung, the
     running proxy's price equals synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens / 1e6. Catches all
     three failures separately: PRICED AT ZERO (the gonk-1zm state), a DIFFERENT
     rate (drift after one side is edited), and a SPLIT input/output rate, which
     is the subtle one -- opercfg models ONE price per token and the meter
     reconciles against LiteLLM's spend, so a split leaves both numbers plausible
     and stops them agreeing.
  2. TestDeployedCloudRungsDeclareNoSyntheticPrice -- opercfg forbids it; a cloud
     rung's price is real, and a synthetic one is a fiction the budget math would
     believe.
  3. TestEveryProjectKeyIsScopedAndBudgeted -- every gonk- aliased virtual key
     carries a positive max_budget. A key with no ceiling cannot refuse anything.

TWO BUGS IN MY OWN TEST, both of the same shape and worth recording because they are the failure mode this file exists to prevent -- a check that runs and asserts nothing:
  - The secret-name prefix compared name[:10] against the 9-character "gonk-key-",
    which can never match, so the key check always SKIPPED.
  - /key/list was requested with size=200. LiteLLM's maximum is 100, so it
    answered 422; the error body has no "keys" field, decoded to an empty list,
    and read as "no keys exist" -- a silent pass. A non-200 is now a FATAL, not
    something to decode.
Both were found only by noticing the test SKIPPED rather than checking 2 keys.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, not assumed: the comparison logic was exercised against a
priced-at-zero rung, a wrong rate and a split rate, and fires on all three while
passing the correct case.

STILL NOT ASSERTED, and it is the one that would catch gonk-8gb directly: that
the key an AGENT PRESENTS is the project's key rather than the proxy admin key.
Checkable indirectly once the gonk-8gb fix deploys -- a project key that has
served sessions should show non-zero spend, and today every one of them is at
zero despite many runs, which is the signature. Left out deliberately rather than
written flaky: on a fresh install with no sessions, zero spend is correct.
close_reason: Closed

title: NetworkPolicies are not enforced: the cluster runs flannel with no policy controller
description:
MEASURED, 2026-09-06. The cluster CNI is kube-flannel and there is NO NetworkPolicy controller anywhere -- no Calico, Cilium, kube-router, Antrea or OVN in any namespace. Flannel provides networking only; it does not implement NetworkPolicy. The API server accepts the objects and NOTHING ENFORCES THEM.

PROVED EMPIRICALLY rather than inferred. A throwaway pod in the gonk namespace carrying the agent's own label (app=gc-agent), which the gonk-agent policy restricts to DNS, litellm:4000, intake:9090 and meter:8080:
    nc ollama.bailey-gpu.svc.cluster.local 11434  -> OLLAMA REACHABLE
    nc litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local 4000     -> reachable (expected)
The first of those is denied by the policy and happened anyway.

WHAT IT INVALIDATES. Several controls that read as enforced are decorative:
  - gonk-agent egress: an agent CAN reach Ollama directly, and Ollama needs no
    credential (gonk-8g9), so a model that decides to call it bypasses LiteLLM,
    its metadata attribution and its budget ceiling entirely.
  - gonk-7oz is worse than its title says. It reports that the agent policy
    allows any port to the whole gitlab namespace so "no forge access" rests on
    credentials alone. In fact NO policy restricts the agent at all, so that is
    true of every destination, not just gitlab.
  - The gonk-meter ingress rule I added for the LiteLLM proxy (gonk-p8j) is
    likewise unenforced. It was written as a deliberate narrow widening; it is
    currently neither narrow nor a widening, because the door was open.

WHAT IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE. Credentials still work. The agent holds no forge
PAT, so it cannot write to GitLab regardless of reachability, and the broker
model does not depend on the network policy for that property. This finding is
about the LAYER THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE DEFENCE IN DEPTH, and there is one fewer
layer than the manifests imply.

WHAT TO DO, and the honest options differ a lot in cost:
  1. Install a policy controller. Calico or Cilium can run alongside flannel
     (canal is exactly this pairing) and would make every existing policy real
     with no manifest changes. Cluster-wide change, affects every workload, and
     policies that have never been enforced may well be wrong -- expect breakage
     the first time they bite.
  2. Rely on credentials and make each one narrow. Credential Ollama (gonk-8g9),
     give the agent a scoped LiteLLM key rather than the admin key (gonk-8gb),
     and keep the agent free of forge creds. This is where the real controls
     already are.
  3. Delete the policies that cannot be enforced, so the manifests stop asserting
     a property the cluster does not provide. Cheapest and the most honest, and
     the worst if a controller is ever installed later and nobody notices the
     policies are gone.
Recommend 2 now and 1 deliberately, and NOT 3 -- the manifests are the design
record even where the cluster does not honour them yet, but they should carry a
comment saying so.
notes: DEFERRED by the owner, 2026-09-06: 'the network controller stuff is a whole other kettle of fish, just assume that that works.' Installing a policy controller is a cluster-wide change affecting every workload, and policies that have never been enforced are likely wrong in ways that would only surface when they first bite. Kept OPEN as the design record, and the practical consequence is recorded on the beads that depend on it: the real controls are credential-shaped (gonk-8gb scoped key, gonk-8g9 credential Ollama), not network-shaped.

title: Triage has no verdict, so every outcome is the same comment
description:
Triage currently has exactly one outcome: post a comment and some labels. It cannot say WHAT KIND of answer it reached, so the broker cannot act differentially and every issue ends the same way regardless of what the agent concluded.

Add a VERDICT to the batch -- a single field on Batch, not a new effect kind, because it describes the batch as a whole rather than one change to make:

  {"verdict":"reply-only","effects":[...]}

THE THREE VERDICTS, and each must have a real action behind it:
  reply-only    No code change is needed, but the reporter needs an answer -- a
                question, a clarification, a "works as designed and here is why".
                Action: what happens today (comment + labels).
  code-change   A genuine defect with an identifiable fix. Action depends on
                policy, see below.
  close         Terminal. No further dialogue is useful -- duplicate, obsolete,
                already fixed, not reproducible. Action: comment + labels AND
                actually close the issue, with the reason in the comment.

code-change BRANCHES ON EXISTING POLICY, actions.features, which is already
resolved and plumbed through gonkcfg.Effective:
  features=false  gonk must NOT propose code on this project. Notify a
                  maintainer instead: the comment stands, plus a label that
                  makes the queue findable. Do not silently drop it -- an
                  identified fix that nobody is told about is worse than no
                  triage.
  features=true   Hand off to the fix flow: render a fix prompt, work in a
                  checkout, return file effects, and open an MR through the
                  same machinery applyScaffoldFiles already uses for the
                  scaffold MR (branch, commit, one MR carrying the bead
                  marker). Never auto-merge.

INVARIANTS THIS MUST NOT BREAK:
- The verdict is MODEL-AUTHORED, so it is a proposal, not ground truth
  (ADR-007). It is validated against a closed set before anything acts on it;
  an unknown verdict is a gate failure, exactly like an unknown effect kind.
- The ACTIONS are deterministic. No model decides whether to close an issue or
  open an MR; the model states a verdict and the broker decides what that
  means. pkg/gate.Classify stays pure and free of LLM judges.
- A batch with no verdict must still parse, so existing behaviour is the
  default and this is additive.
- close is the only verdict that ends a conversation, and it is the one most
  worth being conservative about: prefer reply-only when unsure, and say so in
  the prompt.
close_reason: Closed

title: A cold controller accepts a session and silently never creates the pod
description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-02 on issue !44. The controller pod had been running for 42 SECONDS when dispatch ran. Sequence:

  07:29:12  controller starts (caching-store priming, beads cache stagger=16261ms)
  07:29:53  POST /v0/city/gonk/order/gonk-dispatch/run 202
  07:29:54  'checkout granted for this session'
  07:29:54  POST /v0/city/gonk/sessions 202        <- ACCEPTED
            ... no pod is ever created, and gc logs NOTHING
  07:31:54  'prompt was never fetched by the agent after 40 checks'
  07:31:54  'abandoned session closed'

The identical dispatch succeeded eight minutes later on issue !45 with the same image, same config and a warm controller -- an agent pod appeared within seconds and the triage completed. So this is a startup race, not a broken deployment.

WHAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS is not the race but the SILENCE: /sessions returns 202 Accepted, so the caller believes the session was created, and the k8s provider then does nothing and reports nothing. The only symptom is a two-minute wait followed by 'prompt was never fetched', which reads like an AGENT fault and costs an attempt on the ladder. [session] provider = 'k8s' was present and correct in city.toml, and GC_K8S_IMAGE pointed at an image that exists, so every piece of config a human would check looks right.

Related to but distinct from gonk-fsl (9443 does not bind until init finishes): here the API was already answering, which is precisely why the request was accepted.

WHAT TO DO: (1) find out whether gc's k8s provider is genuinely not ready at that point or whether it failed and swallowed the error -- if it can fail silently, that is the real bug; (2) make dispatch refuse to sling until the session provider can actually create pods, so an unready controller parks the bead as UNKNOWN rather than burning an attempt; (3) at minimum, make 'prompt was never fetched' distinguish 'no pod was ever created' from 'a pod ran and did not fetch', because those have completely different causes and only one of them is the agent's fault.

title: The comment body is mangled by 80-column tmux pane wrapping
description:
FOUND on the FIRST SUCCESSFUL END-TO-END TRIAGE, issue !45, 2026-09-02. The comment posted, the labels applied, and the text arrived broken MID-WORD:

  'The issue describes a problem where the so' / 'rt order resets when paging'
  'the paging mechan' / 'ism does not retain'

CAUSE, and the arithmetic is exact: the fenced payload opens with
{"effects":[{"kind":"comment","body":" -- 38 characters -- followed by 'The issue describes a problem where the so', 42 characters. 38 + 42 = 80. Every break lands on an 80-column boundary. Gas City serves the transcript by capturing the tmux pane, the pane is the default 80x24, and the capture does not JOIN wrapped lines, so a single-line JSON payload comes back with real newlines inserted mid-word.

Note the interaction with gonk-jj8: before that fix these wrap-newlines made the batch unparseable, so this was invisible. Normalising them to \n made the batch parse -- and faithfully preserved the wrap artefacts in the body. The fix was right; it just revealed the layer underneath.

DO NOT 'fix' this by joining newlines in the broker. We cannot distinguish a wrap from a newline the model actually meant, and guessing would silently corrupt any legitimately multi-line body. Fix the CAUSE: make the pane wide enough that the payload does not wrap.

PREFERRED FIX, and it is in our control: the entrypoint runs INSIDE the tmux session, so before starting opencode it can widen the window --
  tmux set-option -g window-size manual
  tmux resize-window -t main -x 4000 -y 200
A detached session with no client sits at default-size 80x24, which is why this bites. Verify by checking that the fenced line in /tmp/agent-output.log exceeds 80 characters unbroken.

ALTERNATIVE, upstream: have Gas City capture with 'tmux capture-pane -J', which joins wrapped lines. Better in principle -- it fixes this for every consumer, not just gonk -- but it is a change we do not own.

This is cosmetic in the sense that triage now works end to end, and NOT cosmetic in the sense that every comment gonk posts is visibly broken.
notes: FIXED and verified 2026-09-06. The entrypoint widens the tmux window before producing output, so the transcript is no longer captured at 80 columns. Issue !58's comment reads cleanly with no mid-word breaks: 'internal/paging/sort.go:29-31 -- the SortByDate case in Sort() hardcodes ascending comparison'. Compare !45, which broke as 'the so/rt order'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two meters racing create duplicate LiteLLM keys, and the project then wedges permanently
description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-02. Issue !43 parked repeatedly with 'virtual-key-missing: LiteLLM virtual key not provisioned yet', retrying every 5 minutes and never recovering. The meter's own log gives the real reason:

  litellm: could not ensure the project's virtual key; recording key-missing
  err: litellm: /key/list: 2 keys share alias, refusing to guess which to update

/key/list confirms exactly two keys with alias gonk-agentic-gonk-e2e-1784441480, BOTH created at 06:11:59 and both with spend 0.0 -- the same second, so this is a race, not drift.

HOW THE RACE AROSE: node orac04 went NotReady (kubelet stopped posting status) and the controller and meter pods stranded on it were force-deleted onto healthy nodes. For a window there were two meters, and 'ensure the project's virtual key' is a check-then-create with no atomicity, so both checked, both found nothing, and both created.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A DUPLICATE: refusing to guess is CORRECT -- picking arbitrarily could silently point a project at a key with different budget or model access. But the refusal is TERMINAL. Nothing reconciles the duplicate away, so the project stays wedged forever and the only exit is a human deleting a key by hand. A fail-closed state with no recovery path is an outage with extra steps, and it is reachable from an ordinary node failure.

TWO THINGS TO FIX, and they are separate:
1. PREVENTION -- make ensure-key idempotent so concurrent meters cannot both create. Either create-if-absent atomically, or make the key name deterministic and treat an already-exists response as success rather than as an error to retry.
2. RECOVERY -- give the duplicate case a deterministic, auditable resolution rather than a permanent park. Candidates: adopt the OLDEST key and log loudly that a duplicate was found; or keep refusing but surface it as a distinct operator-visible condition rather than an indefinite park that reads like a slow provision. Whichever is chosen, the refusal to GUESS should stay; what must go is the absence of any way out.

Note that both duplicates had zero spend, so nothing was double-billed and no history was at stake here -- but that is luck, not design: if the losing key had spend, deleting it would lose that record.
notes: The talos-toolkit instance has since self-healed to a single key, so no project is currently wedged. The RACE IS UNFIXED though, and it recurred tonight in a new way worth recording: it is not only two meters racing. Any event that rolls the meter while intake is registering can leave duplicates, and the failure is SILENT -- intake answers the webhook 200 and dispatches nothing, logging nothing, so the only symptom is that triage stops. Prevention (idempotent ensure) still matters more than recovery.

title: A raw newline in a comment body cost the whole batch; ParseBatch now normalises control bytes inside strings
description:
OBSERVED on issue !43 once the transcript became readable: 'unparseable batch: effects: parse batch: invalid character \n in string literal'. Asked for a multi-line comment body, the model wrote the newline LITERALLY instead of as \n. JSON forbids raw control characters inside string literals, so an otherwise correct triage batch -- good analysis, sensible labels -- was thrown away over a single byte.

FIX, two sides:
1. pkg/effects ParseBatch now normalises raw newline, carriage-return and tab bytes that appear INSIDE a string literal into their escaped forms, before decoding. This is deliberately the narrowest thing that helps and is NOT a JSON repair: it cannot change the meaning of any valid batch, because valid JSON cannot contain those bytes inside a string, so for well-formed input it is a byte-for-byte identity. It does not balance braces, close quotes, strip prose or guess intent -- anything still malformed stays rejected, which rawcontrol_test.go asserts directly. The shape gate remains the sole authority on what a batch may DO; this only decides whether we can read it.
2. The triage prompt now states that the batch must be valid JSON on a SINGLE line and that a line break must be written as \n.

Tests cover both directions: raw newlines and tabs parse and the text survives INTACT rather than being flattened; already-escaped \n is not double-escaped; an escaped quote does not end the string (or every control byte after it would be misread as structural); a pretty-printed batch still parses; and unterminated strings, trailing commas and non-JSON are still rejected.
close_reason: Closed

title: vLLM streaming tool-call deltas repeat id/type without name, which aborts opencode
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 against LiteLLM from inside an agent pod, so this is the exact path opencode uses.

NON-STREAMING IS FINE. A tool-call request to qwen3.6-35b-vllm returns a well-formed call:
  "tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"{\"path\": \".\"}","name":"list_files"},"id":"chatcmpl-tool-...","type":"function"}]

STREAMING IS NOT. With stream:true the same request yields:
  chunk 1: "function":{"arguments":"","name":"list_files"}   <- has name
  chunk 2: "function":{"arguments":"{\"path\": "}            <- NO name, but still "id" and "type":"function"
  chunk 3+: more argument fragments, same shape

OpenAI omits 'id' and 'type' on continuation deltas; vLLM repeats them. opencode's @ai-sdk/openai-compatible adapter treats a delta carrying type:'function' as the START of a tool call and requires function.name to be a string, so chunk 2 throws "Expected 'function.name' to be a string" and the turn aborts after a few file reads. That is the exact error seen in agent pods on both qwen3.6-35b-vllm and qwen3.6-35b-vllm-nothink.

CONTRAST THAT CONFIRMS IT: Ollama-served qwen3-14b emits the ENTIRE tool call in a single delta (complete arguments plus name, then finish_reason) and never produces a continuation chunk -- which is precisely why the 14b rung works and both vLLM rungs do not.

NOT a thinking problem: -nothink behaves identically. Do not chase chat_template_kwargs again.

OPTIONS: check whether a newer vLLM fixes the qwen3_xml parser's streaming emit; try a different --tool-call-parser and re-run the streaming probe above; or normalise in LiteLLM by stripping id/type from continuation deltas. The probe is two curl calls from an agent pod and takes seconds, so verify any change against it directly rather than through a full triage run.

BLOCKS using any vLLM-served rung for agent work, which currently means the 35B is unusable despite being ~70s/turn versus ~16min on Ollama.
notes:
FIXED AND PROVEN END TO END, 2026-09-06, issue !58 on rung qwen3-6-35b:
  trajectory: satisfied, completeness=complete, 10 calls, 8 turns
  verdict code-change -> routed to a maintainer, batch applied, outcome=success
That is the FIRST successful agent turn on a vLLM rung. The comment it produced
is the best gonk has written: "BUG CONFIRMED: internal/paging/sort.go:29-31 --
the SortByDate case in Sort() hardcodes ascending comparison and never checks
the desc flag. The SortByName case correctly branches on desc at line 24." Exact
lines, the defect, a contrast with the working case, and a fix -- and the trace
independently confirms it read sort.go.

IT TOOK TWO REPAIRS, NOT ONE, AND MY FIRST PROBE WAS TOO SIMPLE TO FIND THE SECOND.

  Shape 1: LiteLLM strips function.name from CONTINUATION deltas. vLLM emits it
  on every chunk; the proxy delivered 1 of 5. Repaired by remembering the name
  per (choice index, tool index) and filling it in.

  Shape 2, which only appears with SEVERAL TOOLS in the request -- that is,
  realistic agent traffic, which my single-tool probe was not: the stream
  carries a delta for a tool index whose OPENING WAS NEVER EMITTED. Measured
  with five tools: indices 0 and 2 arrived named, index 1 arrived with NEITHER a
  name NOR arguments. Remembering cannot repair it because there is no name to
  remember. Such an entry cannot be executed, accumulated or identified; its
  only effect is to fail a client that validates each delta, which is exactly
  what kept aborting the turn after shape 1 was fixed. It is now DROPPED --
  which invents nothing, the line this repair must not cross -- and an emptied
  tool_calls list becomes None rather than [], because some clients read a
  present list as "a tool call starts here".

Both live in the hook that already existed for the finish_reason defect
(openclaw-e3mb), and both are SELF-DEACTIVATING: shape 1 only fills a MISSING
name, shape 2 only drops an entry with nothing in it, so when the upstream
release lands they become no-ops.

VERIFIED IN THE REAL IMAGE (ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.99.1), 11 checks,
including that a nameless delta WITH arguments is still kept and named, that
named calls either side survive, and that a droppable entry does not take a real
one with it. contrib/litellm/verify_in_container.py makes it repeatable.

A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME RUN, worth its own bead: the labels the agent
proposed were gonk/backend, gonk/bug, gonk/paging -- with a SLASH, while the
project's configured label_prefix is "gonk::". The broker applied them verbatim,
so a project's label namespace is whatever the model happens to type. Only the
broker's own labels (gonk::needs-maintainer, gonk::verdict-code-change) used the
configured prefix.
close_reason: Closed

title: The agent's batch was valid but unreadable: tmux dies with the entrypoint, so the transcript came back empty
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 on project 75 issues !37 and !38, immediately after prompt-by-reference and non-interactive mode landed. THIS IS THE LAST MILE and it is probably a defect I introduced in gonk-5k5 part A.

WHAT IS PROVEN WORKING: prompt delivery (the pod pulls, 'prompt fetched by the agent pod'), the per-session overlay from the fetched row, the ob5 provider allowlist, non-interactive execution, and the vLLM backend. vLLM logs show the model being CALLED AND GENERATING: 'POST /v1/chat/completions 200 OK', 808 tok/s prompt throughput, 25.7 tok/s generation, request count going 1 -> 0 as it completes, ~70s per turn (versus ~16 minutes on Ollama -- gonk-w41's repoint worked).

WHAT FAILS: the sweep classifies the session gate-failed, not infra-failed, so it DID read and judge the session -- it simply found no valid artifact. 'bead denied reason=ladder-exhausted detail=2 rungs, 2 gate failures'. No comment, no labels.

THE HYPOTHESIS, and why it points at my change: before part A, the prompt was typed into opencode's TUI and the agent's output was RENDERED INTO THE TMUX PANE, which is what Gas City captures and what sweep reads via GetSessionOutput. On issue !30 that pane visibly contained a complete GONK_BATCH_START/END fence. Now the entrypoint execs 'opencode run', which writes to STDOUT. The entrypoint runs under 'tmux new-session -d', and gonk-j9z already established that a process's stdout there does NOT reach the container log -- so it is entirely plausible it does not reach the captured pane in the same form either, or that the session ends and the pane is torn down before capture. Either way the broker would see an empty transcript and correctly report no fence.

I CHANGED THE OUTPUT PATH WITHOUT VERIFYING THE READER. That is the mistake, and it is the same class as the bugs this codebase keeps finding: a step that looks like success while the value it was carrying is silently dropped.

HOW TO CONFIRM CHEAPLY: run one triage and capture the pane WHILE the model is generating (the vLLM turn is ~70s, so it is observable), or tee opencode's stdout to the pane explicitly. If the pane is empty while vLLM is generating, the hypothesis is confirmed.

FIXES, in preference order: (1) have the entrypoint tee 'opencode run' output into the pane (or write it where Gas City captures) so the existing reader keeps working; (2) capture opencode's stdout to a file and have the broker read THAT by reference, the same shape as the prompt fetch -- arguably the better design, since it stops depending on a terminal-rendering side effect for correctness; (3) use 'opencode run --format json' and parse events, which is the most structured but changes what the fence looks like. Note (2) composes with the closed-fence backstop already in the sweep.
notes: RESOLVED AND PROVEN END TO END, 2026-09-02 07:40, issue !45. gonk posted its first real triage comment: correct analysis of the reported bug, a clarifying question to the reporter as instructed, the bead anchor comment, and labels gonk::bug and gonk::needs-investigation applied. The full path works -- webhook, dispatch, prompt-by-reference, non-interactive opencode, fenced batch, transcript read, shape gate, broker apply.

title: Delivery is fixed, but a 35B-on-Ollama turn produces no fenced batch in ~16 minutes
description:
FOUND 2026-09-01 immediately after prompt-by-reference landed (gonk-mzd), on project 75 issue !36.

The blocker has CHANGED CHARACTER. Prompt delivery now works -- the pod pulls its prompt, renders its overlay from the fetched row, confirms the provider allowlist, and runs opencode NON-INTERACTIVELY. All of that is visible in the pane and in 'prompt fetched by the agent pod'. What does not happen is a fenced batch.

WHAT RAN: attempt 2, rung qwen3-6-35b -> model qwen3.6:35b, which is the OLLAMA-backed 35B, not the vLLM one. The pane showed 'build - qwen3.6:35b' and nothing else for ~16 minutes; the session then ended on its own (correct -- run mode exits) with no GONK_BATCH fence, so no artifact reached the ladder and the bead escalated to gonk::needs-human. Every layer behaved correctly; the model simply did not finish useful work.

CONTRAST WORTH KEEPING: the SAME prompt shape on qwen3-14b took 32.6 SECONDS and produced a complete, well-formed fence (recorded on gonk-5k5). So this is a ~30x regression in turn time from moving up a rung, on a backend that loads the model per request.

LIKELY CAUSES, in the order worth checking:
1. WRONG BACKEND FOR THE RUNG. The catalog's qwen3-6-35b points at ollama_chat/qwen3.6:35b. The vLLM entry (qwen3.6-35b-vllm) serves the SAME weights with continuous batching, paged KV, prefix caching and speculative decoding, and is the one built for sustained agent load -- Ollama's load/unload shape is not. This is exactly what gonk-gyj is about, and it is now blocking a milestone rather than being an optimisation.
2. Cold model load on every request, and bailey hosting both Ollama and vLLM resident at once (gonk-38o memory pressure).
3. The prompt is larger than the 14B run's -- it now carries repo context via the rig -- so a slower backend compounds.

WHAT TO DO: point the rung at qwen3.6-35b-vllm and re-run !36 unchanged. That is a one-line operator-values change and it isolates the backend as the variable. If the turn completes, gonk-gyj stops being deferred work and becomes the fix. NOTE gonk-1zm still applies either way: no local model is priced in LiteLLM, so neither backend's spend closes the USD door.
notes: BACKEND REPOINT WORKS, 2026-09-02. The rung now names qwen3.6-35b-vllm and vLLM logs confirm it is being used: 'POST /v1/chat/completions 200 OK', 808 tok/s prompt throughput, 25.7 tok/s generation, ~70 SECONDS per turn against ~16 minutes on ollama_chat/qwen3.6:35b. Prefix cache hit rate 78%. So the backend was the variable, exactly as predicted, and Ollama's load/unload shape is confirmed wrong for sustained agent work. Deployed via gitops f9cbe9b. What remains is NOT this bead: the model now generates fine but the sweep still reports gate-failed, which points at the output PATH rather than the model -- see gonk-2tb.

title: Implement prompt-by-reference so the entrypoint PULLS its prompt (unblocks the triage milestone)
description:
THE REMAINING BLOCKER for gonk-712, established live 2026-09-01.

Today the agent pod is started as:
  /bin/sh -c "... tmux new-session -d -s main 'gonk-agent-entrypoint' && sleep infinity"
with NO arguments, so the entrypoint never sees a prompt. Gas City then PUSHES the prompt out of band by typing it into the opencode TUI after startup. That push is unreliable: across five live runs only one composer ever received text, and the pod carries GC_STARTUP_PROMPT_DELIVERED=1 even when the composer is empty -- a success flag for work that did not happen.

Because the entrypoint gets no argv, gonk-5k5 part A (exec 'opencode run -- <prompt>') is correct but DEAD CODE as deployed. It has no prompt to run with.

THE FIX, already designed: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-implementation.md (T0 passed, T1-T6 unstarted). Store the prompt keyed by session alias and have the entrypoint FETCH it, rather than being typed at. Everything needed is already in the pod's environment -- GC_ALIAS=gonk.triage.p75.i35.a1 was present on the live pod -- so the entrypoint can ask for its own prompt by name.

WHY PULL BEATS PUSH HERE, beyond the observed flakiness: a pull either returns the prompt or fails loudly, whereas the current push cannot distinguish 'typed into a ready composer' from 'typed into a splash screen'. It also removes a keystroke path that a bang in issue text can exploit (the original gonk-e9m injection concern), and it composes with part A to give a session that receives its work as an argument and exits when done.

SEQUENCING: this bead, then part A becomes live automatically, then the sweep's closed-fence backstop (already deployed, f4958b0) judges the result. Those three together are the whole remaining distance to a real triage comment.
notes:
DEPLOYED AND PROVEN WORKING 2026-09-01, v0.1.0-2e536c9c1fac. The delivery problem is SOLVED. Evidence from the live run on project 75 issue !36, all four pieces visible in one agent pane:

  gonk-agent-entrypoint: rendered /etc/gonk/overlay/opencode.json (model=qwen3.6:35b)
  gonk-agent-entrypoint: provider check ok: opencode resolved only gonk/ models
  gonk-agent-entrypoint: starting opencode run (non-interactive)
  controller: prompt fetched by the agent pod  alias=gonk.triage.p75.i36.a2.PESQZGE2FTJ5ZBYPOAIA6M2BXM

That is: the pod PULLED its prompt (never once achieved by the old push in five prior runs); the MODEL came from the fetched row rather than static env, which is the gonk-m6t attribution seam working; the ob5 provider allowlist held; and opencode ran NON-INTERACTIVELY, so the session reached a terminal state on its own.

T6 ACCEPTANCE, half met. The one-shot check passed by hand exactly as the plan asks: a second GET of the consumed alias returns 410. The authenticated routes still demand a bearer (the cost route answered 'unauthorized' to an unauthenticated probe), so the exemption really is confined to the one GET.

WHAT DID NOT HAPPEN: no triage comment. The bead (go-id06) ended gonk::needs-human. Attempt 2 ran ~16 minutes on qwen3.6:35b via OLLAMA and the session ended without a fenced batch, so no artifact reached the ladder and it escalated correctly. That is no longer a DELIVERY failure -- it is a model/harness one, and it is a different bead. See the follow-up.

title: Prompt delivery into the opencode TUI is intermittent: 1 of 4 runs received its prompt
description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-01 across four consecutive live triage runs on project 75.

  !30  prompt ARRIVED -- composer rendered the full triage prompt, agent read the repo, closed a fence in a 32.6s turn
  !31  prompt NEVER ARRIVED -- pane sat at the opencode splash screen, empty composer, for the session's life
  !33  prompt NEVER ARRIVED -- same, pod s-go-bv59 still idle at the splash 10+ minutes in
  !32  never dispatched at all (webhook lost during a restart window -- separate, gonk-icj)

So delivery succeeded once in four. This is the old gonk-e9m symptom recurring after that bead was recorded as functionally resolved, and it is a RACE, not a hard failure: the prompt is typed as keystrokes into a TUI, so it depends on opencode's composer being ready to receive them when the broker sends. Nothing reports an error -- the submit succeeds, the session is created, and the pane is simply empty, which is why it reads as 'the agent did nothing' rather than 'the prompt was lost'.

CONFOUND, stated honestly: runs !31 and !33 happened while the stack was churning from my deploy/rollback/redeploy cycle, with Dolt cold and the controller logging MySQL i/o timeouts and a flapping circuit breaker. So contention may be what widens the race rather than it being uniformly 1-in-4. That does not change the conclusion -- a delivery mechanism that a slow moment can silently defeat is the wrong mechanism -- but it does mean the ratio should not be quoted as a measured rate.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN: gonk-5k5 part A (commit 8e85df6, pipeline 2283) replaces 'opencode <flags>' with 'opencode run -- <prompt>', passing the prompt as an ARGUMENT rather than typing it into a TUI. That removes this race by construction -- there is no composer to be unready. It was originally justified as making sessions exit; it turns out to be the fix for delivery too, which raises its priority from hygiene to blocker.

COMPOUNDING EFFECT worth its own attention: a session that never receives its prompt still occupies the agent pool, so subsequent issues do not dispatch at all (!34 never got a pod while s-go-bv59 sat idle). One lost prompt therefore blocks the queue behind it until the reservation expires.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-01, and it changes what the fix has to be.

The agent pod's container command is:
  /bin/sh -c "... tmux new-session -d -s main \"gonk-agent-entrypoint\" && sleep infinity"

THE ENTRYPOINT RECEIVES NO ARGUMENTS AT ALL. There is no --prompt on argv, so GONK_PROMPT is always empty and the entrypoint's whole prompt branch -- including the new 'opencode run' path from gonk-5k5 part A -- is DEAD CODE in this dispatch flow. It falls through to 'exec opencode "$@"' with empty argv, which is precisely the TUI we are trying to stop starting. Part A is correct but UNREACHABLE as deployed; confirmed on the live pod running the new image v0.1.0-4594e43cc0de.

The prompt is instead delivered OUT OF BAND by Gas City's startup-prompt mechanism, typed into the TUI after the session starts. The pod carries GC_STARTUP_PROMPT_DELIVERED=1 while the composer is visibly EMPTY -- a flag reporting success for work that did not happen, which is this project's signature failure mode and exactly why this looked like 'the agent did nothing'.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY IS: the existing prompt-by-reference design (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-implementation.md, T1-T6 unstarted). The pod already has everything needed to pull rather than be pushed: GC_ALIAS=gonk.triage.p75.i35.a1 is in the environment. The entrypoint should fetch the prompt for its alias and hand it to 'opencode run' -- at which point part A stops being dead code and becomes the consumer that plan needs. So the two pieces compose: prompt-by-reference supplies delivery, part A supplies non-interactive execution, and neither works alone.

DO NOT ship part A expecting it to fix delivery. It cannot, until something puts the prompt where the entrypoint can read it.

title: The sweep waits for the SESSION to end, but opencode's TUI never exits -- this is why no comment has ever been posted
description:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-30 on project 75 issue !30, session gonk.triage.p75.i30.a1, agent pod s-go-1p8v. THIS IS THE REAL ANSWER TO gonk-712 and it supersedes gonk-au1's premise.

WHAT HAPPENED, with times:
  19:49:20  rig: checkout granted (alias gonk.triage.p75.i30.a1)
  19:50:37  broker session created, rung qwen3-14b, attempt 1
  ~19:51:1x agent emitted a COMPLETE GONK_BATCH_START/END fence
            tmux pane reports the model turn took 32.6s
  19:51:12  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  19:52:12  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  19:53:xx  same, and the pod is still Running at 4m23s

THE AGENT DID ITS JOB. It read the repo through the rig checkout (Read .agent/README.md, Glob **/*.ts, **/*.js), reasoned about the issue, and closed the fence -- all in 32.6 seconds of model time.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT TIME. cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go:284 brokerSessionView returns (nil, nil) whenever view.Running || view.State == sessionStateRunning, and cmd/gonk-gate/sweep.go:177 then logs 'still running; nothing to judge yet' and returns WITHOUT reading the batch. Gas City reports the session Running because the opencode TUI process is alive -- and the TUI does not exit after answering. So the session is PERMANENTLY Running, the completed batch is never read, and the bead waits until its reservation expires and is classified infra-failed.

WHY gonk-au1 IS WRONG. That bead concluded 'A triage turn on qwen3-14b takes longer than [5m], so the sweep reaps the session at the deadline EVERY TIME, before the agent can emit its fence.' The turn takes 32.6 SECONDS. The fence IS emitted, comfortably inside even the old 5m. What the 5m TTL actually did was cap how long we waited before reaping a session that was never going to report finished. Raising it to 30m (done, gitops 3ae5d0c) does not fix the milestone -- it only changes the reap from 5m to 30m, and it made this diagnosis possible by leaving the session alive long enough to inspect.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and they are a real design choice:
  (A) Make the agent process EXIT after emitting the batch -- run opencode non-interactively (run mode) rather than leaving a TUI resident. Cleanest, and it matches the broker model where the agent is a pure producer of one batch.
  (B) Judge on TRANSCRIPT CONTENT rather than session state: a closed GONK_BATCH_END is the completion signal, regardless of whether the process is alive. Decouples the verdict from a TUI lifecycle detail, but means defining 'complete' in the sweep.
(A) is probably right and (B) may be worth having anyway as a belt-and-braces completion signal. Note this also interacts with the old carry-forward that gonk-gate sweep is inert until something stamps SessionEndedAt.

SEPARATE DEFECT SEEN IN THE SAME RUN, worth its own bead: the emitted batch is not valid JSON. The label effect reads {"kind":"label","add":"gonk::bug","gonk::csv-export"} -- a bare value with no key -- and the object closes with one brace too many. Even once the sweep reads the batch, the shape gate will reject this. That is the argument for guided decoding (gonk-vpm) and it is now observed rather than predicted.
notes: FIXED. The premise -- 'this is why no comment has ever been posted' -- no longer holds: comments are posted routinely (!45, !48, !53, !58). Resolved by three changes rather than one: non-interactive 'opencode run' instead of the TUI, the sweep treating a CLOSED FENCE as the completion signal rather than process exit (gonk-au1), and the entrypoint holding after the turn so Gas City's tmux-backed transcript survives to be read (gonk-2tb).

title: reservation_ttl=5m reaps every triage session before it can finish -- this is why no comment has ever been produced
description:
THE ANSWER TO gonk-712, found 2026-08-19. It is a config value, not a code bug.

steve/gitops clusters/orac/apps/gonk/helmrelease-gonk.yaml sets operatorConfig.instance.meter.reservation_ttl: 5m, overriding the chart default of 60m. A triage turn on qwen3-14b takes longer than that, so the sweep reaps the session at the deadline EVERY TIME, before the agent can emit its GONK_BATCH_START/END fence.

MEASURED LIVE, issue !27 on project 75:
  01:15:27  broker session created         gonk.triage.p75.i27.a1  rung=qwen3-14b
  01:15:51  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  01:16:51  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  01:17:51  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  01:18:51  sweep: session still running; nothing to judge yet
  01:19:53  sweep: session still running past its reservation; reaping rather than waiting
            reservation_expired_at=2026-08-19T01:19:10.691564Z
  01:19:54  sweep: re-sling fired  outcome=infra-failed  next=retry
Roughly 3m43s from create to deadline (the reservation starts at /decide, just before the create). The agent was STILL WORKING and was killed for it.

WHY THIS HAS HIDDEN SO LONG. The classification is correct at every step and nothing looks like an error: 'still running; nothing to judge yet' is an INFO, the reap is the gonk-u1p.6 machinery working as designed, and infra-failed correctly does not escalate the rung. The bead then re-slings, gets reaped again, and exhausts max_infra_retries (2 here). Every layer reports exactly what it should. The prompt arrives -- verified by capturing the tmux pane of a live session, which shows the full triage prompt with the fence instructions rendered in opencode's composer -- so this is NOT gonk-e9m.

THE VALUE IS ALSO SUSPICIOUS ON ITS FACE: it sits in the file directly beneath max_clock_skew: 5m and max_spend_staleness: 5m, with no comment justifying it, which reads like it was matched to its neighbours rather than measured against a model turn.

WHAT TO DO. Raise it -- but measure first rather than guessing: one unreaped triage run against qwen3-14b tells you the real distribution, and the value should have headroom over the slow tail, not the median. Note the trade: a longer TTL means a genuinely wedged session holds its budget reservation longer before ExpireReservations reclaims it, and it interacts with max_infra_retries: 2 (two reaps and the bead is denied). It is a deployment value in gitops, NOT a chart default -- the chart's 60m is already generous.

WORTH CHECKING AT THE SAME TIME: gonk-gyj. The rung catalog points at qwen3-14b (16K context) while several 128K models are served, including a vLLM 35B. A faster or better-fitting model changes the required TTL.
notes: FIXED, and its stated premise was FALSIFIED along the way. The bead claimed 5m reaped every session; a measured turn took 32.6s. The real cause was brokerSessionView returning nil while view.Running, plus the transcript being unreadable after the entrypoint exited. reservation_ttl is now 30m and sessions complete: !58 finished in ~2m40s with 10 tool calls.
