title: Synthetic pricing was never applied in LiteLLM: the USD door does not close on ANY local rung
description: VERIFIED against the live cluster 2026-08-13. litellm-config's model_cost_map has exactly TWO entries, both for qwen3-14b (one bare, one 'anthropic/qwen3-14b'), and BOTH are priced input_cost_per_token: 0 / output_cost_per_token: 0. Every other local model -- qwen3-8b-bailey, qwen3.6:35b, qwen3.6:35b-nothink, nemotron3:33b, gemma4-26b-bailey, and both vLLM entries -- has no cost-map entry at all. Meanwhile the gonk HelmRelease declares synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens 0.25 (qwen3-14b) and 0.5 (qwen3-6-35b). Those synthetic prices exist ONLY on gonk's side. The chart's own comment says they MUST agree with LiteLLM's model_cost_map and it renders an advisory ConfigMap to copy from; it was never copied. CONSEQUENCE: real GPU work records spend 0.0, so the per-project USD virtual-key ceiling NEVER TRIPS on a local rung. This is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT reason local budgets do not bind, separate from the documented Ollama network bypass (gonk-8g9): even traffic that correctly traverses LiteLLM's front door is unpriced. Already demonstrated and written down at docs/environment.md:97-99 ('spend: 0.0 for the local model, on a real 25-token call... the synthetic-pricing problem demonstrated rather than argued') but never filed as work until now. WHAT STILL BINDS: gonk-meter's own token ceilings (monthly_tokens, per_task_tokens) are enforced in the meter's ledger independent of LiteLLM's USD accounting, and cloud rungs are priced normally, so CLOUD budgets remain hard. FIX: populate model_cost_map with the synthetic prices for every local model named by a rung, copying the chart's advisory ConfigMap; add a startup or CI check that every rung's synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens has a matching non-zero cost-map entry, so the two cannot silently diverge again. Also note both vLLM entries lack a model_info block entirely, so LiteLLM does not know their context window either -- relevant to gonk-gyj.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED BY ARITHMETIC, 2026-09-06.

The bead was still true: LiteLLM's entries for the local models carried no cost fields at all, only max_input_tokens. So every local rung billed $0, the virtual key's USD counter never moved, and a project's monthly_tokens ceiling had no hard enforcement anywhere. gonk's stated invariant -- a hard per-project budget at the LiteLLM door via virtual keys PLUS synthetic pricing -- was half-built: the keys were provisioned and the pricing never applied, so the guarantee was nominal.

APPLIED, matching each rung's synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens in the operator config:
  qwen3-14b                  0.25 USD/1M -> input_cost_per_token = output_cost_per_token = 2.5e-07
  qwen3.6-35b-vllm           0.50 USD/1M -> 5.0e-07
  qwen3.6-35b-vllm-nothink   0.50 USD/1M -> 5.0e-07

INPUT AND OUTPUT CARRY THE SAME RATE deliberately. opercfg.PricePerToken() is synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens / 1e6 -- ONE price per token, not a split -- and the meter reconciles against LiteLLM's spend, so a split here would silently desynchronise the two counters. The two 35b routes are priced identically so pointing a rung at either twin cannot change what a project spends.

VERIFIED END TO END, and the arithmetic is exact rather than approximate. A 25-token call (18 prompt + 7 completion) on the PROJECT's virtual key:
    expected 25 * 2.5e-07 = 0.0000062500
    observed spend        = 0.0000062500
and max_budget = 25.0, which is exactly monthly_cost_usd(0) + monthly_tokens(50M) * max pricePerToken(5e-7), the formula in internal/meter/litellm/admin.go.

A TRAP WORTH RECORDING for whoever tests this next: the gonk-litellm secret is the MASTER/ADMIN key the meter uses to PROVISION keys, not a project key. A call made with it bills a key with no alias and no budget, and the project's spend stays 0 while everything looks configured. The project's virtual key lives in the keysink secret, gonk-key-<project>-<hash> in the gonk namespace (GONK_KEYSINK_PREFIX). Test with that one.

STILL UNVERIFIED BY ANYTHING AUTOMATED: the agreement between the operator config's synthetic_usd_per_1m_tokens and LiteLLM's model_list. opercfg.go says as much -- "The operator MUST configure the same number in LiteLLM's model list. That agreement is unverifiable from here; Plan 06 checks it." It is now correct by hand; a drift check belongs in the e2e harness, because nothing in the gonk repo can see the gitops values.

title: Onboarding the agentic/ repos risks gonk watching ITSELF: membership=true inherits group membership
description: pkg/glab/projects.go:19-25 ListMemberProjects enumerates via GET /api/v4/projects?membership=true. GitLab's membership=true includes projects inherited through GROUP membership, not just direct project membership. nagus, rom and quark all live in the agentic/ group -- and so does gonk-project (id 69). Therefore: adding the gonk bot (user 49) to the agentic GROUP would silently make gonk-project a watched project, giving a code-writing agent a path to its own broker, gate and effect-shape.toml. That is precisely the scenario gonk-066 (workflow-scope gating, still open) exists to prevent, and it would arrive as a side effect of onboarding rather than as a decision. ACTIONS: (1) onboard nagus/rom/quark by PER-PROJECT membership only, never group-level; (2) verify whether the bot is already a group member and whether gonk-project is already being reconciled today; (3) consider a hard denylist of project IDs in intake config so self-watching fails closed regardless of how membership is granted -- belt and braces, since membership is granted in GitLab's UI outside gonk's control. Relates to gonk-4v8, gonk-066, gonk-8s0.

title: Support guided decoding as an OPTIONAL per-rung capability (shape gate stays the authority)
description: gonk's architecture depends on the agent emitting a well-formed proposed-effects batch, and Phase 3 adds a second schema-shaped artifact for review findings. Today that relies on the model following instructions plus a fence parser. Warp's equivalent defence is a TOLERANT PARSER -- scan for the last JSON object carrying the required keys -- implemented in three separate places, because models wrap output in prose despite explicit instructions. gonk can do strictly better: vLLM (xgrammar/outlines) and SGLang both support guided decoding. Constrain the sampler to the effect-batch JSON schema and malformed output becomes IMPOSSIBLE rather than tolerantly parsed -- an entire failure class removed, at the sampler, which is the most deterministic place available. This is an advantage Warp structurally cannot have (they proxy vendor APIs and can only constrain by prompting and retrying), and it composes with Phase 3: the annotated-diff coordinate scheme is far more reliable when the model cannot emit a syntactically invalid comment object. Requires the vLLM path (gonk-gyj). Evaluate whether LiteLLM passes guided-decoding params through to the backend, or whether gonk must call vLLM directly for this -- that routing question is the main unknown.
notes: NOW OBSERVED, not predicted. Live triage run 2026-08-30 (project 75 issue !30, qwen3-14b) emitted this as its effects batch: {"effects":[{"kind":"comment","body":"..."},{"kind":"label","add":"gonk::bug","gonk::csv-export"}]}} -- the label effect is a bare value with no key, and the object closes with one brace too many. It is not valid JSON, so the shape gate will reject it even once gonk-5k5 lets the sweep read it. The comment half was sensible prose; the failure is purely structural, which is exactly the class guided decoding removes at the sampler. This is the first real evidence for this bead rather than an argument from Warp's experience.

title: Onboard nagus, rom and quark as the first real target repos
description: DECIDED 2026-08-13 (owner): the first real targets are agentic/nagus, agentic/rom, agentic/quark on gitlab.orac.local. All Go, all with .gitlab-ci.yml, all with .agent/ already initialized (so ADR-007's orientation tier exists today, not hypothetically). PROFILES: nagus = 134 files, 33 test files, 73 commits/90d, DEPLOYED via gitops (own image + shared CNPG), sanitizes untrusted listing content -> genuine issue flow but the highest blast radius and security-sensitive. rom + quark = near-identical siblings scaffolded from homelab/go-service-template, 61 files / 4 test files each, 3 commits/90d, NOT deployed -> bounded blast radius but thin activity. Neither profile satisfies both criteria alone; together they do. SUGGESTED ORDER: prove the plumbing on rom or quark first (a bad MR costs nothing, small enough to diagnose in one sitting), hold the sibling as a control or A/B pair, bring nagus in third once the loop is trusted. RISK TO CHECK BEFORE ONBOARDING: all three are in the agentic/ group and so is gonk-project; gonk-8s0 records that discovery today is bot membership, so a GROUP-level bot add would give the agent a path to gonk's own broker/gate/effect-shape.toml -- exactly what gonk-066 exists to prevent. Onboard PER-PROJECT, never group-wide. Uniform Go toolchain across all three makes the .gonk.yml validation contract consistent and known-good. Three projects also makes per-project budgets and attribution (gonk-m6t) genuinely exercised rather than theoretical.

title: gonk's rung catalog routes to qwen3-14b (16K ctx) while a vLLM-served 35B at 128K sits unused
description: LiteLLM serves 7 local models. gonk's site-local rung catalog names qwen3-14b, which litellm-config pins to num_ctx/context_window/max_input_tokens/max_tokens = 16384 via ollama_chat/qwen3:14b. Meanwhile bailey-gpu runs a vLLM deployment (up 8h) serving RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 as qwen3.6-35b-nvfp4, exposed through LiteLLM as 'qwen3.6-35b-vllm' and 'qwen3.6-35b-vllm-nothink' at api_base http://vllm.bailey-gpu.svc.cluster.local:8000/v1. vLLM args: --max-model-len=131072, --gpu-memory-utilization=0.35 (~45GB), --max-num-seqs=16, --max-num-batched-tokens=16384 (prefill batch budget, NOT the context window -- easily misread as one), fp8_e4m3 KV cache, chunked prefill, prefix caching, MTP speculative decoding, and crucially --enable-auto-tool-choice with --tool-call-parser=qwen3_xml + --reasoning-parser=qwen3. Also available at 128K: ollama qwen3.6:35b(-nothink) and nemotron3:33b. ACTION: point the implementation/triage rungs at the vLLM 35B (8x context, MoE 3B-active so fast, native tool-call parsing) and re-baseline any analysis that assumed a 16K window. Note --max-model-len is 131072 while the stated design target was ~250k; decide whether that is a deliberate step-down or drift. Also: docs/environment.md lines 60-62 still claim 'this instance's models are qwen3-14b and qwen3-8b-bailey' and is stale.

title: Credential Ollama so local-model budgets are hard, not advisory
description: Today an agent pod can reach http://192.168.1.142:11434 directly with NO credential, bypassing LiteLLM and therefore all metering and budget enforcement. This is the standing 'local budgets are advisory' gap, documented in docs/environment.md but never filed as work. The documented fix has always been 'unsuspend Cilium so NetworkPolicy is enforced' -- but an auth proxy in front of Ollama closes the same hole far more cheaply and does not depend on the CNI migration. One credential turns local budgets hard and removes the largest asterisk on the project's central claim. Complements gonk-7oz (agent NetworkPolicy too broad). Raised by the Fable second-opinion review, 2026-08-13, as the highest value-per-effort item not on any list.

title: Phase 2: spec gate -- roadmap.md/vision.md, 4-state triage, PRODUCT/TECH specs
description: Move human review upstream: approve a spec instead of correcting a finished diff (Warp's named highest-leverage checkpoint). (a) roadmap.md + vision.md at repo root with per-area routing hints and non-goals -- cheapest high-leverage item found. (b) 4-state triage rubric ready-to-implement/ready-to-spec/needs-info/wait-to-implement, NO confidence score or priority; cautious-tie-break; needs-info must list the smallest unblocking questions. (c) specs/<slug>/PRODUCT.md as NUMBERED testable invariants (no implementation) + TECH.md with commit-pinned links and tests mapped to invariant numbers -- the numbering is the join key across spec->impl->verify. (d) human approval gate before ready-to-implement. (e) skills as versioned files, <=200 lines, scripts shipped as resources not written on the fly. Composes with gonk-kxg and gonk-07d.
notes: REVISED per second-opinion review (roadmap 11b): SPLIT. The cheap routing half stays here -- roadmap.md/vision.md, 4-state triage rubric, skills-as-files. The SPEC AGENT (PRODUCT.md/TECH.md + human spec gate) MOVES AFTER Phase 3. Reason: Warp's spec gate removes variance across a team of engineers with differing prompt skill; that variance does not exist with one operator, who already IS the spec gate. What costs the operator is wrong diffs, and the detector for those is verification. Build the detector first.

title: Phase 1: implementation agent -- issue to reviewable MR
description: THE gap. New pack agent+order: read issue, smallest cohesive change, run validation, emit effects batch incl. branch/commit/mr. Extend pack/agents/*/effect-shape.toml beyond comment+label. Broker keeps sole write authority. Port anti-lying guardrails INTO THE VALIDATOR (batch claiming completion must carry a real MR URL; claiming validation passed must carry command+exit code; progress comments capped). Validation commands come from .gonk.yml fail-closed, never guessed. Stamp a deterministic MR<->bead metadata block (bead id, rung, skill version, session alias) -- this is the join key phases 3-4 need; retrofitting is expensive. See roadmap Phase 1.
notes: RE-REVISED 2026-08-13 per roadmap 11c. The 16K-context premise was WRONG: it is a property of the qwen3-14b Ollama alias, not the platform. LiteLLM serves 5 models at 131072 including a vLLM NVFP4 Qwen3.6-35B MoE with native tool-call parsing (gonk-gyj). So: the SEARCH SUBAGENT MOVES BACK OUT to Phase 4/5 -- it is a cost optimization, not a precondition. What moves UP instead, because the binding risk is now 'will the model emit a valid appliable edit' rather than 'will it fit': the annotated-diff coordinate scheme + validator, the anti-lying validator, the opencode edit-tool investigation (what its pinned edit tool does on a fuzzy miss and how much of a file it echoes -- the first real test of whether opencode stays the right harness for a code-writing rung), and tool-name tuning against the qwen3_xml parser. Also now blocked on gonk-4v8: the first target repo must be a real non-gonk project.

title: EPIC: local parity with Warp's cloud software factory
description: Roadmap: docs/research/2026-08-13-gonk-local-parity-roadmap.md. Reach triage->spec->implement->review->verify->ship->monitor entirely self-hosted with local inference, keeping gonk's invariants (hard per-project budgets, no LLM judges, zero forge creds in pods, fail-closed config). Sequencing principle: THROUGHPUT BEFORE INTAKE -- Warp's own factory stalled with 1300 issues stuck in ready-to-implement because triage scales and implementation does not. Phases: 0 unblock, 1 implementation agent, 2 spec gate, 3 review+verify, 4 feedback loop, 5 harden, 6 compound. MIT reference implementations listed in the roadmap appendix.
notes: Roadmap doc: docs/research/2026-08-13-gonk-local-parity-roadmap.md. Phase beads: gonk-3so (1 implement) -> gonk-e5r (2 spec) -> gonk-td7 (3 review+verify) -> gonk-g98 (4 feedback) -> gonk-1zu (5 harden) -> gonk-jk9 (6 compound). Phase 0 blockers gating gonk-3so: gonk-mzm, gonk-e9m, gonk-ob5, gonk-bgx, gonk-j9z (also gonk-msz, gonk-7oz). Deliberately NOT building: computer-use verification, embeddings index, session steering/handoff UI, mobile, multi-tenant/SSO, deep multi-agent orchestration, LLM-judged escalation.

title: Registry cleanup: gonk holds 183GB of 294GB; kaniko cache repo is 139GB unbounded
description: The gitlab registry PVC hit 100% (gonk-mzm) and gonk is the dominant consumer. Metadata-DB attribution: agentic/gonk-project/cache = 139GB across 1296 tags (kaniko --cache-repo, never pruned); gonk-agent 26GB/203 tags; gonk-controller 25GB/194; gonk-meter 4.3GB/391; gonk-intake ~3GB/197. Blobs referenced ONLY by gonk repos: 183GB of the 294GB total. Reclaim the cache repo and prune old build tags, then stop it recurring with a cleanup policy and a CI rules change.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-13. 921 tags deleted (not the 924 originally planned -- the guard fix in 4fdb6cf protects the three -testclock tags carrying the deployed sha, so gonk-meter kept 17 rather than 14. 924 minus 3 is exactly the expected delta).

FINAL STATE: cache 0, gonk-agent 17, gonk-controller 14, gonk-intake 16, gonk-meter 17. All 15 tags carrying v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 verified present across all four repos, including the three -testclock ones.

Reclamation still pending on the registry's 1-day GC review delay; expected 179 GB.
RECLAIM CONFIRMED 2026-08-17. The 1-day registry GC review delay has passed and the space came back: /var/lib/registry is 101G used of 296G, 195G free, 35%. Predicted 179G, observed roughly 195G across all repos. Closing.

Recurrence is gonk-07f's job (cleanup policy + volume alert). The CI half of 'stop it recurring' already landed in 10dda82 (stop rebuilding every image on every commit, drop caches that cannot hit) and 4fdb6cf (the prune guard protects every tag carrying the deployed sha, not just its build group).
close_reason: Prune complete (921 tags) and reclaim confirmed: 35% used, 195G free. Recurrence guard is gonk-07f.

title: Wire the rig checkout end to end: cmd mains, chart env, and getting the per-session URL into a pooled pod
description:
FOLLOW-ON to d7de8fc, which landed pkg/rig, the decision-point grant, the entrypoint fetch, the three-tier scaffold prompt and the NetworkPolicy. Those are built and tested; they are NOT yet reachable in a running cluster because nothing constructs them.

REMAINING:
 1. cmd/gonk-intake/main.go -- construct rig.Handler{Store: rig.NewStore(nil), Fetch: <the existing *glab.Client>} and pass it as intake.ServerConfig.Rig. Nil today, so /rig/ 404s and no checkout is ever served.
 2. cmd/gonk-gate/main.go -- construct rig.Client{BaseURL: <intake private addr>} and set dispatchDeps.Rig / RigBaseURL from env (suggest GONK_RIG_BASE_URL, defaulting to http://gonk-intake-internal.gonk.svc:9090). Unset today, so grantCheckout is a clean no-op and scaffold falls back to the probe list.
 3. chart -- surface that base URL to the controller (gonk-gate runs there) as a value + env. The NetworkPolicy already allows agent -> intake:9090.

 4. THE REAL ONE: GONK_RIG_URL is PER-SESSION, and a pooled generic pod cannot receive per-session env -- the same channel gap as gonk-e9m. entrypoint.sh reads GONK_RIG_URL and no-ops when empty, which is correct but means the fetch never fires on the pooled path today.
    TWO WAYS OUT, in preference order:
      a. Make the URL DERIVABLE instead of delivered: static base URL in pod env (per-install, which Gas City DOES allow) + the pod's own session alias. If the pod can learn its alias -- from Gas City env, hostname, or the downward API -- it composes the URL itself and no per-session channel is needed at all. THIS SHOULD BE CHECKED FIRST; it would decouple the checkout from e9m entirely. Establish what a session pod actually has in its environment.
      b. Deliver it with the assignment, once gonk-e9m's per-assignment delivery lands: at that point the entrypoint/wrapper runs per assignment and the clone step runs in the same moment, which is the shape e9m implies anyway.

 5. Once delivery works, flip needsCheckout["triage"] to true so triage can read .agent/ -- deliberately left false because it changes every triage prompt.
 6. Consider calling Store.Revoke when a session ends (session teardown already exists in gonk-gate), so a pod outliving its work stops being able to pull the tree. Grants expire in 30m regardless.

VERIFY WHEN DONE: a scaffold session on a real project produces .agent/ content that cites files only present in the repository, and the intake log shows 'rig: checkout granted' followed by a 200 delivery.
notes:
WIRED 2026-08-11, commit 100c70a. Items 1-4 done; 5 and 6 remain.

ITEM 4 RESOLVED, AND IT DID NOT NEED gonk-e9m. The question was whether a pooled generic pod could learn its per-session URL. It can, because the URL splits into two halves that are separately available:
  GONK_RIG_BASE_URL  per-INSTALL, injected into agent.toml [env] by the chart's bootstrap-city initContainer -- the same channel that already carries GONK_LITELLM_URL/GONK_MODEL.
  GC_ALIAS           per-SESSION, put in every agent pod's env by Gas City ITSELF (verified live with printenv; GC_SESSION_ID and GC_INSTANCE_TOKEN are there too).
The pod appends its own alias to a static base. No per-session channel, no Gas City change, no dependency on the delivery redesign.

This was already established in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-design.md's channel table -- I should have read that before writing gonk-j9z's item 4, which assumed the channel was closed. Worth knowing that design exists: it solves the same class of problem for the PROMPT and reaches the same conclusion.

Also confirmed while looking: agent pods are named s-<session-id> (s-go-8oj, s-go-4m4), so hostname is a second, independent route to pod identity if GC_ALIAS ever goes away. The pod additionally carries a projected SA token whose claims include pod.name/pod.uid -- the unforgeable upgrade path if gonk ever goes multi-tenant, per that same design.

DONE: intake constructs rig.Handler over its existing bot PAT (private listener only); gonk-gate constructs rig.Client from GONK_RIG_BASE_URL and grants at the decision point; the chart renders the base for BOTH the controller and the agent; entrypoint composes and fetches before opencode starts. Chart test covers both halves -- if either stops rendering, a pooled pod silently runs with no working copy and scaffold falls back QUIETLY rather than going red, so nothing else would catch it.

STILL OPEN:
 5. needsCheckout["triage"] is still false. Flipping it lets triage read .agent/ and changes every triage prompt -- do it deliberately, with a live run.
 6. Store.Revoke is never called. Grants expire in 30m regardless, but session teardown is the natural place.
 7. NOT YET PROVEN LIVE. Everything here is unit- and chart-tested; no real scaffold session has fetched a real tree. That needs a deploy and an onboarding run, and it is the only thing that would catch a wrong assumption about the GitLab archive's directory prefix (the entrypoint strips one component) or about GC_ALIAS's exact value at runtime.
ITEMS 5 AND 6 ALSO LANDED -- commit 26dfc3b (2026-08-12), whose message says 'Closes the two follow-ups left on gonk-j9z'. No bd update followed it, so the note above still listed them as open. Corrected 2026-08-17.

 5. needsCheckout['triage'] flipped to true. The issue is still injected; the addition is the project's own .agent/, which is what makes a triage judgement specific to THIS repository instead of generic -- and it is exactly what scaffold exists to write. Until this flip nothing read it, and the v1 formula told the agent to 'Load .agent/ from the repository first' with no repository present, which is the same empty-directory failure as gonk-msz. renderTriagePrompt mentions the working copy ONLY when a grant succeeded, so a fetch failure degrades to precisely the prompt triage used before -- claiming a checkout that is not there is the bug being fixed, so the prompt must never assert one unconditionally.
 6. closeSession now revokes the grant beside the session close. Best-effort and Debug-level (unlike the leaked-pod Error next to it) because grants carry a 30m TTL, so a failure costs at most that window; DELETE is idempotent, 204 for unknown or already-revoked, since teardown runs after the bead has moved on.

SO THE ONLY THING LEFT ON THIS BEAD IS ITEM 7: NOT PROVEN LIVE. All of items 1-6 are unit- and chart-tested and none has ever run in a cluster. THE CODE IS NOT DEPLOYED -- images are pinned at v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 (2026-08-10) and every rig commit (2739633, 2a70711, d7de8fc, 100c70a, 26dfc3b, d09b10a) is after it.

Two assumptions only a live run can check, both named earlier: the GitLab archive's directory prefix (the entrypoint strips one component) and GC_ALIAS's exact runtime value. And note the failure mode is QUIET by design -- if either half stops rendering, a pooled pod runs with no working copy and scaffold falls back silently rather than going red. The chart test is the only thing standing between that and an invisible regression, so the live verify line matters: intake log shows 'rig: checkout granted' followed by a 200 delivery, and the session's output cites files only present in the repository.
DEPLOYED 2026-08-18. v0.1.0-ef59b5b921ae is live in ns gonk (steve/gitops 76976c9): controller, intake and meter all Running on the new tag, 0 restarts, HelmRelease Ready=True. Items 1-6 are now RUNNING code rather than only tested code, for the first time.

Verified the chart half actually rendered rather than assuming it:
  GONK_RIG_BASE_URL=http://gonk-intake-internal.gonk.svc:9090   (controller env)
  GC_K8S_IMAGE=...gonk-agent:v0.1.0-ef59b5b921ae                (per-session pods)
That matters because if either stopped rendering, a pooled pod would run with no working copy and scaffold would fall back QUIETLY rather than going red.

ITEM 7 IS NOW THE ONLY THING LEFT AND IT IS ACTIONABLE. Still unproven: the GitLab archive's directory prefix (the entrypoint strips one component) and GC_ALIAS's exact runtime value. Verify line unchanged -- intake logs 'rig: checkout granted' followed by a 200 delivery, and the session's output cites files only present in the repository.

DO NOT use gonk:63:scaffold as the vehicle: it has ONE infra retry left of max_infra_retries=2 and a second failure needs another manual ledger delete (gonk-9nx). Use a fresh bead.

CAUTION FROM THE SAME CLUSTER CHECK: gonk-u6p is live and retrying every ~60s on gonk:75:issue:24, so the controller log currently carries a steady 409 stream. Filter it out before reading a triage run's logs or it will bury the lines you want.
ITEM 7 VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-19 on v0.1.0-6f8d09f46e0f. Issue !27 on project 75, session s-go-wuvq:

  /workspace has 4 files:  .agent/  .gonk.yml  README.md  RIG_PROOF.md
  /workspace/.agent:       README.md

That is the repository, in the pod, fetched by the pod itself from gonk-intake with no forge credential. First time this has ever worked.

WHAT ITEM 7 ACTUALLY CAUGHT, which is why it insisted on a live run: the extract passed 'tar --no-absolute-names', and THAT FLAG DOES NOT EXIST. GNU tar 1.35 spells the opt-out -P/--absolute-names and strips leading '/' by default. tar exited 64 on every session since the rig slice landed. Both assumptions this bead flagged as only-checkable-live turned out fine -- the archive prefix strips correctly with --strip-components=1, and GC_ALIAS holds the expected value -- and the thing that was broken was a flag nobody thought to doubt.

The failure was invisible by construction, three ways at once: the fetch is non-fatal by design, so it logged a WARNING and continued; the entrypoint runs under 'tmux new-session -d', so its stdout never reaches the container log; and BOTH grant sites logged success the whole time. 'rig: checkout granted' was true and meant nothing.

FIXED in 6f8d09f, with test/entrypoint/ as the guard -- deliberately NO build tag, because test/images/ (which does test the real container) has never run in CI (gonk-ak0). Reintroducing the flag fails it with the production error verbatim.

Items 1-6 were already done; item 7 was the last one. CLOSING.

INCIDENTAL, and it cost a verification round: my first attempt (issue !26, filed 01:10:55) vanished without trace because intake had restarted at 01:10:21 for this very deploy, and gonk-fan means the project reads unsynced and webhooks are 200'd and dropped. POST /admin/reconcile on the intake private port fixed it immediately ({kicked:true}, 202). The deploy-then-immediately-test loop walks straight into this every time.
close_reason: Item 7 verified live: /workspace carries the repository in a real session pod (s-go-wuvq, issue !27). Root cause was a non-existent tar flag; fixed in 6f8d09f with a CI-visible guard.

title: The agent NetworkPolicy allows any port to the whole gitlab namespace, so 'no forge access' rests on credentials alone
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while designing controller-side clone delivery (gonk-msz).

networkpolicy/gonk-agent egress, as deployed:
    53/udp,53/tcp -> ns kube-system            (DNS)
    4000/tcp      -> ns litellm                (the virtual key's endpoint)
    8080/tcp      -> gonk meter pods
    ANY PORT      -> ns gitlab                 <-- this one
There is NO egress rule for the controller (9443) or intake (9090).

WHY IT MATTERS. images/agent/entrypoint.sh states the design property outright: 'NO forge credentials in the agent pod (broker design, spec 9/10). The agent never talks to GitLab: the broker reads the issue and posts the triage comment on its behalf.' That property is currently enforced by ONE mechanism -- the absence of a credential. The network is wide open to GitLab on every port, so anything that puts a usable token in the pod immediately has full forge reach, with no second line of defence.

AND SOMETHING DOES SHIP A TOKEN: pack/formulas/gonk-triage.toml declares a bot_token var and documents it reaching the pod as GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_BOT_TOKEN (a DELIBERATE v1 compromise, per its own comment: 'two of these are secrets transiting an order var, which the v2 broker removes'). So the two halves of the safety story disagree: the entrypoint says no creds, the formula ships one, and the netpol would not stop it being used.

CORROBORATING BEHAVIOUR, observed live 2026-08-11: given a prompt that asked it to triage an issue, the model DID attempt to reach GitLab and reported 'Unable to fetch information from GitLab due to transport errors'. It failed on credentials/DNS, not because anything forbade the attempt.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY THEORETICAL. The agent runs untrusted, attacker-influenceable input by construction: an issue title and body written by anyone who can file an issue. gonk-e9m already showed that input reaching a shell. Defence in depth here is cheap.

SUGGESTED:
 1. Drop the blanket ns gitlab egress. The agent has no legitimate reason to reach the forge under the broker design -- the controller does all forge I/O. If a future checkout path needs it, allow exactly that (see gonk-msz: the preferred design clones controller-side and serves it, needing an egress rule to the CONTROLLER, not to GitLab).
 2. Remove bot_token from the formula var set, or document precisely why the pod still needs it and scope it.
 3. Keep the entrypoint's stated property and the netpol in agreement -- today a reader of either one would draw the wrong conclusion about the other.
notes:
NETPOL LANDED 2026-08-11, commit 2a70711 (owner-approved: drop entirely).

The agent->GitLab egress is now OFF by default behind networkPolicy.gitlabEgress.enabled, and PORT-SCOPED via networkPolicy.gitlab.ports even when deliberately re-enabled -- the in-cluster branch previously emitted no ports: at all, which is precisely what made it any-port. Replaced by egress to gonk-intake's private listener, which is where the per-session checkout now comes from (gonk-msz), so the pod gets a repository without ever holding a forge credential.

Tests: the existing test asserted the OPPOSITE (that agents CAN reach GitLab) and is inverted with the reasoning recorded; new tests cover off-by-default, port-scoping when enabled, and the intake checkout path. Assertions read the rendered egress RULES rather than the whole document, because the template's comments legitimately name the destinations it denies -- a substring check over the doc would have passed for the wrong reason. Goldens updated; the only manifest change is the gitlab namespaceSelector rule giving way to the intake podSelector rule.

STILL OPEN, deliberately NOT closed by this:
 1. pack/formulas/gonk-triage.toml still declares bot_token and documents it reaching the pod as GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_BOT_TOKEN. The netpol now means a leaked token buys much less, but the right fix is to stop shipping it. That is an owner decision, not a cleanup.
 2. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE: mention is not yet ported to the broker. If its v1 formula path expects the pod to reach GitLab it now fails at the network instead of quietly on credentials -- the better failure, but it IS a behaviour change. networkPolicy.gitlabEgress.enabled=true is the escape hatch.
 3. Cilium is still suspended, so NO NetworkPolicy on this cluster is enforced by the CNI. This change is correct in the manifest and enforced by nothing today; do not read the green tests as a dropped packet.

title: Scaffold is told the repo is checked out in its workdir, but nothing ever clones it
description:
RAISED BY OWNER 2026-08-11, confirmed by inspection the same day.

pack/formulas/gonk-triage.toml's step tells the agent to do four things:
  'Read issue !{{issue_iid}} in project {{project}} and triage it.'
  'Load .agent/ from the repository first: it is the project's own context.'
  'Apply labels to the issue, each prefixed {{label_prefix}}.'
  'Post exactly one comment ...'
All four are GitLab or repository operations.

THE POD CAN DO NONE OF THEM:
  - images/Dockerfile.agent creates /workspace EMPTY (mkdir -p /workspace; WORKDIR /workspace). Nothing clones the rig into it.
  - images/agent/entrypoint.sh only ASSUMES a clone: RIG_DIR=/mnt/c/Users/steve/Code/gonk, and it treats a missing .git as non-fatal ('no clone yet'). It installs a git hook into a repository that is not there.
  - The controller's Gas City data root /city has NO rigs directory at all, so the city is not holding a clone to hand over either. Controller logs corroborate: 'assignedWorkBeads: 0 beads (rigStores=0)'.
  - entrypoint.sh states outright: 'NO forge credentials in the agent pod (broker design, spec 9/10). The agent never talks to GitLab: the broker reads the issue and posts the triage comment on its behalf.'

So the prompt and the pod contradict each other. Observed live 2026-08-11 while proving gonk-e9m: the model followed the prompt, tried to reach GitLab, and returned a fence whose entire content was 'Unable to fetch information from GitLab due to transport errors.' The fence was well-formed -- the delivery channel worked -- and the triage was still worthless.

I originally waved this through as expected behaviour for a credential-less pod. That was wrong: the agent should never have been REACHING for GitLab, because the prompt should never have asked it to.

RELATED CONTRADICTION worth resolving at the same time: the formula declares a bot_token var and says it reaches the pod as GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_BOT_TOKEN, while entrypoint.sh claims the pod holds no GONK_BOT_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN and wires no glab auth. Either the pod has forge creds or it does not; right now the docs say no and the plumbing ships one.

OWNER'S DIRECTION: opencode should not be fetching from GitLab at all. Either
  (a) the startup script prepares the workdir by CLONING FROM THE CONTROLLER before it starts opencode, or
  (b) the agent is instructed to do that immediately on session start.
(a) is the better fit for the broker design -- it keeps forge creds out of the pod entirely and makes the workdir a precondition rather than a task the model can fail. It needs the controller to expose a clone source, which /city does not currently provide.

Either way the ISSUE TEXT itself should be injected, not fetched: dispatch already has the title and body from the webhook payload (see gonk-kp5), so the agent never needs to read GitLab to triage.

BLOCKS REAL TRIAGE OUTPUT: until this is fixed, a perfectly delivered prompt still yields a fence containing an error, which is the artifact the sweep will accept.
design:
CORRECTED 2026-08-11 after reading both prompt paths. My original framing conflated them.

THERE ARE TWO TRIAGE PROMPTS, and only one is broken:

1. v1 FORMULA -- pack/formulas/gonk-triage.toml. Tells the agent to 'Read issue !N', 'Load .agent/ from the repository first', 'Apply labels', 'Post exactly one comment'. All four need forge creds or a checkout the pod does not have. This is the defective one, and per gonk-e9m's evidence ('<!-- gonk:model:... -->' + 'Triage GitLab issue !18') it is what was live.

2. v2 BROKER -- cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go renderTriagePrompt. ALREADY DOES EXACTLY WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR, verbatim:
     'Here is the issue, already fetched for you -- do NOT fetch anything yourself'
     'Do NOT post anything yourself. Do NOT run glab, git, bd, or any external API -- you hold no credentials and any such call will fail.'
   runBrokerDispatch fetches the issue CONTROLLER-SIDE (buildIssueContext) precisely because 'the pod has no forge creds', degrading to a reference-only prompt if the fetch fails. The agent only EMITS a GONK_BATCH of comment/label effects; gonk-sweep applies them under the controller's own PAT.

So for TRIAGE the owner's requirement is already designed and implemented -- it ships with the broker slice (gonk-u1p). No clone is needed there at all: injecting the issue text is strictly better than cloning, and the broker already does it.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP IS SCAFFOLD, and it is exactly the owner's point.
renderScaffoldPrompt tells the agent:
    'Write durable project context for the repository X, WHICH IS CHECKED OUT IN YOUR WORKING DIRECTORY.'
    'Read enough of it to be accurate...'
    'Reading the working directory is expected and encouraged.'
and its own comment says 'The agent has no forge creds but it DOES have the repository checked out in its rig, so unlike triage it is told to read.'

NOTHING CHECKS IT OUT:
  - images/Dockerfile.agent creates /workspace EMPTY (mkdir -p /workspace; WORKDIR /workspace).
  - images/agent/entrypoint.sh only ASSUMES a clone (RIG_DIR=$PWD) and treats a missing .git as non-fatal, installing a git hook into a repo that is not there.
  - The controller's /city has NO rigs directory; controller logs show 'rigStores=0'.
So scaffold is asked to read a repository that is not present, and 'an honest gap is a SUCCESS' means it will cheerfully write .agent/ files describing a project it never saw. That is worse than failing: it produces confident, wrong, DURABLE context that every later session reads.

THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND gonk-bgx ('a newly-onboarded project can never reach triage: scaffold gates it'). Scaffold cannot do its job, so the gate never opens.

FIX, following the owner's option (a) -- prepare the workdir BEFORE opencode starts:
  1. The controller clones the rig and the entrypoint materialises it at WORKDIR, so the checkout is a PRECONDITION rather than a task the model can fail. Clone from the controller, not the forge, to keep forge creds out of the pod (broker design, spec 9/10).
  2. Scaffold must FAIL LOUDLY if the workdir has no repo, instead of writing invented context. The current 'honest gap is a SUCCESS' wording is safe only when the repo is genuinely present.
  3. Triage needs no clone -- keep the broker's inject-the-issue approach.

ALSO RESOLVE THE CRED CONTRADICTION: gonk-triage.toml declares a bot_token var reaching the pod as GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_BOT_TOKEN, while entrypoint.sh states the pod holds no GONK_BOT_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN and wires no glab auth. Either the pod has forge creds or it does not; today the docs say no and the plumbing ships one.
notes:
CHECKOUT DELIVERY, DESIGNED 2026-08-11 from the owner's correction. The owner is right and my earlier objection was wrong in an important way.

I said a clone could not work because pods are pooled and generic and the project is unknown at pod start. That only rules out cloning IN THE ENTRYPOINT AT POD START. It does not rule out the clone, because the right trigger is not pod start -- it is THE DECISION POINT, controller-side: the moment the broker has read the project's config from the repo, parsed it, compared the config for that event shape against the event, and decided to act. At that instant the project, the ref and the event shape are all known, and the controller holds the PAT. That is exactly where a shallow clone belongs.

FEASIBILITY, checked rather than assumed:
  - git, tar and gzip ARE in the agent image (curl and wget are NOT), so the pod can clone over HTTP using git itself. No new tooling needed.
  - Gas City CANNOT hand the pod a volume: its k8s session provider exposes only GC_K8S_IMAGE, GC_K8S_NAMESPACE, GC_K8S_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and GC_K8S_PREBAKED. No PVC/volume knob, and CreateSessionRequest has no rig field. So a shared-PVC handoff needs an upstream change; everything below is doable in gonk alone.
  - Longhorn provides RWX if a shared volume is ever preferred later.

PROPOSED SHAPE (no forge creds in the pod, works with pooled pods):
 1. At the decision point, gonk-gate shallow-clones the project with the controller's PAT (--depth 1, single ref) into a per-session workspace keyed by the session alias.
 2. The controller serves that workspace as a git repo over HTTP on an in-cluster endpoint, at an unguessable per-session path (the alias is already a unique correlation key).
 3. The pod clones it: git clone --depth 1 <url> into WORKDIR, BEFORE opencode starts, so the checkout is a precondition rather than a task the model can fail -- which is the owner's option (a), just sourced from the controller instead of the forge.
 4. The URL is per-session, so it rides the same per-assignment channel the prompt does. That is why this pairs naturally with gonk-e9m: once delivery is per-assignment, a clone step runs at the same moment, with the project finally known.

CONDITIONAL BY EVENT SHAPE, per the owner: most shapes need the checkout, some do not (an MR approval, for instance). The decision point is already where that is known, so 'does this event shape need a checkout?' belongs in the same config comparison rather than being a separate lookup later.

BLOCKER TO NOTE: networkpolicy/gonk-agent has NO egress to the controller (9443) or intake (9090), so step 3 needs a new rule. It DOES currently allow any port to the whole gitlab namespace -- filed as gonk-7oz, and that rule should be dropped as part of this rather than relied upon, since cloning from the forge directly would need creds in the pod.

WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES: the controller-side probe-list context that landed in 2739633 is the SAFETY floor, not the destination. It stops scaffold inventing .agent/ content today. A real shallow checkout gives full-repository fidelity and removes the context-budget ceiling that forced the probe list, at which point buildRepoContext can be retired for scaffold.

title: Sweep cannot read a broker session: the session key matches 2 Gas City sessions and the read 409s
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-11 08:42:53Z on v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55, gonk-controller log.

  api: GET /v0/city/gonk/session/gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1 409
  WARN sweep: could not read broker session bead=gonk:75:issue:24
  err: 409 urn:gascity:error:session-conflict -- 'ambiguous session identifier:
       "gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1" matches 2 sessions: go-s4ug, go-93gk'

gonk addresses broker sessions by a DERIVED key (gonk.triage.p<project>.i<issue>.a<attempt>) and assumes it identifies at most one Gas City session. It does not: two sessions carry the same key, so Gas City refuses to guess and returns 409. The sweep then cannot read the session it is responsible for, for THIS bead, permanently -- the ambiguity does not age out on its own.

WHY THERE ARE TWO. Not yet established. Most likely a re-sling created a second session under the same attempt number rather than incrementing .a<n>, which would make every re-slung bead a candidate to wedge this way. gonk-e9m's re-sling loop (no fence -> re-sling) is the obvious source of repeat attempts, so the two are probably linked.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is a THIRD distinct way for a bead to sit forever while every layer reports success: intake 200s the webhook, the session exists, and the sweep's read is the only thing that fails -- as a WARN, not an error. Same silent-stall signature as gonk-zp3 and gonk-2do.

NEXT STEPS:
 1. Find both sessions (go-s4ug, go-93gk) and diff their creation time, attempt number and bead ref to establish which code path minted the duplicate.
 2. Decide the contract: either the derived key must be unique by construction (include the session ULID, or always increment .a<n>), or the sweep must handle a multi-match by selecting the newest rather than failing.
 3. A 409 here should not be a WARN the sweep shrugs off -- an unreadable session means the bead cannot progress and should be surfaced.
notes:
STILL LIVE AFTER THE 2026-08-18 DEPLOY, and it is a PERMANENT RETRY LOOP, not a one-off. Observed on v0.1.0-ef59b5b921ae:

  {"level":"WARN","msg":"sweep: could not read broker session","bead":"gonk:75:issue:24",
   "err":"gascity: GET /v0/city/gonk/session/gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1: 409: ..."}

Firing roughly every 60 seconds, indefinitely -- 20 matching lines in a 10-minute window. The bead gonk:75:issue:24 is the same issue that produced the zp3 diagnosis on 2026-08-10, so this has been retrying continuously for over a week and will not stop on its own.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS PRIORITY SUGGESTS: sweep never reaches a terminal judgement for this bead, so nothing ever closes it and nothing reclaims whatever it holds. That is the same shape as gonk-xkm (the capacity leak that wedged the cluster on 2026-08-03) -- a per-dispatch resource that is never released because the code path that would release it cannot complete. Worth checking whether the 409 also blocks session teardown, and if so this is a P1 that behaves like a P0 over a long enough window.

Also note it makes the controller log permanently noisy, which raises the cost of reading it during any future live debugging -- exactly what gonk-6a6 was fixed to enable.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND THE STALL IS FIXED 2026-08-18. The 409 was never the reason this was permanent -- the reason was gonk's own handling of it.

sweepRunning computed 'expired' (the reservation deadline) at sweep.go:147 and then RETURNED on any session-read error at :152-156, before the switch that uses it. So the deadline was computed and thrown away on exactly the path that needed it most. Everything downstream -- gate.Signals{ReservationExpired: expired}, gate.Classify, the meter Outcome call -- was unreachable for an unreadable session.

VALIDATED EXHAUSTIVELY, not by inspection of the one path. Every exit from sweepRunning before gate.Classify:
  L139  v1 bead with no session stamp        -- not a broker path, correct
  L156  broker session read error            -- THE BUG, ignored 'expired'
  L165  still running, v == nil              -- CORRECT, guards on '&& !expired'
  L267  meter Outcome failed                 -- after Classify, different concern
L165 is what proves it was an oversight rather than a decision: the adjacent branch, for the same class of 'cannot judge yet', explicitly honours the deadline. And only two call sites read a session -- broker_apply.go:285 (sweep, affected) and broker_inject.go:728 (dispatch-side prompt polling, different lifecycle) -- so no other handler shares the defect.

(For the record: I tried validating this via graphify first. It did not -- graphify-out/ is from 2026-07-30, predates fc77fb4, and places sweepRunning at L115 rather than L130; it is also a reference graph, so it answers 'what references what', not 'which branches return early'. The exhaustive grep above is what actually established it.)

THE FIX. The error path now splits on the same deadline the running path uses: inside the reservation it still returns and retries next tick (a transient 5xx must not become a verdict), past it, it falls through with view nil so ReservationExpired classifies the bead INFRA-FAILED. That does not escalate the rung (gate.Escalates is true only for gate-failed) and IS bounded by max_infra_retries, so the bead can finally stop instead of retrying a read that can never succeed.

Tests: TestSweepClassifiesABrokerSessionItCanNeverRead (reproduces the production 409 exactly, failed before the fix with '0 outcomes') and TestSweepStillWaitsOnAnUnreadableSessionInsideItsReservation (pins that the in-reservation behaviour did NOT change). gcapitest gained AmbiguousAlias, deliberately a set and not a countdown -- a decrementing fake would model a transient blip and hide the only property under test. Gates green: gofmt, vet, go test ./..., chart, pack.

NOT FIXED HERE, filed as gonk-6n8: the duplicate alias itself. Two sessions were minted under gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1 4m29s apart because the meter's attempt number is idempotent while an unsettled reservation is open, and dispatch is not. This fix makes the resulting ambiguity SURVIVABLE; 6n8 is what stops it being created.

VERIFY AFTER DEPLOY: gonk:75:issue:24 should classify infra-failed and stop looping. The one thing that would prevent it is a ZERO ReservationExpiresAt on that record ('expired' is false when the field is unset) -- broker_inject.go:638 does stamp it from the decide response, so it should be set, but confirm the 60s WARN actually stops rather than assuming it.
VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-18 on v0.1.0-0376e5ba05d7. The stall is over.

  22:12:46 WARN  broker session unreadable past its reservation; classifying rather than retrying forever
                 bead=gonk:75:issue:24 reservation_expired_at=2026-08-10T23:16:06.382128Z
  22:12:46 ERROR POST /v1/policy/outcome failed (meter still starting, connection refused) -- retried
  22:13:17 WARN  classifying rather than retrying forever  (the real 409, naming go-s4ug and go-93gk)
  22:13:18 INFO  sweep: re-sling fired  outcome=infra-failed  next=retry
  22:13:18 WARN  bead denied  reason=infra-retries-exhausted
                 detail='rung "qwen3-14b" failed on infrastructure 2 times in a row'

First terminal judgement for that bead in eight days, and then it STOPPED -- infra-failed did not escalate the rung and max_infra_retries bounded the retries, exactly as the fix intended. Zero 'could not read broker session' lines in the following five minutes.

MY DEPLOY CAVEAT IS RESOLVED: reservation_expired_at is populated (2026-08-10T23:16:06Z), so broker_inject.go:638 does stamp it and no manual ledger clear was needed.

BONUS EVIDENCE FOR THE OTHER HALF OF THE GUARD: the 22:12:46 tick hit a genuinely transient error (meter still starting) and sweep RETRIED rather than losing the bead, then classified on the next tick once the 409 was the real error. That is the post-Classify return path at sweep.go:267 doing its job, and it means the fix distinguishes transient from permanent in production and not merely in the unit test.

MINOR, NOT WORTH ITS OWN BEAD UNLESS IT RECURS: the teardown that follows the verdict logged 'POST /v0/city/gonk/session/gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1/close 404'. Harmless here -- both sessions had already ended, so there was nothing to close -- but note the close is BY ALIAS and so is subject to the same ambiguity; a close against an ambiguous alias cannot be trusted to have closed the right thing. gonk-6n8's unique-by-construction alias fixes that too.

CLOSING. The stall this bead describes is fixed and proven. The remaining work -- stopping two sessions being minted under one alias in the first place -- is gonk-6n8.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: the bead classified infra-failed and stopped after 8 days looping. Alias-uniqueness half is gonk-6n8.

title: opencode run --attach silently yields an empty turn; standalone run works
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while proving out-of-band prompt delivery for gonk-e9m, in-cluster, real gonk-agent image v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55.

SYMPTOM. 'opencode run --attach http://127.0.0.1:4096 --model gonk/qwen3-14b --format json <prompt>' against a local 'opencode serve' creates a session, emits exactly ONE event -- step_start, with a real sessionID and messageID -- then EXITS 0. No assistant text, no tool call, no error on stdout, stderr or the server log. Reproduced 3/3.

Server DEBUG log shows it gets all the way to the provider and then stops:
  message=stream providerID=gonk modelID=qwen3-14b agent=build mode=primary
  message='llm runtime selected' llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=gonk llm.model=qwen3-14b
...and nothing after it.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, by direct test against LiteLLM with the SAME project virtual key (gonk-key-homelab-talos-toolkit-7eca789a):
  - LiteLLM reachable and the key valid: /v1/models lists all three rungs.
  - The model answers: a plain completion for 'Reply with exactly the word GOLF...' returned content 'GOLF', 36 tokens. So the model is up and not cold-start-failing.
  - Tool-calling is SUPPORTED: the same model handed a tools array returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed read_file call. So 'the local model cannot do tools' is NOT the explanation.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, untested. LiteLLM advertises qwen3-14b with max_input_tokens 16384 -- the SMALLEST of the three rungs and the FIRST rung in the instance ladder, i.e. the default for every triage. opencode's build agent sends a large system preamble plus ~20 tool schemas before any user text; a trivial request measured 33 prompt_tokens bare and 138 with ONE tool defined. If the preamble exceeds 16K the request fails at the provider, and the ai-sdk path appears to swallow that into an empty successful turn.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND e9m. If confirmed, triage on rung 1 can never produce an artifact regardless of how the prompt is delivered, and enforce_ladder_order=true means rung 1 is where every bead starts. That would make this a second, independent cause of the same 'session runs, produces nothing' signature that gonk-zp3/gonk-e9m chased -- and it fails SILENTLY and returns exit 0, which is the property that made the first one cost six days.

NEXT STEPS:
 1. Count the real preamble: run the same prompt against qwen3.6:35b (131072 input) -- if it completes, the limit is confirmed as the cause with no code change needed to test.
 2. Ask LiteLLM for the failing request: check its logs for a context-length error on the qwen3-14b call at 2026-08-11T08:42:38Z.
 3. If confirmed: either raise qwen3-14b's context, drop it as a triage rung, or give triage a smaller agent than 'build' (opencode run --agent).
 4. Independently, opencode turning a provider error into exit 0 with no diagnostic is worth an upstream report -- DRAFT, DO NOT POST (docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md).
notes:
DIAGNOSED AND CORRECTED 2026-08-11. MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG -- recorded here because it was wrong in a way worth not repeating.

I blamed rung 1's 16K input limit. It is not that. A completed turn measures input=6415 tokens for a trivial prompt and 6676 for a realistic triage prompt -- opencode's build-agent preamble is ~6.4K, comfortably inside qwen3-14b's 16384. Ruled out by measurement, not argument.

THE ACTUAL FAULT is --attach. Proven side-by-side in ONE pod, same overlay, same model, same prompt, seconds apart:
  standalone  opencode run ...            -> step_start, text 'GOLF', step_finish reason=stop, input=6415 output=3
  attached    opencode run --attach ...   -> step_start ONLY, exit 0, no text, no error
Server DEBUG on the attached run is identical up to 'llm runtime selected llm.provider=gonk llm.model=qwen3-14b', then goes straight to loop step=1 / 'exiting loop' with nothing in between.

NOT merely a client-side display loss. 'opencode export <sessionID>' run against the SERVER afterwards returns no assistant text for that session either. The turn genuinely produces nothing; the client is not just failing to render it.

Corroborating, from the other end: neither LiteLLM nor ollama ever saw a chat completion for the attached runs. ollama reported 'all slots are idle' with only qwen3:14b resident throughout. So --attach abandons the turn BEFORE any HTTP request to the provider.

CONSEQUENCE FOR gonk-e9m: the out-of-band design stands, but it must NOT be built on serve + run --attach. Standalone 'opencode run' is proven working and is the path to build on; --session/--continue still need to be proven for resume (spec 11.4) since they were only exercised via the broken --attach here.

WORTH AN UPSTREAM REPORT (DRAFT, DO NOT POST -- docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md): 'run --attach' abandons a turn and exits 0 with no diagnostic on any stream. Exit 0 on a silently dropped turn is the same fail-silent class that cost this project six days on gonk-zp3.

WHILE HERE, unrelated and live: ollama is returning a steady stream of 503 'maximum pending requests exceeded' on /api/embed from 10.244.5.80, with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1. That is the queue-full flood pattern, not OOM. Not gonk's, but someone's -- filing separately.
CLOSING AS DIAGNOSED 2026-08-17. The question this bead asked -- why does the attached run produce nothing -- is answered, and the answer is recorded on gonk-e9m as a correction to its design field, which is where it changes a decision. Nothing here is a code fix in gonk: the fault is in opencode's --attach path, and gonk's response is simply not to build on it.

Remaining work has been split out rather than dropped:
 - the upstream draft is now gonk-ckb (P3, drafts on disk, owner posts).
 - --session/--continue for resume are recorded on gonk-e9m as UNPROVEN, since they were only ever exercised through the broken --attach.
 - the ollama /api/embed 503 flood noticed while here was already handled: gonk-38o, closed 2026-08-11 (restored nomic-embed-text failover).

WORTH KEEPING FROM THIS BEAD: my first hypothesis was wrong and the correction is instructive. I blamed rung 1's 16K input limit; measurement killed it (a real triage prompt is 6676 input tokens against qwen3-14b's 16384, so the preamble was never the problem). The 16K figure went on to be wrong at the roadmap level too -- see the local-parity roadmap section 11c.1, where 'qwen3-14b at 16K' turned out to be the wrong model entirely and several 128K models were already served. Two separate conclusions were drawn from that one bad number.
close_reason: Diagnosed: --attach is the fault, not context length. Design correction recorded on gonk-e9m; upstream draft split to gonk-ckb.

title: DEPLOY: v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 -- ships the meter key-alias fix (gonk-c4s), currently only hand-patched

notes:
DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-11 08:31Z.

Tag v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 (pipeline 2043, 19/19 green) is live on all four images. Chose 2043 over the newer green 2044/2045: those build 04264f1/9455abf, which are bead- and docs-only commits with no code delta over 4b3c7e1, so rolling them adds churn and re-opens verification for nothing.

  controller sha256:dee92905..  intake sha256:12bcfbc5..
  meter      sha256:22f61f0d..  agent  sha256:35728415..

Step 2 -- gitops e38b094 bumped all four tags (helmrelease-gonk.yaml 74/86/97/102), 83 convention checks passed, pushed. Worth knowing for the next deploy.

PROOF THE FIX IS LIVE, not just absence of a warning: intake's reconcile re-registered BOTH projects against the new meter at 08:25:56 and 08:25:57, i.e. AFTER meter began listening at 08:25:10. Both returned state=active with intact key_refs. Re-registering a project whose LiteLLM key already exists is exactly the recurrence condition that used to yield key-missing, so the duplicate-alias path is confirmed fixed against the live LiteLLM.

Incidental: intake came up ~70s before meter and logged 6 'meter registration failed' connection-refused WARNs before succeeding. Self-healing, but it is startup-order noise on every rollout.
