title: beadstore List and findBeadID silently truncate at bd's default limit of 50
description:
LIVE BUG, found 2026-08-10 while resolving the source-beads design blockers. Independent of that design.

pkg/beadstore/bd.go runs 'bd list --label <x> --json' at line 90 (findBeadID) and line 220 (List) with NO --limit. bd list defaults to --limit 50 (use 0 for unlimited); the file contains zero occurrences of 'limit'.

CONSEQUENCE NOW: runSweep does Store.List(StateRunning) and Store.List(StateParked). Past 50 running beads the sweep SILENTLY SEES ONLY 50 -- the rest are never judged, never closed, and their sessions are never torn down. It degrades exactly when the system is busiest, and it looks identical to 'there was nothing to do'. Same failure shape as gonk-6a6: silence that reads as success.

findBeadID is likelier benign (an anchor should match one bead) but it also silently drops a >50 result set, and it already ignores len(rows)>1 -- see ADR-003 line 122, 'a duplicate bead means duplicate spend'.

FIX: pass --limit 0 explicitly, or paginate. Then add a test that proves >50 beads are all returned -- the current tests cannot catch this because the fakes do not model bd's default.

BLOCKS the source-beads patrol (gonk-8us), which by design enumerates the entire retained backlog every pass.

title: Source beads design review: 10 blockers before slice 2 can start
description:
A superpowers code review of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md found roughly half its factual claims wrong or overstated, and the wrong ones were load-bearing. Verdict: NOT READY TO IMPLEMENT. The principle (level-triggered, record-at-receipt) was endorsed.

VERIFIED WRONG BY ME AFTER THE REVIEW, not taken on trust:
- pkg/gcapi has NO bead route (grep returns nothing) -> OD-2 is blocked, not resolved.
- ghook Deduper.Seen RECORDS the key and returns false on first sight (dedupe.go:43), so 'fail the webhook and GitLab retries' is a no-op -- the redelivery hits OutcomeDuplicate and is answered 200+dropped.
- the webhook handler is ASYNC (main.go:315-323, non-blocking send to a 256 chan, 200 written immediately), so failing the webhook on a store error is an architecture change, not a return-code change.
- beadstore.StateNeedsHuman's own comment says the sweeper must NEVER re-pick denied beads; the spec listed budget deny among the holes to cover and had no needs-human row. As written the patrol would re-drive denied work every pass and spend money on work already declined.

Full list of the 10 blockers is in the spec's 'Code review outcome' section: OD-2 mechanism, deny terminal, storage shape at backlog scale (BdCLI forks one bd comments per row and appends a JSON comment per write), anchor charset validation against payload-injected delimiters, immutable anchor identity (owner/repo renames), the parse rule, migration label ordering, stampede controls (freshness bound, ordering, fairness, dry-run gate), groups: not generalizing to non-path sources, and resolution-vs-live-session ownership.

Blocks gonk-9w0 (slice 2). gonk-cjb (slice 1) can proceed on items 4/5/6, which are anchor-format decisions.

RELATED: gonk-fm7.2 raised the OD-2/idempotency intersection on 2026-07-30 and was never answered. Answer it as part of OD-2 -- it is the same question.
notes:
BLOCKER 1 AND 3 RESOLVED 2026-08-10, and both were my error.

Gas City HAS a full bead HTTP API -- POST /v0/city/{city}/beads, GET /v0/city/{city}/bead/{id}, /update /close /reopen /assign /deps, /beads/ready, /beads/graph/{id}, with ?limit= supported. Verified in the gascity source at the pinned GASCITY_REF. pkg/gcapi having no bead route meant only that WE NEVER WROTE THAT CLIENT. I checked gonk's client and reported it as a platform gap. That is the second time this session an unverified negative produced a wrong conclusion.

BLOCKER 1 (OD-2 mechanism): RESOLVED. Intake writes source beads over the existing signed city API with a new pkg/gcapi client. No Dolt credential, no netpol egress to 3306, no upstream gascity change, no new service -- intake already holds the grant and already talks to gonk-controller:9443.

BLOCKER 3 (storage shape): LARGELY DISSOLVES. The enumeration problem was BdCLI's fork-per-row plus append-only comment log. An HTTP list with ?limit= returns the set in one call with no subprocess. BdCLI stays for the controller's in-flight path; source beads do not inherit its shape.

ADR-003 decision 4 SUPERSEDED NARROWLY (owner): intake gains exactly one piece of durable state, the source bead, because a stateless intake cannot satisfy requirement 1. Cache stays derived/in-memory. Decision 6 (intake does not resolve config -- meter owns Config(anchor)) and decision 3 (non-200s limited to 401/405/415/413) both STAND.

Remaining blockers are the eight I can resolve from evidence: deny terminal, anchor charset validation, immutable numeric ids, parse rule, migration ordering, stampede controls, config-resolution ownership (settled by ADR-003 d6), resolution-vs-live-session ownership.

title: Source beads 4: patrol re-evaluates eligibility and drains the backlog, with a cap
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

THE CAPABILITY THIS WHOLE EPIC EXISTS FOR: a maintainer flips actions.pipelines: true and the next patrol processes the backlog gonk already saw and ignored. Today a config change only affects events that arrive afterwards.

Per open bead: re-read the project's CURRENT config; category off -> ineligible (RETAINED, not deleted -- that retention IS the backlog); already satisfied (artifact present) -> done; otherwise hand to the existing dispatch path.

THE BIG HAZARD -- BACKLOG STAMPEDE. Flipping a category on a busy project makes hundreds of beads eligible at once. The meter's budget gate is a real backstop but it is a SPEND gate, not a CONCURRENCY gate. This needs an explicit per-pass dispatch cap AND an operator-visible count of what a config change is about to unlock. Silent bulk dispatch is how the cluster wedged on 2026-08-03. Any cap that drops work must SAY what it dropped -- a silent truncation reads as 'processed everything'.

ACCEPTANCE: turn a category off, deliver events, turn it back on -> the patrol processes the backlog, reports how many items it is about to process, and honours the cap across passes rather than dropping the remainder.
notes:
OD-3 RESOLVED (owner, 2026-08-10): config resolution is PER SOURCE TYPE. There is no universal answer and the design should stop looking for one.

- Repo-backed sources (GitLab today, GitHub -- which has an equivalent per-project config file) keep .gonk.yml, layered under the instance backstop exactly as now.
- Sources with no repo (Alertmanager, Jira) are configured by an INSTANCE-SCOPED ConfigMap -- the pattern already used for GitLab backstops.

So Config(anchor) -> effective eligibility config joins Ingest/Resolve on the source-adapter seam.

PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN-TREE, nothing to invent: gonk-operator-config is 'groups: {} / instance: {budget, enabled, ladder}' -- an instance -> groups -> project tightening chain, with groups already present and currently unused. Non-repo sources extend the same idea with a per-source-type section.

THAT SECTION MUST BE SCOPED, not one global block: otherwise Alertmanager is all-or-nothing across every service and you cannot enable it for one and not another. groups: {} is the existing shape for that scoping.

CONSENT MODEL DIFFERS, name it in the implementation: on GitLab a maintainer opts in by COMMITTING .gonk.yml -- consent lives in the repo, expressed by someone with write access, and the instance can only set a ceiling the project tightens. A non-repo source has no such artifact; the operator turns it on centrally and is the ONLY authority, with no tightening layer beneath. Legitimate for infrastructure alerts, but it means 'enabled' in the instance ConfigMap is the whole decision to spend, so it must read as a deliberate operator action and never a default.

title: Source beads 3: patrol closes beads whose external object resolved
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

A reconciler over source beads: startup pass plus periodic, mirroring Reconciler.Loop's startup ladder (runStartupLadder, gonk-fan) so a restart converges promptly instead of one interval later.

Ask the source for each open bead's current state and close what is done: issue closed, pipeline green, MR merged, job superseded by a newer run on the same ref, Prometheus alert resolved. This is what stops unbounded growth and stops gonk acting on stale work.

SOURCE SEAM: Ingest(event) -> anchor, external state; Resolve(anchor) -> open|resolved|gone. Everything else in the patrol is source-agnostic. Alertmanager is arguably the cleanest fit because it reports resolution itself.

HAZARDS: per-bead GETs do not scale -- batch (issues updated_after, pipelines by ref) and reconcile against the bead set, the shape the project reconciler already uses. And resolution must NOT yank a live session; let teardown finish.

ACCEPTANCE: close an issue externally -> the patrol closes the bead and does not dispatch it.

title: Source beads 2: record the event at RECEIPT, before any gate
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

Intake must find-or-create the source bead on the anchor BEFORE Gate 1, stamp LastEventAt and the observed external state, then run the existing gate and write its outcome as a Disposition. beadstore.Put already upserts on the anchor so a replayed webhook converges rather than duplicating.

NEW STATES: observed, ineligible, deferred (alongside today's running/parked/done) plus resolved.

INVARIANT: the bead stays UNROUTED. beadstore.Put creates unrouted beads today (no assignee, no gc.routed_to); scale_check sizes pools from routed beads and the 2026-08-03 wedge was stale routed beads generating permanent pool demand (gonk-p2e). A bead per received event, if routed, reproduces that at much larger scale.

OD-2 BLOCKS THIS -- who writes it. (a) intake writes directly: preferred, because anything order-mediated is lost in exactly the outage windows this exists to survive; costs intake store access, widening a deliberately narrow credential surface. (b) intake fires a gonk-observe exec order: cheap credential-wise but depends on the supervisor ticking, and it demonstrably skips ticks under FS pressure (supervisor.fs_pressure.skipped_tick, observed 2026-08-10). (c) fold into dispatch: simplest and useless, since it does not survive the drop it exists to record.

ACCEPTANCE: file an issue while the project is deliberately key-missing -- a source bead exists, state=deferred, reason recorded. Restart the controller mid-flight: no duplicate, no loss.
notes:
OD-2 RESOLVED (owner, 2026-08-10): INTAKE CREATES THE BEAD. Create it as soon as we see the work; another process may amend it afterwards, which beadstore.Put's upsert-on-anchor already supports.

MY EARLIER OBJECTION WAS WRONG. I claimed this would widen intake's deliberately narrow credential surface. The deployment says otherwise: intake already carries GONK_GC_WRITE_KEY_FILE / GONK_GC_WRITE_KEY_ID=gonk and GONK_SUPERVISOR_URL=http://gonk-controller.gonk.svc:9443, and already builds an ed25519 Signer to fire grant-gated orders (cmd/gonk-intake/main.go:270-275). Intake is ALREADY a signed city mutator. There is no new credential to grant.

THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS MECHANICAL AND NARROW: intake is a distroless image with one binary, so it CANNOT use beadstore.BdCLI, which shells out to bd. It needs a beadstore.Store implementation that writes over the city API using the grant it already holds. That is also the better design -- intake stays distroless with no subprocess, the write travels the same signed path as everything else, and no new secret is mounted.

REJECTED: a gonk-observe exec order (depends on the supervisor ticking, and it demonstrably skips ticks under FS pressure -- supervisor.fs_pressure.skipped_tick, observed live 2026-08-10 -- so it is lost in exactly the windows this exists to survive); folding into dispatch (does not survive the drop it exists to record).

FAILURE MODE: if the source-bead write fails, FAIL THE WEBHOOK (non-2xx) instead of today's 200-and-drop, so GitLab retries and the forge is the durable queue. Bound it -- GitLab disables a hook after sustained failures (hook alert_status) -- but a retried delivery beats a silently discarded one, which is what lost issue !23.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: this adds a second Store implementation alongside BdCLI. They must agree on anchor semantics, so the anchor parse/format from gonk-cjb should be the shared seam rather than duplicated.

title: Source beads 1: anchor vocabulary -- source type/id, source-defined scope, object types
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

Today: gonk:{project_id}:issue:{iid} (pkg/intake/dispatch.go:199). Issues only, no source identity, so project 75 on one instance collides with project 75 on another.

New: gonk:{source_type}:{source_id}:{scope}:{object_type}:{object_id}
  gonk:gitlab:orac:75:issue:24
  gonk:github:com:anthropics/claude-code:issue:1234
  gonk:prometheus:orac:platform:alert:{fingerprint}

source_type is what KIND of source (gitlab/github/prometheus), NOT 'forge kind' -- non-forge sources are explicitly in scope. scope is SOURCE-DEFINED and must not be parsed as a numeric project id, or the first Prometheus alert breaks the format.

MIGRATION HAZARD, do not skip: the anchor is the dedupe key AND the bead title AND a label. Changing its shape orphans every existing bead -- in-flight work would be re-created under a new anchor and could be triaged twice. Either read-compat both forms for a window or run a one-time rewrite of titles+labels. Also verify bd's label length tolerates the longer form (colons are already proven fine).

ACCEPTANCE: parse+format round-trips for all five example shapes; an old-form anchor is still resolvable; a source_type gonk does not know is rejected rather than silently mis-parsed.
notes:
OD-1 RESOLVED (owner, 2026-08-10): lazy migration -- ship a version that reads the old anchor format and rewrites it to the new one on sight. No batch job, no maintenance window.

PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE OBVIOUS ONE IS WRONG. The intuition is 'one startup pass migrates the instance during upgrade'. Nearly true, and the gap is the dangerous part: BdCLI.List(state) (bd.go:219) enumerates by the STATE label gonk::<state>, and runSweep only ever calls it with StateRunning and StateParked -- so a startup pass migrates IN-FLIGHT WORK ONLY. done beads are never enumerated by anything.

done beads are exactly the ones that matter. findBeadID (bd.go:89) resolves an anchor by the label gonk-anchor:<anchor>, so a new-format lookup cannot match an old-format label. A new event on an issue whose old bead is done would MISS, create a fresh bead, and RE-RUN TRIAGE -- the exact failure this epic exists to prevent.

So the fallback goes at the LOOKUP seam, not only in enumeration:
  findBeadID(anchor): try new-format label; on miss try old-format label; on hit rewrite title + anchor label to the new form, then return.

Then startup/patrol enumeration migrates in-flight beads eagerly, a terminal bead migrates the instant it becomes relevant again (precisely when correctness depends on it), and a half-migrated store is always correct.

Preserve: idempotent rewrite (label add/remove on one bead id, so racing processes converge); the extra bd list costs only on a MISS, so steady state pays it on genuinely new objects only; removable later behind its own bead.

State labels need no migration -- observed/ineligible/deferred/resolved are additive gonk::<state> labels.

ACCEPTANCE ADDITION: a done bead in the OLD format, plus a new event for the same object, must resolve to the SAME bead and must not re-run triage.

title: EPIC: source beads -- level-triggered work intake that survives restarts
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

gonk is edge-triggered: a webhook is gated at receipt and if the gate says no the event is GONE. Every Store.Put runs inside gonk-gate dispatch, i.e. AFTER intake's Gate 1 and the meter's Gate 2 both pass; pkg/intake.Dispatch holds no store at all. Proven live 2026-08-10: issue !23 was accepted 200, dropped as state_key-missing, and left zero beads and zero city events -- unrecoverable, a human had to file a second issue.

PRINCIPLE: record the fact at receipt, decide what to do about it later and repeatedly. A source bead is a durable record that an external object exists and something happened to it -- NOT a work item. Eligibility is derived, and re-derived, from the project's current .gonk.yml and the object's current state. Same shape as pkg/intake/reconcile.go, which already reconciles PROJECTS level-triggered with a startup ladder; this applies it to WORK ITEMS.

UNLOCKS: a maintainer flipping actions.pipelines: true means the next patrol processes the backlog gonk already saw and ignored. Today that config change only affects future events.

INVARIANT, LOAD-BEARING: source beads stay UNROUTED until the patrol decides to act. beadstore.Put already creates unrouted beads (bd create --title <anchor> --labels <anchor-label>, no assignee, no gc.routed_to) and that must stay true -- Gas City's scale_check sizes pools from ready+unassigned beads by gc.routed_to, and the 2026-08-03 wedge was stale routed beads generating permanent pool demand (gonk-p2e). A bead per received event, if routed, reproduces that at much larger scale.

title: EXTERNAL: homelab/ci-templates!4 -- .manifest-merge cannot detect a single-arch image
description:
SOURCE BEAD for an external work item. The work lives in another repo and is NOT ours to merge; this bead exists so gonk can see and depend on it.

WHERE: https://gitlab.orac.local/homelab/ci-templates/-/merge_requests/4
BRANCH: fix/manifest-merge-detects-single-arch (commit 5f94ff3)
STATE: open, awaiting owner review. Per the gitops-repo convention, homelab/ci-templates takes an MR + review because it is SHARED across projects -- blast radius across repos, not production-vs-not. I author, the owner reviews and merges.

WHAT IT FIXES: crane digest --platform does not filter when handed a single-platform manifest -- it returns that manifest's own digest for EVERY platform asked, exit 0. So .manifest-merge's verification printed 'ok linux/arm64' and 'OK: publishes as indexes over [amd64 arm64]' for an amd64-only image. The one job whose purpose is proving an image is multi-arch could not tell multi-arch from single-arch. That is how gonk-n50 stayed green through six days of total outage.

THE CHANGE: three assertions instead of one -- the tag IS an index (grep -F on the OCI index / docker manifest-list media type), every platform resolves, and each child differs from the index digest AND from every other platform's child. Plus tests/verify-manifest-merge.sh, which extracts the real block out of kaniko.yml and drives it against a stub crane; against the OLD block, single_arch/docker_single/dup_child all exit 0.

WHY GONK CARES, TWICE OVER:
1. gonk consumes this template at ref: main (see gonk-j6b), so the change reaches gonk's next pipeline the moment it merges -- unreviewed-by-us, by construction.
2. Until it merges, gonk's own *-index jobs are verified by the broken check. Every gonk release is currently taking my out-of-band verifier's word for it, not CI's.

REVIEW NOTES RAISED IN THE MR: it is a behaviour change (a consumer whose tags are already single-arch now goes red -- that is the point, but it may surface elsewhere; only four projects include this template); it adds a retroactive [0.2.2] CHANGELOG entry that can be dropped; and tests/ is a new directory in a repo that had none.

WHEN IT MERGES: tag v0.2.3, then pin gonk to it (gonk-j6b) and close both.
notes:
MERGED by the owner 2026-08-11 (confirmed: MR !4 state=merged).

Consequence for gonk, immediately: gonk includes this template at ref: main (gonk-j6b), so gonk's NEXT pipeline is verified by the fixed three-assertion check. The gap where every gonk release rested on my out-of-band verifier instead of CI is closed for new builds.

The last release verified the old way was v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55, now deployed -- I verified those four images independently with verify-indexes.sh before rolling them (gonk-c9i), so nothing shipped on the broken check's word.

REMAINING: no v0.2.3 tag exists yet. The plan on this bead was tag v0.2.3, then pin gonk to it (gonk-j6b). Tag is unpinned-inert -- consumers at ref: main already have the change -- so gonk-j6b is the real remaining work and now unblocked apart from needing that tag cut.
close_reason: Closed

title: ParsePrivateKey's trim fallback eats key bytes: ~4.6% of ed25519 write keys fail to load
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 while running the full suite for gonk-6a6: pkg/gcapi TestParsePrivateKeyStillTrimsTextFiles failed with 'raw length 63'. It is FLAKY, ~1 run in 22, which is why it had been passing.

An earlier fix made exact-length input verbatim to stop bytes.TrimSpace corrupting raw keys, and its comment says so. But the trim fallback it left behind has the identical bug one layer down. A key delivered as TEXT -- which is exactly how the gc write key arrives, a Helm/Vault secret file with a trailing newline -- is 64+1=65 bytes, not an exact length, so it takes the TrimSpace path. TrimSpace does not stop at the newline it was aimed at: it keeps going, so a key whose LAST byte is whitespace loses that byte too, and one whose FIRST byte is whitespace loses that one. 6 whitespace values of 256, two ends, so ~4.6% of freshly minted keys.

IMPACT: a key rotation had roughly a 1-in-22 chance of producing a controller that cannot sign at all -- no session creation, no dispatch, and an error message ('raw length 63 is neither a 32-byte seed nor a 64-byte key') that points at the key file rather than at the parser.

FIX (done): try candidate readings in order -- verbatim, minus one trailing newline, minus a trailing CRLF, then TrimSpace as a last resort -- and accept the first whose length is a valid ed25519 size. Stripping may only ever produce a valid key, never eat into one.

TEST: TestParsePrivateKeyTrimNeverEatsKeyBytes, exhaustive over 2 sizes x 6 whitespace bytes x both ends x both line endings = 48 cases, deterministic. Mutation-tested: the old logic fails 48/48.
close_reason:
FIXED IN OUR CODEBASE (pkg/gcapi/writeauth.go -- gonk's own Gas City API client, not vendored upstream, so no gascity issue is needed). Commit e50ce45, built in pipeline 2020, deployed live in v0.1.0-7eb0036750e7 on 2026-08-10.

The parse now tries candidate readings in order -- verbatim, minus one trailing newline, minus a trailing CRLF, TrimSpace last -- and accepts the first whose length is a valid ed25519 size, so stripping can only ever PRODUCE a valid key and never eat into one.

TestParsePrivateKeyTrimNeverEatsKeyBytes covers 2 sizes x 6 whitespace bytes x both ends x both line endings = 48 deterministic cases (the original bug was only reachable ~1 run in 22 by chance). Mutation-tested: the previous logic fails 48/48.

title: make push can silently clobber a CI-published multi-arch index
description:
Makefile 'push' builds single-arch images (TARGETARCH ?= $(shell go env GOARCH)) and pushes them to the SAME unsuffixed tags CI publishes as OCI indexes. A by-hand push therefore replaces a correct multi-arch index with a single-arch image, and nothing re-runs to notice.

This caused gonk-n50: six days of total outage, 1593 controller restarts, with CI green throughout.

Options: (a) make 'push' refuse to write an unsuffixed tag that already resolves to an index; (b) make 'push' write only to a -$(ARCH)-suffixed or -dev tag; (c) delete the hand-push path entirely now that CI builds images reliably. (c) is probably right -- the Makefile push path exists from the era when no runner had ever run a job, and that era is over.
design: Prefer (c). If (a), the check is: crane manifest $TAG | grep -F 'application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json' -> refuse.

title: gonk-gate's stdout is discarded: exec-order logs reach no pod log, no bead, no file
description:
FOUND while diagnosing gonk-zp3, 2026-08-04.

gonk-dispatch and gonk-sweep run as Gas City EXEC ORDERS, and everything gonk-gate writes to
its structured logger goes nowhere:
- NOT in the controller pod log. `kubectl logs deploy/gonk-controller | grep "sweep:"`
  returns nothing while sweep is demonstrably running every 30s (order.fired /
  order.completed events prove it).
- NOT on the order tracking bead. go-wisp-rx6xuc (an order:gonk-dispatch tracking bead) has
  an empty description and carries only close_reason in metadata.
- NOT on disk. /city/.gc has no logs directory; runtime/ holds only packs and
  session-reconciler-trace.

So every line the last two sessions of work deliberately made LOUD is invisible in
production. That includes the ones written specifically to be seen:
  "sweep: session close failed -- ITS POD IS LEAKED"
  "reap: closed an ORPHANED session -- no bead claimed it"
  "reap: cannot read the bead store; reaping NOTHING this tick"
  "prompt delivery failed; session will idle -- re-sling will retry"
  "sweep: triage batch rejected, applied nothing"
An ERROR nobody can read is the same as no ERROR. This undercuts the whole "make the
silent failure loud" thread running through sessions 5-7: the code says it loudly and the
deployment eats it.

WHAT TO CHECK: whether Gas City captures exec-order stdout at all (an order tracking bead
field, an events payload, a configurable log sink), or whether gonk-gate must write
somewhere durable itself -- a file on the city volume, or straight to the event stream via
the API it already holds a signed client for. Writing to the city event log has the
attraction that `gc events` already aggregates it and the sweep already has the client.

Blocks gonk-zp3, and blocks any future live diagnosis of the dispatch/sweep path.
close_reason:
FIXED AND PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-10 in v0.1.0-7eb0036750e7.

Gas City runs exec orders with cmd.Stdout AND cmd.Stderr pointed at one in-memory buffer (cmd/gc/order_dispatch.go shellExecRunner at GASCITY_REF 4fda5a28) and logs it ONLY when the order fails; on success 'output' is never referenced again. gonk-sweep is built to exit 0 by design, so its every line was discarded. The channel is closed at the Gas City end and could not be fixed there.

FIX (cmd/gonk-gate/logsink.go): records go to stderr AND a durable sink, defaulting to /proc/1/fd/1 -- PID 1 in the controller container is gc and its stdout is the container log pipe. Chosen over a file on the city volume because /city is an emptyDir that nothing rotates and this namespace has already lost pods to eviction; the kubelet does rotate the container log. UNSET means enabled, not disabled (a chart that forgets it must still be readable). Sink failure degrades to stderr and never stops a run -- gonk-gate trailers runs from a git hook where a non-zero exit blocks a commit. slog.SetDefault added so the slog.Default() call sites stop being discarded too.

PROOF: kubectl -n gonk exec <controller> -- gonk-gate this-subcommand-does-not-exist emitted
  {"time":"2026-08-10T22:37:09Z","level":"ERROR","msg":"unknown subcommand",...}
and the IDENTICAL record was then read back out of kubectl logs deploy/gonk-controller.

Mutation-tested: defaulting to disabled, dropping stderr, dropping the same-file dedupe, and weakening the degradation note are each caught by cmd/gonk-gate/logsink_test.go.

Unblocks gonk-zp3.

title: [bug] Triage produces NO artifact on v0.1.0-80f906b34717: two attempts, both closed, zero comments
description:
LIVE 2026-08-04, smoke test of release v0.1.0-80f906b34717. Issue !22 on
agentic/gonk-e2e-1784441480 ("CSV export drops the final row...").

WHAT HAPPENED: the webhook fired, dispatch ran, a session was created within 10s, the
prompt was submitted successfully (request.result.session.submit ok, seq 61), the agent ran
for ~4m45s, and then the sweep judged it and closed it. TWO attempts ran (a1 s-go-dm67,
a2 s-go-7ira). ZERO notes on the issue. No labels applied.

WHAT IS NOT THE PROBLEM (all verified this run):
- session teardown: both sessions closed cleanly, zero leaked pods -- that half of the
  release works and is confirmed
- project registration: meter reports the project active with triage enabled
- prompt delivery: the submit's terminal event came back ok, which is the machinery from
  gonk-u1p.7 reporting a genuine success rather than a 202
- pod scheduling: sessions started in 3-28s, no FailedScheduling

ALSO OBSERVED, likely relevant: a SECOND dispatch fired 24s after the first and failed with
  request.failed create_failed "session alias already exists:
  \"gonk.triage.p75.i22.a2\" already belongs to go-7ira"  (seq 57)
  order.failed gonk-dispatch exit status 1 (seq 58)
So two dispatches raced for the same bead+attempt. The alias collision is the create being
correctly refused, but the race itself is worth understanding -- it burns an order run and
may be burning a ladder attempt.

THE BLOCKER ON DIAGNOSING IT, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING TO FIX: gonk-gate's stdout is not
captured ANYWHERE. gonk-dispatch and gonk-sweep are exec orders; their log lines
("sweep: bead done", "broker session created", "sweep: triage batch rejected", the whole
classification story) do not appear in the controller pod log, are not on the order tracking
bead (checked go-wisp-rx6xuc: description empty, no output metadata), and there is no
.gc/logs directory. Every structured log gonk-gate emits is being discarded, which is why
this bug cannot be diagnosed from the outside. FIX THAT FIRST -- it is a small change and it
is the difference between reading the answer and guessing at it.

NEXT STEPS once logs exist: determine whether the agent produced a batch at all (peek the
transcript before the session is closed -- note the sweep now closes it, so grab the
transcript first), and whether the sweep classified it as gate-failed, infra-failed, or
reaped past its reservation. The reservation-expiry path is a live suspect: it would judge
and close a session that was still working, and it now actually tears the pod down where
before it only logged.

Blocks gonk-712 (prove gonk end-to-end).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CHAIN ESTABLISHED LIVE 2026-08-10, on v0.1.0-7eb0036750e7 with gonk-6a6's log sink deployed. Two independent faults, both now separated.

FAULT 1 (FIXED, was blocking everything): meter could not provision the project's LiteLLM virtual key, so intake answered EVERY webhook 200 and dropped it as state_key-missing and gonk-dispatch never fired at all. Cause was updateByAlias re-sending key_alias on /key/update, which LiteLLM rejects as a duplicate of itself. Filed and fixed -- see the sibling bead and commit 49d0d7d. Immediate remediation applied by hand: deleted the orphaned LiteLLM key for alias gonk-agentic-gonk-e2e-1784441480 (its plaintext was unrecoverable, so it was dead weight blocking a fresh mint); both projects now report state=active.

FAULT 2 (THE ORIGINAL BUG, now isolated): with dispatch working again, issue !24 dispatched cleanly --
  {"msg":"broker session created","alias":"gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1","rung":"qwen3-14b","attempt":1}
and the sweep then said, in one line, what four earlier investigations could not:
  {"msg":"sweep: triage batch rejected, applied nothing","violation":"no GONK_BATCH_START/END fence in session transcript"}
  {"msg":"sweep: re-sling fired","outcome":"infra-failed","next":"retry"}
  {"msg":"sweep: session closed","session":"gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1"}

THE AGENT NEVER RECEIVES THE PROMPT. Fetching the live transcript of attempt 2 (gonk.triage.p75.i24.a2) at 10s, and again minutes later until the session ended, returns the SAME single turn every time: opencode's TUI splash screen and nothing else --
  'Ask anything... "Fix a TODO in the codebase" / Build - qwen3-14b gonk (LiteLLM) / /workspace 1.18.3'
No prompt text, no model turn, no tool call. opencode sits at an empty composer for the session's whole life, so of course there is no batch fence. The sweep's judgement is CORRECT; the artifact was never producible.

So zp3 is not an extraction, validation, shape-gate or peek-window problem -- all of those are ruled out by the violation string being 'no fence' rather than any of the others, and by applyBrokerBatch reading the transcript rather than LastOutput.

zp3 IS gonk-e9m: prompts are delivered as tmux send-keys keystrokes into opencode's TUI, and they are not landing. Note gonk-u1p.7's delivery confirmation reports SUCCESS (the submit's terminal event comes back ok), so the 202-vs-receipt machinery is working and is NOT lying -- the keystrokes are accepted by Gas City and still do not reach the composer. That makes the out-of-band prompt delivery in gonk-e9m's design the actual fix, not a nice-to-have.

SUGGEST: close zp3 as diagnosed and let gonk-e9m carry the fix, or re-scope zp3 to 'prompt never reaches opencode' and keep e9m for the security half.
CLOSING AS DIAGNOSED 2026-08-17, taking the first of the two options this bead's own notes offered. The diagnosis is complete and the fix belongs to gonk-e9m, which is where the design and the six-task plan already live. Nothing is lost by closing: the root-cause chain (meter key provisioning -> intake drops every webhook -> dispatch never fires; then, with dispatch working, the agent sits at opencode's splash screen for the session's whole life) is recorded above in full.

What this bead established that outlives it:
 - Fault 1 is FIXED in 49d0d7d (updateByAlias must not re-send key_alias on /key/update).
 - Fault 2 is gonk-e9m, not an extraction/validation/shape-gate/peek-window problem -- all four are ruled out by the violation string being 'no fence' and by applyBrokerBatch reading the transcript rather than LastOutput.
 - The sweep's judgement was CORRECT. The artifact was never producible.
 - gonk-u1p.7's delivery confirmation is NOT lying: the submit's terminal event genuinely comes back ok, and the keystrokes are still not reaching the composer. That distinction is what took four investigations to see.

BOOKKEEPING FIX MADE WHILE CLOSING: this bead's description claimed 'Blocks gonk-712' in prose, but no dependency edge ever existed -- gonk-712, the end-to-end milestone, had NO edges at all. The real edge (gonk-712 blocked by gonk-e9m) has now been created, so closing this does not orphan the milestone.

title: Deploy the teardown fixes and prove in-cluster that gonk cleans up after itself
description:
The deployed image is v0.1.0-a682e5d3e7ce, which PREDATES both gonk-xkm (sweep/dispatch
close their sessions) and gonk-4d7 (the orphan reaper). Neither has ever run in the cluster.
Until this lands, gonk still leaks a 500m/1Gi pod per dispatch on orac.

WHAT TO DO:
1. make images && make push (the tag comes from the git SHA -- never `latest`).
2. Deploy, then kick the intake reconcile: gonk-fan means every intake restart races the
   meter and nothing recovers for 10 minutes without POST /admin/reconcile on the intake
   private port.
3. Prove it with a REAL dispatch, not a probe: trigger one triage on a live issue and assert
   the session pod is GONE afterwards. `kubectl -n gonk get pods` must return only the four
   service pods once the sweep has judged the bead.
4. Prove the reaper separately: create a session with a gonk-shaped alias and no bead
   record (e.g. `gc session new triage`, then rename, or just let a dispatch fail), wait out
   reapGrace (10 minutes), and confirm the sweep closes it and logs
   "reap: closed an ORPHANED session".
5. Watch for the log line that means teardown FAILED but the run continued:
   "ITS POD IS LEAKED". It appears in three places and is deliberately ERROR level.

THE ONE ASSUMPTION STILL UNPROVEN END-TO-END: a signed close BY ALIAS over the HTTP route.
Alias resolution was verified via the CLI (which may resolve locally); the route's input doc
says "Session ID, alias, or runtime session_name" and the resolver family is shared, but the
signed HTTP path has not been exercised. It matters more than it looks: all three teardown
call sites close by alias AND treat 404 as success, so if the route did not resolve aliases,
every teardown would 404, be read as "already gone", and the whole fix would do nothing while
reporting success. Watch for "session closed" INFO lines with no corresponding pod deletion.

BEFORE TOUCHING THE CLUSTER: gonk:63:scaffold still carries one infra-failed attempt of a
max of 2. One more failure re-poisons it and it needs another manual ledger delete
(gonk-csz). Do not re-trigger scaffold as the smoke test; use triage.
notes:
DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-04. Release v0.1.0-80f906b34717 is live.
HelmRelease gonk.v73, chart 0.1.0+80f906b34717, all four services Running on the new tag,
GC_K8S_IMAGE (the per-session agent image) updated too.

THE HEADLINE RESULT: TEARDOWN WORKS IN PRODUCTION. Smoke test = issue !22 on
agentic/gonk-e2e-1784441480. Two triage sessions were created (a1 s-go-dm67, a2 s-go-7ira)
and BOTH were closed:
  seq 75  bead.closed       go-7ira
  seq 76  worker.operation  operation:"close" result:"succeeded"
          agent_name:"gonk.triage.p75.i22.a2" duration_ms:2879
fired by gonk-sweep. The namespace is back to exactly four service pods, zero sessions.
On the previous build both of those pods would still be running -- that is the leak fixed,
observed rather than argued.

AND IT RESOLVES THE ONE CAVEAT gonk-4d7 left open: the close resolved BY ALIAS
(gonk.triage.p75.i22.a2), over the signed HTTP route, in production. That was the sharpest
risk in the whole change -- all three teardown call sites close by alias and treat 404 as
success, so a route that did not resolve aliases would have made every teardown a silent
no-op. It resolves. Claim now made on evidence.

gonk-fan: kicked POST /admin/reconcile (202 {"kicked":true}). NOTE the kick logs NOTHING on
either side -- intake logs no result and meter logs no requests at all (one line, ever) --
so the 202 is another receipt that means nothing. Verified positively instead by querying
meter directly: both homelab/talos-toolkit and agentic/gonk-e2e-1784441480 are state=active
with triage enabled.

RELEASE MECHANICS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:
- `make push` is the WRONG release step. It depends on `images`, so it rebuilds before
  pushing -- and GONK_TAG is computed from git HEAD at invocation. HEAD moved between my
  build and my push (a bead commit), so it silently started building a DIFFERENT tag than
  the one staged in the gitops bump. Committing on schedule would have pointed flux at a
  tag built locally and never pushed: ImagePullBackOff across the namespace. Push the
  already-built images directly and take the tag from what is verifiably in the registry.
- THE INGRESS CANNOT CARRY THE BIG IMAGES. traefik 504s on chunked upload of the ~500MB
  agent and controller layers (the small intake/meter images go through fine, though meter
  needed one retry after a 499). Workaround: kubectl port-forward svc/gitlab-registry 5000
  in the gitlab namespace and push to localhost:5000 with --tls-verify=false, same
  repository path. The pre-existing localhost:5000 tags in the local image store show a
  previous session found the same wall.
- `podman manifest inspect` cannot verify these images: single-arch images fail with
  "Treating single images as manifest lists is not implemented" even though the manifest is
  fetched successfully. Verify with an actual pull instead.

STILL BROKEN, NOT CAUSED BY THIS RELEASE AS FAR AS CAN BE TOLD: no triage comment landed on
!22. Filed separately.
