title: Verifier step 3: the sandboxed runner (no creds, no network, caps, fresh sandbox, controller-supplied tree)
description:
Third slice of the verified change pipeline. Produces the pkg/verify.StepResult values the
verdict engine (gonk-cyr) consumes.

THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS COMPONENT IN GONK, and it deserves to be treated as hostile. It
runs attacker-influenced CODE -- a different threat model from the agent pod, which runs a
model over attacker-influenced TEXT.

  - NO CREDENTIALS. No bot PAT, no LiteLLM key. It is non-agentic and needs no model, so it
    should be the only component in gonk holding nothing at all.
  - NO NETWORK, or denylist-by-default egress. A test suite that phones home is
    exfiltration with a green tick. Today's NetworkPolicy is UNENFORCED (Flannel; Cilium
    suspended) -- this component is what makes the owner's CNI plan load-bearing rather
    than advisory, and it should not ship before that is settled.
  - HARD RESOURCE AND WALL-CLOCK CAPS, and a run that hits them is recorded infra-failed,
    never gate-failed, so a hang cannot escalate a bead onto a pricier rung.
    pkg/verify.Evidence.Incomplete is the field for this.
  - FRESH SANDBOX PER RUN, never reused across projects.

THE DEPENDENCY PROBLEM, which "no network" as first written contradicts: most real suites
resolve dependencies. The clean answer is a VENDORED TREE HANDED IN BY THE CONTROLLER,
along with a pre-warmed cache, so the verifier holds nothing and needs no network. An
allowlisted package proxy is NOT the answer -- registry requests are themselves an
exfiltration channel.

WHAT IT MUST COLLECT, and this is the part a runner built for a boolean cannot retrofit:
per-step COLLECTED / PASSED / FAILED / SKIPPED test IDs, plus a build-vs-assertion
distinction. The ids must be stable across steps 0/1/2 -- an unstable id reads to the
monotonicity rule as "deleted and replaced", i.e. it silently manufactures gate failures.
Start with one language's framework (Go's test2json is the obvious first, and it gives
collected/passed/failed/skipped honestly) rather than a generic parser.

BOUNDED RETRIES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Retrying step 2 until green launders a flake into a
pass; retrying step 1 until red launders one into a valid red. Both bounds live here, and
disagreement is reported via pkg/verify.Evidence.Nondeterministic rather than resolved by
the runner picking a winner.

VERDICT INTEGRITY, stated plainly so it is not lost: isolation stops escape and
exfiltration, it does NOT make the verdict trustworthy. The evidence is produced by a test
framework running in-process with the agent's code, and a hostile diff can fabricate
whatever this runner parses. Verifier-green is EVIDENCE FOR A HUMAN, never merge authority.

title: Verifier step 2: split-diff effect kinds and their path gates (both directions)
description:
Second slice of the verified change pipeline. Depends on pkg/verify (gonk-cyr, done).

THE EFFECT KINDS. The agent emits patch text in the batch rather than the controller
reading the rig -- consistent with the existing contract, inspectable, bounded by the batch
size cap. A change too large to express as a bounded patch is a change that wants a human.

THE PATH GATES, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE ONE THAT WAS MISSED. The original design
constrained only the test diff; review found that a CODE diff touching test files sails
straight through the sequence. Both directions are needed:
  - the test diff may write ONLY files matching the repository's declared test patterns;
  - the code diff may NOT write files matching those patterns (the symmetric gate).
Note these are DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the primary control: pkg/verify's monotonicity rule
already closes the same holes semantically. Path gates fail earlier and with a clearer
message; they are not what makes the property true.

READ THE PATTERNS FROM THE BASE COMMIT. `.agent/` is the one prefix agents may write, so a
run that rewrites its own test declarations in the same batch is a self-widening loophole.
This also applies to the test COMMAND.

MECHANICS THE DIFF-AS-EFFECT ROUTE NEEDS (from the design):
- Pin the base SHA in the batch: the verifier checks out exactly the commit the diff was
  generated against, never the branch tip, or step 0 races the repository.
- Specify the patch format (git format-patch style, rename detection on): plain unified
  diff handles renames and binaries poorly.
- Raise the per-kind size caps. The current 64 KiB/file and 256 KiB/batch in
  pkg/effects/file.go were sized for `.agent/` prose; two diffs plus effects will not fit.
  A deliberate change to make, not one to discover.
- The protected-path denylist (already shipped, commit 69b3dce) applies to BOTH diffs and
  is not weakened by either allowlist.

AND THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO GET BACKWARDS: no downstream policy may key off the DECLARED
scope or the diff's claimed classification -- only off the OBSERVED diff. Narrowing into a
privileged class ("touches only .agent/, so auto-merge") is a grant the attacker steers via
the issue body. The intent output is only ever a rejection predicate.

title: Verifier step 1: the verdict engine (test-ID sets, monotonicity, red-for-the-right-reason, outcome classes)
description:
First slice of the verified change pipeline (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-verified-change-pipeline-design.md),
which sequences the verifier FIRST and ALONE.

WHY THE VERDICT ENGINE IS THE FIRST SLICE AND NOT THE SANDBOX. The design's own
correction says the test-ID collection the monotonicity rule depends on "belongs in its
first version rather than bolted on later" -- because red->green ALONE does not make
test-weakening unreachable (review found three ways through: delete-one-add-one, a code
diff touching test files, and skips/deselection). The invariant that closes all three is
set arithmetic over collected/passed test IDs, and if the runner is built first it will be
built to report a boolean and the sets will be retrofitted. So: the pure, deterministic
verdict logic first, with the runner plugged in behind an interface.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD (all pure functions, no process execution, no containers):
- Test identity and result sets per step: collected, passed, failed, skipped.
- Step 0 gate: base must be GREEN. Not optional -- red->green is meaningless on an
  already-broken repo, and step 0 is also the honest answer for a repo gonk should not be
  writing to yet.
- Step 1 gate: RED, red in the NEW tests specifically, and by ASSERTION FAILURE rather
  than build/collection error. A test diff that does not compile is also red, and an agent
  that writes a broken test then "fixes" it in the code diff produces a perfect red->green
  trace having fixed nothing.
- Step 2 gate: GREEN.
- THE MONOTONICITY RULE, which is the whole point: tests collected AND passed at step 2
  must be a superset of those collected and passed at step 0, plus the new tests from
  step 1. Closes delete-one-add-one, code-diff-touches-tests, and skip/deselect
  SEMANTICALLY -- wherever attempted, by whichever diff.
- Outcome classes as a CLOSED set, each distinct: pass, gate-failed, flake,
  no-verifier-path, infra-failed. Two of these matter more than they look:
  * flake must never be laundered into pass by retry-until-green (nor into a valid red by
    retry-until-red at step 1) -- bound retries in BOTH directions;
  * no-verifier-path must NOT feed ladder escalation. Refactors, docs and dependency bumps
    have no red-able test by construction, so without this class every such bead
    gate-fails and the failure mode is a spend loop climbing toward cloud rungs.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS BEAD (follow-on slices, in order):
- split-diff effect kinds and their path gates (test diff limited to test patterns; code
  diff may NOT touch test-pattern files -- the symmetric gate the original note missed);
- the sandboxed runner: no credentials, no network, hard caps, fresh sandbox per run,
  controller-supplied checkout and vendored deps. It runs attacker-influenced CODE, which
  is a different threat model from the agent pod, and it is what makes the CNI plan
  load-bearing rather than advisory.

A CONSTRAINT THAT MUST NOT BE LOST: test patterns and the test command are read from the
BASE COMMIT, never from the incoming batch. `.agent/` is the one prefix agents may write,
so a run that rewrites its own test declarations in the same batch is a self-widening
loophole.

AND THE HONEST LIMIT, from the design's verdict-integrity section: isolation stops escape
and exfiltration, it does NOT make the verdict trustworthy. The evidence is produced by a
test framework running in-process with the agent's code. Verifier-green is EVIDENCE FOR A
HUMAN, not merge authority.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 (session 7), TDD, in pkg/verify. Gates green: gofmt, vet, go test ./...

Classify is a total function Evidence -> Verdict with a documented priority order, in the
style of pkg/gate and for the same reason: ANYTHING WE COULD NOT OBSERVE OUTRANKS ANYTHING
WE JUDGED. Incomplete run > nondeterminism > no suite > missing step > base > step 1 >
step 2 > monotonicity.

THE POINT OF THE PACKAGE is that it works in TEST ID SETS, not booleans. All three loopholes
review found in the original red-green claim are closed by one rule, and each has a test
named after it:
  (a) delete-one-add-one          TestMonotonicityCatchesDeleteOneAddOne
  (b) code diff deletes tests     TestMonotonicityCatchesCodeDiffDeletingTests
  (c) skip / deselect             TestMonotonicityCatchesSkippedTest
plus TestMonotonicityRequiresTheNewTestToPassAtStepTwo, which closes add-a-failing-test-
then-withdraw-it. (c) is closed for free by keeping Passed and Skipped as separate fields:
green means "nothing that RAN failed", so a skipped test is absent from Passed and the
semantic check catches it without a rule of its own.

MUTATION TESTED, because "the tests pass" is not evidence the rule is load-bearing -- this
is the security boundary of the whole design and the project has been bitten four times by
checks that were satisfied incidentally:
  - drop the base-passed half of monotonicity -> kills (a), (b), (c) and green-green
  - drop the new-tests half                   -> kills the withdraw-the-new-test case
  - count a skipped test as passed            -> kills (c) alone
Each mutation killed exactly the tests that should die, and no others. Source restored
byte-identical afterwards (verified by diff).

OUTCOME CLASSES. Six, and the boundaries are about ESCALATION, not tidiness: only
gate-failed may escalate a rung. base-broken is separate from no-verifier-path because the
causes differ (fix your repo vs this change class is unverifiable) even though neither
escalates; collapsing either into gate-failed buys an escalation out of something the agent
could not have fixed. flake and infra-failed both mean "no verdict available" and are
checked FIRST -- the flake test deliberately supplies a textbook-pass sequence, because
accepting the happy reading is precisely what laundering looks like.

An unknown Mode returns infra-failed rather than falling through to pass, so a change class
added upstream and not handled here fails loudly.

NOT DONE, unchanged from the original scope: the split-diff path gates and the sandboxed
runner. The runner plugs in behind StepResult, which describes WHAT HAPPENED and never what
it means -- so the runner cannot express a verdict and the verdict cannot depend on how the
runner was built.
close_reason: Verdict engine implemented, TDD, mutation-tested. Runner and split-diff path gates are separate follow-on slices.

title: Orphan-session reaper: close any gonk session with no live bead record (the only teardown net that actually works)
description:
Follow-up to gonk-xkm, which closed the three teardown paths gonk controls directly. This
covers the case none of them can: a dispatch process that DIES between creating the session
and reaching any close call (pod evicted, order timeout, controller restart mid-dispatch).
Such a session has no bead in StateRunning, so gonk-sweep will never look at it and never
close it. It is invisible, not merely long-lived.

WHY NOT sleep_after_idle. Established while implementing gonk-xkm and worth not
re-deriving: Gas City's idle sleep is ATTACHMENT-based, not activity-based. IdleSince is
set only from info.DetachedAt (cmd/gc/compute_awake_bridge.go:142) and the idle branch
(compute_awake_set.go:467) requires !IdleSince.IsZero(). gonk's sessions are headless and
never attach, so DetachedAt is permanently empty -- verified against the live session beads,
every leaked one carried detached_at: "". Setting sleep_after_idle on the pack agents would
be inert. It is not a safety net, it just looks like one.

`gc session prune` does not cover it either: it prunes suspended/asleep/drained sessions,
and the eleven leaked ones were all "active".

SHAPE:
1. pkg/gcapi.ListSessions -> GET /v0/city/{city}/sessions (the route exists; gcapi has no
   client for it yet).
2. A gonk-sweep pass: for every session whose alias matches gonk's own scheme
   (brokerSessionAlias -- gonk.{agent}.p{pid}[.i{iid}].a{attempt}), close it if no bead
   record in StateRunning claims it. Match on OUR alias scheme only: never close a session
   gonk did not create, and never close one whose bead is legitimately running.
3. Give it a grace window (a few minutes) so a session created seconds ago by a dispatch
   that has not yet written its record is not reaped out from under itself. That race is
   real -- the create precedes the Store.Put by the whole prompt-delivery window.

THE TEST: seed a session with no record, sweep, assert it is gone; seed one WITH a running
record, sweep, assert it survives. The second assertion is the load-bearing one -- a reaper
that is too eager kills live agents mid-turn, which is strictly worse than the leak.
notes:
LIVE VERIFICATION 2026-08-03, read-only against orac. Unit tests prove what the code says;
these are the four assumptions that could have been wrong about what the API DOES.

1. ENVELOPE SHAPE. GET /v0/city/gonk/sessions returns {total, next_cursor, partial} exactly
   as gcapi.SessionList decodes. next_cursor and partial come back as JSON null when unset,
   which Go leaves as the zero value -- no decode error.
2. ROW SHAPE. All four fields the reaper reads are present and named as assumed:
     {"id":"go-wisp-r2ph5y","alias":"triage-adhoc-aca9b114dc","state":"active",
      "created_at":"2026-08-03T16:31:07Z"}
   created_at is RFC3339, which is what the grace window parses.
3. CLOSE BY ALIAS RESOLVES. This was the sharpest risk in the whole teardown change:
   closeSession/abandonSession/runReap all close by ALIAS, and all three treat 404 as
   success. Had alias resolution not worked, every teardown would have 404'd and been read
   as "already gone" -- the fix would have done NOTHING while reporting success, which is
   precisely the bug class it was written to end. Verified: closing by the alias
   `triage-adhoc-aca9b114dc` resolved to id go-wisp-r2ph5y and closed it.
   (Caveat stated honestly: that was via the CLI, which may resolve locally rather than
   through the HTTP route. The route's own input doc says "Session ID, alias, or runtime
   session_name" and both use the same resolver family, but an end-to-end signed close by
   alias over HTTP has not been run.)
4. CLOSED SESSIONS ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE API LIST. This one nearly bit: `gc session list`
   still shows a closed session as `asleep`, which would have meant the reaper re-closed the
   same session every 30s forever. The API list -- what the reaper actually reads -- returns
   total 0. gcapitest already modelled it that way, so the fake was faithful by luck as much
   as design, and this is now checked rather than assumed.
Also incidentally confirmed: a real ad-hoc alias (`triage-adhoc-aca9b114dc`) does NOT match
gonkSessionAlias, so the "not ours" guard holds against a real name and not just invented ones.

STILL NOT DONE, and it is the honest remaining gap: THE REAPER HAS NOT RUN IN-CLUSTER. The
deployed image is v0.1.0-a682e5d3e7ce, which predates both gonk-xkm's teardown and this. A
build+deploy is needed before any claim that gonk cleans up after itself in production.
close_reason: Reaper implemented, TDD, seven mutations each killing exactly one test, and the four live API assumptions verified read-only. Deployment and an in-cluster run remain -- tracked separately.

title: Stale formula-era work beads generate permanent pool demand; nothing ever prunes them
description:
FOUND while diagnosing gonk-pev, 2026-08-03.

Gas City's default scale_check counts READY, UNASSIGNED work beads whose gc.routed_to
matches an agent template, and turns each into new-session demand. min_active_sessions = 0
does NOT suppress this -- it is only the floor.

The city store currently holds eight such beads, all created 2026-08-02 on the FORMULA path
that the broker port replaced:
  routed_to=scaffold            go-5oi, go-gjh (gonk-scaffold roots), go-aw4, go-u3w (steps)
  routed_to=control-dispatcher  go-0d9, go-h28, go-4y5, go-ykq
Their titles read "Scaffold .agent/ in " with an empty project -- they are #4668
var-substitution casualties, so even if a session claimed one it would run a prompt that
names no repository.

They will generate poolDesired=2 for scaffold and 1 for control-dispatcher FOREVER. Nothing
in gonk closes a work bead it did not finish, and the broker path that replaced the formula
path has no idea these exist.

TWO SEPARATE THINGS TO DO:
1. Clean up the eight beads now (operational, one-off).
2. Decide what owns the general case. When a trigger migrates from the formula path to the
   broker path, its in-flight formula beads become permanently unclaimable demand. Either
   the migration closes them, or the sweeper learns to recognise a routed bead with no
   corresponding gonk bead-store record and close it. The second is more durable and also
   covers beads orphaned by a failed pour.

RELATED: this is what made the e578f81 start_command fix look like it caused a regression.
It did not cause the demand; it made two-day-old demand satisfiable for the first time.
notes: Cleanup half DONE 2026-08-03: closed go-5oi, go-gjh, go-aw4, go-u3w, go-0d9, go-h28, go-4y5, go-ykq and the two orphaned step specs go-0zz, go-ea5. They had to be closed in dependency order (leaves first); bd refuses a parent while a child is open. Confirmed effect: the scaffold pool sessions drained by themselves and poolDesired went to zero. What REMAINS is item 2 -- deciding what owns the general case, so a formula-to-broker migration cannot strand unclaimable demand again. That is the actual bug; today's cleanup was operational.

title: Broker-created scaffold session never becomes running; controller also spawns scaffold POOL sessions
description:
LIVE 2026-08-03, homelab/talos-toolkit, on v0.1.0-a682e5d3e7ce.

GOOD NEWS FIRST -- the scaffold broker port works up to delivery. The broker created the session with the right alias and dispatch failed LOUDLY and precisely instead of silently:

  ERROR prompt delivery failed; session will idle -- re-sling will retry
  agent=scaffold alias=gonk.scaffold.p63.a1 bead=gonk:63:scaffold
  err=session "gonk.scaffold.p63.a1" never accepted its prompt after 40 attempts: session is not running yet

That is exactly the machinery from gonk-u1p.7 doing its job: before today this would have reported success and stranded an idle session.

THE REMAINING FAILURE: the broker-created session never reaches running within deliverPrompt's ~90s budget (40 attempts x 3s, gated on GetSessionOutput().Running).

SUSPECTED CAUSE, needs confirming. The controller is ALSO spawning scaffold POOL sessions at the same time:
  poolDesired: scaffold = 2
  scaleCheck: scaffold = 2
  session lifecycle: op=start session=s-go-zjod template=scaffold outcome=start_enqueued
  ... then outcome=stale_async_start duration=8.088s
plus pods labelled gc-session=scaffold-go-7lys and scaffold-go-aruq.

So there are up to three scaffold pods contending: two pool-spawned and one broker-created. pack/agents/scaffold/agent.toml sets min_active_sessions = 0, so poolDesired = 2 is unexpected and is the first thing to check -- did adding start_command/[env] make the agent look 'poolable' to buildDesiredState in a way it did not before? Triage has the identical block and does not do this, which is the useful comparison.

Note also 'stale_async_start' on s-go-zjod, and client-side throttling on the k8s API ('Waited before sending request ... 1.0s') while the controller polls for those pods -- so pod-start latency under contention may simply exceed the budget.

LADDER STATE: one infra-failed attempt now recorded on gonk:63:scaffold. ONE retry left before it re-poisons and needs another manual ledger delete (gonk-9nx), so diagnose before re-triggering.

NEXT STEPS: (1) work out why poolDesired=2 for an agent with min_active_sessions=0; (2) confirm whether the broker session's pod is being created at all, or queued behind the pool pods; (3) only then consider whether deliverPrompt's budget is too tight -- do NOT raise it first, the budget is not the bug if the pod is never scheduled.
notes:
--- VERIFIED 2026-08-03 (session 7). Root cause confirmed by removing it.

Closed the 8 stale formula-era work beads (+2 step specs) and the 13 leaked session pods.
Both predictions held:

1. The two scaffold POOL sessions went to `draining` the moment their driving work beads
   (go-u3w, go-aw4) closed, and their pods exited without any further intervention. That
   confirms the demand was bead-driven, not agent.toml-driven. poolDesired/scaleCheck no
   longer appear in the controller log at all.
2. Capacity reclaimed: johnny memory 98% -> 63%, orac04 91% -> 61%, venus cpu 96% -> 83%
   of requests. The control-dispatcher create-timeout-recreate loop stopped on its own.

THE PROOF (not inference): created a bare probe session from the triage template with
`gc session new`. Pod triage-adhoc-58f5c50f2a scheduled and reached Running in 18 SECONDS,
no FailedScheduling event. Same template, same image, same node pool that could not place a
pod an hour earlier. Probe closed; ns gonk is back to the four service pods and zero sessions.

So the delivery budget was never the problem, and the 40x3s loop was correct all along --
it was reporting, accurately, that a pod which could never be scheduled had not started.

This bead now waits on gonk-xkm. Reclaiming capacity by hand does not fix anything: the next
dispatch leaks another pod and this returns. Do NOT re-trigger gonk:63:scaffold (one infra
retry left) until sessions are closed automatically.
STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-17: moved out of in_progress. Nothing is actively being worked on this and it has not been touched since 2026-08-03; leaving it claimed hid that.

THE BLOCKER IS CLEARED. This bead was waiting on gonk-xkm (gonk never closes an agent session; every dispatch leaks a 500m/1Gi pod until the cluster cannot schedule), and gonk-xkm is now CLOSED -- session teardown was proven in production on v0.1.0-80f906b34717, where two triage sessions closed cleanly with zero leaked pods.

WHAT REMAINS is a re-verification, not a diagnosis: confirm a broker-created scaffold session now reaches running inside deliverPrompt's 40x3s budget, on a cluster that is no longer capacity-starved. Two preconditions before re-triggering:
 1. Deploy first. Images are still pinned at v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 (2026-08-10); the whole rig-checkout slice and the PAGER fix are committed and NOT running.
 2. gonk:63:scaffold has ONE infra retry left of max_infra_retries=2. A second failure re-poisons it and needs another manual ledger delete (gonk-9nx, still open). So this is not a cheap experiment -- prefer a fresh bead over re-triggering that one.

AND CHECK WHETHER THIS IS STILL THE RIGHT TARGET. Scaffold is on the formula path (gonk-bgx), and the local-parity roadmap's accepted revisions say to DELETE the formula machinery and port mention onto the broker rather than maintain two orchestration idioms -- carrying both is what produced the silently-dead mention trigger (gonk-ecn) and the stale-work-bead pool demand (gonk-p2e) that caused this bead's own capacity leak in the first place. If scaffold moves off formulas as part of gonk-bgx, most of this bead is absorbed by that work.

title: Classify the work BEFORE implementing it, and route non-code diagnoses to an issue instead of a diff
description:
From the GitLab Duo review (2026-07-19, written up 2026-08-02 in docs/reference/gitlab-duo-workflows.md). This is the one piece of that synthesis gonk has neither built nor designed, and it is the sharpest safety property available for the 'fix broken pipeline' action.

THE RULE, in the owner's words at the time: 'an issue that turns out to be a feature request should not result in code changes; a CI failure that looks like infrastructure should not result in infrastructure changes' -- instead they generate issues or follow-up work.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST FOR PIPELINES. An agent told to make CI green has deleting or skipping the failing test as a LOCALLY OPTIMAL move. That is not adversarial behaviour, it is what a well-meaning model does when the objective is stated that way. The red-green monotonicity check (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-verified-change-pipeline-design.md) is the backstop that catches it. Classification is what stops the perverse objective from being handed to a model in the first place: diagnose the failure, and if it is infrastructure, flake, or a dependency outage, the correct OUTPUT IS AN ISSUE, not a diff.

IT FITS THE EXISTING INVARIANT. A classifier choosing between 'produce a diff' and 'produce an issue' selects a SMALLER capability set -- it never grants one. So it is consistent with 'a model may narrow but never widen', and it does not need the escape hatch that a scope-widening classifier would.

WHAT DUO DOES, for reference: flows are YAML declaring components typed as AgentComponent (LLM) or OneOffComponent (deterministic), composed sequentially by routers. gonk has no vocabulary for 'this step is deterministic' -- it is implicit in which binary runs. Adopting the TYPED DISTINCTION is worth it; adopting LangGraph-style routers is not (gonk's flows are short, its state is on beads, its composition is a controller loop).

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE:
- Where does the classification live -- an extra agent, or a first turn of the same session? An extra session is another dispatch and another reservation; a first turn is cheaper but mixes the classifier's context with the worker's.
- What is the closed set of classes? At minimum: code-fixable / infrastructure / flake / feature-request / cannot-determine. It must be CLOSED, and 'cannot-determine' must route to a human rather than to a default.
- The classification must be recorded on the bead and be the thing that selects the agent, so the routing decision is auditable after the fact.

Blocks actions.pipelines. Should land before, not alongside, any code-writing agent.
notes:
PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02 as the triage VERDICT (gonk-aib): a closed set -- reply-only, code-change, close -- proposed by the model, validated before anything acts on it, and recorded as a gonk::verdict-* label so the routing decision is auditable in the place humans actually look. This satisfies this bead's central rule for TRIAGE: a diagnosis that is not code-fixable produces a reply or a close, never a diff, and the classifier selects a SMALLER capability set rather than granting one.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL WANTS, and I have deliberately not done:
- The PIPELINE classifier (code-fixable / infrastructure / flake / feature-request / cannot-determine) is a different axis from the triage verdict and is still unbuilt. actions.pipelines stays blocked.
- "cannot-determine must route to a human rather than to a default" is not yet expressed. The triage set has no such member; an ABSENT verdict defaults to reply-only, which is defensible because reply-only is the least-capability outcome, but it is a default and this bead asks for a route.
- The classification does not yet SELECT THE AGENT, because there is only one agent to select.

WHY THE CODE-WRITING HALF IS NOT WIRED. The code-change verdict currently routes to a maintainer (actions.features off, or policy unreadable) or labels gonk::fix-queued (features on). It does NOT dispatch a code-writing run, and that is on purpose: gonk-066 says the syntactic shape gate "must be closed before any code-writing agent ships", and this bead says it "should land before, not alongside, any code-writing agent". Wiring a diff-producing agent now would violate both. The queue label is the honest end of the built path.

title: The shape gate is syntactic; it cannot express workflow scope, and that must be closed before any code-writing agent ships
description:
Raised by the owner 2026-08-02: 'what mechanism is the broker using to validate whether the agent response is the right shape? if the agent proposes an action that doesn't fit the workflow, how would the broker be able to tell?' -- with three examples: editing files outside the scoped MR, adding an assignee who should not be added, and deleting CI jobs to turn a red pipeline green without fixing it.

WHAT THE GATE ACTUALLY IS, all four stages, all SYNTACTIC:
1. effects.ParseBatch -- JSON with DisallowUnknownFields; kind must be in knownKinds.
2. effects.Validate -- per-kind CARDINALITY from the agent's effect-shape.toml. A kind absent from the file is forbidden {0,0}. That is the whole of it: counts, nothing about content.
3. effects.ValidateTargets -- an effect naming target_iid must name an iid from the injected context.
4. effects.ValidatePaths -- canonical, relative, under .agent/, deduped, size-capped.

Nothing in that chain understands the WORK. It answers 'is this batch in-contract', never 'is this change appropriate'.

WHY THE THREE EXAMPLES ARE ALL CAUGHT TODAY -- AND WHY THAT IS NOT REASSURING. Each is blocked by CAPABILITY STARVATION, not by validation:
- CI job deletion: .gitlab-ci.yml is outside .agent/, so the path gate rejects it.
- Assignee: there IS no assignee effect kind, so ParseBatch rejects it as an unknown kind.
- Out-of-scope files: outside .agent/, path gate again.
The vocabulary is one kind with one path prefix. The gate looks strong because there is almost nothing an agent can say.

THE MOMENT A feature/bugfix AGENT EXISTS that legitimately edits src/**, all three become UNDECIDABLE by this design:
- 'only files in scope for this bug' -- the broker has no notion of scope. A path allowlist cannot express relatedness.
- 'did not delete a test to make CI green' -- a diff removing a test job is SYNTACTICALLY IDENTICAL to one removing a genuinely dead job. Distinguishing them is judgement, and spec 6.3 says no LLM judges.
- 'assignee who should not be added' -- an allowlist of project members is decidable; 'should not' is not.

WHAT ACTUALLY PROTECTS THE REPO TODAY, and it is worth being clear it is not the validator: the artifact is a MERGE REQUEST. Nothing scaffold proposes reaches the default branch without a human merging it. And actions.pipelines / actions.features are config-only -- pkg/intake/render.go says 'gonk will not touch failing pipelines. (Not implemented yet.)'. The safety property is 'the vocabulary is tiny, every word in it is bounded, and the output is reviewed'.

WHAT TO BUILD BEFORE A CODE-WRITING AGENT SHIPS (all decidable, no model in the loop):
a) A PROTECTED-PATH DENYLIST enforced for EVERY agent regardless of its shape: CI definitions (.gitlab-ci.yml, .gitlab/, .github/), .gonk.yml itself, CODEOWNERS, anything under a configured protected list. Today scaffold is safe via a per-agent ALLOWLIST (.agent/); the next agent needs a wider allowlist and that protection silently evaporates. A denylist fails in the safe direction and is the one item worth doing NOW, while there is exactly one file-writing agent to retrofit.
b) CI INTEGRITY as a first-class rule: a diff from a non-CI agent that touches a pipeline definition is refused outright. This answers the third example permanently instead of incidentally.
c) SCOPE BINDING BY CONSTRUCTION: the bead carries a declared scope (paths from the issue, or an explicit scope: in .gonk.yml) and file effects outside it are rejected. Deterministic, and it makes 'in scope' a fact the controller supplied rather than a judgement the model made.
d) ASSIGNEE/REVIEWER allowlist from project membership, never self-assign.
e) Judge the MR's PIPELINE, and verify the pipeline DEFINITION is unchanged as part of judging -- otherwise 'CI passed' is a claim the agent could have manufactured.

Blocks any features/pipelines work. Not urgent for triage or scaffold as they stand.
notes:
DESIGN NOTE WRITTEN 2026-08-02: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-verified-change-pipeline-design.md

Owner's architecture: an intent/judgment phase BEFORE the session, .agent/ steering the session turns, and a deterministic post-session assessment. The session returns a SPLIT DIFF (tests separately from code) plus non-code effects, and a NON-AGENTIC verifier applies the diffs to a checkout and runs the suite.

THE RESULT WORTH KNOWING: the red-green sequence closes this bead's own CI example by construction, not by policy.
  step 0: base                      -> must be GREEN
  step 1: base + test diff          -> must be RED (in the NEW tests specifically)
  step 2: base + test diff + code   -> must be GREEN
An agent that deletes or weakens a test to turn a pipeline green cannot produce that transition: removing a test makes step 1 GREEN, and step 1 must be red. The failure mode that could not be JUDGED becomes a state the sequence cannot REACH. Strictly stronger than the protected-path denylist, which only says 'not that file'; this says 'not that behaviour, wherever attempted'.

THE INVARIANT for the intent phase, and it is the whole of its safety: a model may only NARROW the envelope, never widen it -- its output INTERSECTS with the static envelope, never UNIONS onto it. Narrow wrongly and the run fails closed (a re-sling, no damage). Allow it to widen and the untrusted issue body chooses its own permissions.

Also settled: the intent phase does NOT pick a rung. Spec 6.3's 'no upfront complexity classification' stands -- a classifier that sets the starting rung lets whoever writes the issue text choose how much gonk spends.

ONE DISAGREEMENT RECORDED, on approve-for-merge. It is in the owner's list of non-code effects and the note argues against building it: every safety property here rests on the MR being a human review boundary, and an agent that can approve removes the only control that does not depend on a validator being complete. Even 'never approve your own' means one agent authorises another's output, and they share a failure mode -- same model, same untrusted text. The honest alternative for unattended merges is a DETERMINISTIC auto-merge policy owned by the operator in .gonk.yml (e.g. scaffold MRs touching only .agent/ with 0/1/2 green), which is a rule the operator wrote rather than a judgement an agent made.

ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCES the note adds: step 0 is not optional (without it red-green is meaningless on an already-broken repo); 'red' must be assertion failure, not a build error, and must be the NEW tests failing; the test diff needs its own path gate or production code smuggles in; flakiness must be a recorded outcome class, never a retry-until-green; and the verifier is the most dangerous component in the system -- it runs attacker-influenced CODE, so no credentials, no network, hard caps, fresh sandbox. It is what makes the CNI plan load-bearing rather than advisory.

SEQUENCING: verifier first and alone (useful by itself, needs the most hardening), then split-diff effect kinds, then red-green, then the intent phase last -- it is the only part with a model in it and is worthless until there is a scope for it to narrow.

title: A newly-onboarded project can never reach triage: scaffold gates it and scaffold is on the broken formula path
description:
FOUND LIVE 2026-08-02 while onboarding the first real project (homelab/talos-toolkit, id 63).

THE CHAIN, as designed:
  .gonk.yml merged -> intake classifies the project 'pending' because .agent/ is absent
  'pending' GATES TRIAGE: pkg/intake/dispatch.go:171 -- 'spec 5.3: triage waits for .agent/'
  intake dispatches a SCAFFOLD job to create .agent/ via a post-merge MR
  once .agent/ exists -> state 'valid' -> triage dispatches

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: the scaffold never completes, so the project is stuck at 'pending' FOREVER and no issue is ever triaged. Confirmed end to end: the owner opened issue #1 on talos-toolkit, the webhook ARRIVED and was accepted (gonk_intake_webhook_total{event="Issue Hook",outcome="accepted"} 1) and the dispatch was dropped with gonk_intake_dispatch_dropped_total{reason="state_pending"} 1.

WHY SCAFFOLD FAILS -- TWO independent upstream bugs, both already known, both on the path triage no longer uses:

1. #4668 (formula-order dispatch drops caller vars). PROVEN LIVE: the rendered scaffold task bead go-aw4 has title 'Scaffold .agent/ in ' and description 'Read repository  and populate .agent/...'. The {{project}} var is EMPTY. The formula cannot know which repo to scaffold.

2. #4891 (k8s provider never composes PromptSuffix). Scaffold pours a FORMULA -- cmd/gonk-gate/dispatch.go orderForTrigger['scaffold'] = 'gonk-scaffold' -- and agentForTrigger maps ONLY 'issue-triage'. So scaffold still delivers its prompt the way triage used to, which does not work on this backend. No scaffold session/pod was ever created.

SO: gonk-u1p.7's fix ported TRIAGE to the broker and made it work, but ONBOARDING still runs through the un-ported path. Every new project hits this. The e2e project (75) does not, because its .agent/ predates all of it.

OPTIONS:
a) UNBLOCK NOW, per project: commit .agent/ by hand (an MR, mirroring what scaffold would have opened). intake's check is only glab DirExists(AgentDir) (pkg/intake/state.go:32), so any content satisfies the gate. Cheap, per-project, does not scale.
b) PORT SCAFFOLD TO THE BROKER, the durable fix. Add 'scaffold' to agentForTrigger and give it the runBrokerDispatch treatment -- create the session directly with a unique alias, deliver the prompt via the confirmed path, and have sweep judge the MR artifact instead of a comment (cmd/gonk-gate/artifact.go already maps scaffold -> 'mr'). This sidesteps BOTH upstream bugs the same way triage did, and reuses deliverPrompt/awaitCreate unchanged. Mention-reply has the same problem and would follow.
c) Relax the spec 5.3 gate so triage does not wait for .agent/. NOT recommended without the owner: .agent/ is the durable repo context that keeps triage from guessing, and the gate is deliberate.

RECOMMEND (b), with (a) as the immediate unblock for talos-toolkit so the live triage path can be proven on a real repo now.

title: opencode fails OPEN to a built-in cloud provider when its config is unreachable
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 during the T0 spike (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-implementation.md). Not the thing being tested -- fell out of a misconfigured test run, which is exactly how this would happen in production.

WHAT HAPPENED. An opencode invocation in agent pod s-go-8oj did not receive OPENCODE_CONFIG (the tmux server it launched under did not inherit the exported env -- see finding 3 on T0). opencode did NOT fail. It silently fell back to a built-in default provider, rendered 'Build - Big Pickle OpenCode Zen' in its status bar, ANSWERED THE PROMPT CORRECTLY, and exited 0.

WHY THIS MATTERS. gonk's metering story rests on one claim: the agent pod's only route to a model is the LiteLLM virtual key, so spend is attributed and budgets are enforceable. This is a path where that is false. With no gonk credential and no LiteLLM involvement, the pod reached an external model provider and got a completion. Whatever the billing arrangement, the call was UNMETERED and UNATTRIBUTED, and gonk had no way to know it happened.

It is also a fail-OPEN, which is the opposite of the posture ADR-006 sets for every other seam in this project. The entrypoint refuses to start without a model or a LiteLLM key (images/agent/entrypoint.sh) precisely so that a misconfigured pod dies loudly instead of talking to something unexpected. opencode's own default undoes that the moment OPENCODE_CONFIG does not resolve.

RELATED, SAME ROOT: during the same spike the model ran a WebFetch against https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42 from the agent pod and it succeeded. The agent NetworkPolicy nominally forbids that; it is unenforced (Flannel implements no NetworkPolicy, Cilium suspended -- see the banner in chart/gonk/templates/networkpolicy-gonk-agent.yaml). So today there is no network backstop behind the config.

WHAT TO DO (not yet designed):
- Verify the fallback provider list and whether it can be disabled outright (opencode config / env). Preferred fix: make the agent image refuse to run opencode without a resolvable overlay, rather than trusting opencode to refuse.
- The entrypoint already renders the overlay and exports OPENCODE_CONFIG. Add a positive check that opencode ACTUALLY loaded it -- e.g. assert the resolved provider is 'gonk' before handing over -- instead of assuming the export took.
- Feeds the Cilium argument: the netpol is the backstop that would have caught this, and it is not enforced.

Filed from the T0 spike; not a blocker for the prompt-by-reference plan, but it is a P1 because it silently breaks the budget guarantee.
notes: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-30 (commit c070508). L1 enabled_providers + L2 entrypoint pre-flight + OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1. THREE-PART VERIFICATION against the real image v0.1.0-c07050847922: (1) BUG REPRODUCED -- with no config, 'opencode models' in the shipped image resolves six built-in cloud providers (opencode/big-pickle, deepseek-v4-flash-free, hy3-free, mimo-v2.5-free, nemotron-3-ultra-free, north-mini-code-free). (2) L1 PROVEN by A/B in TestAgentImageOpencodeResolvesOnlyTheGonkProvider: the test PASSES rather than skips, meaning the control genuinely listed foreign providers and the allowlist is what removed them; a vacuous pass is structurally impossible. (3) L2 PROVEN: the guard logic run in-image with no config REFUSES with exit 1 and names the leaked providers. Guard logic separately driven through all five failure modes with a stubbed opencode (only-gonk -> pass; foreign mixed in / rc!=0 / empty output / only-foreign -> all refuse). NOTABLE: the built-in list DRIFTED since the Aug bead -- 6 now vs 7 then, hy3-free is new, laguna-s-2.1-free and ling-3.0-flash-free are gone. That drift is itself the argument for an allowlist over a denylist: a denylist written in August would already be stale and silently permissive. L3 (NetworkPolicy) remains unenforced -- gonk-7oz. Unrelated pre-existing failure found in the same suite and filed as gonk-a5x (trailers test fails on a root-owned TempDir, not a code defect).
close_reason: Closed

title: Prompts are delivered as KEYSTROKES into opencode's TUI; a bang in issue text runs a shell in the agent pod
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-01, ns gonk.

Gas City delivers a session message with tmux 'send-keys -l' (internal/runtime/carrier.go), i.e. as literal keystrokes into whatever TUI is running in the pane. opencode's composer treats '!' as its SHELL-MODE trigger. So any prompt containing a bang is not asked -- it is EXECUTED.

Reproduction (session go-57b, a healthy live triage pod):
  submitted: 'Hello there, see issue !42 and reply with exactly the word GOLF and nothing else.'
  rendered:  '$ Hello there, see issue 42 and reply with exactly the word GOLF and nothing else.'
             (bang eaten, shell prompt shown)
  produced:  '/bin/sh: 1: Hello: not found'
The model never saw the message at all. Multi-line text, backticks and JSON braces were each tested separately and are FINE -- the bang alone is the trigger, anywhere in the string, not just at position 0.

This was the cause of every wedged triage session: gonk's prompt began '<!-- gonk:model:... -->' and also said 'Triage GitLab issue !18', so the entire prompt ran as a shell command, opencode created an empty session and sat on a spinner forever with no LLM request in its log.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS:

1. FUNCTIONAL (mitigated in gonk). cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go now strips '!' from the prompt before submitting (sanitizeForKeystrokeDelivery) and no longer emits the '<!--' marker lines. Verified live: issue 21 produced a real triage analysis and a well-formed GONK_BATCH_START/END fence. Lossy -- exclamation marks and GitLab '!123' MR references do not survive.

2. SECURITY (NOT fixed, and not fixable in gonk alone). The prompt embeds an UNTRUSTED GitLab issue title and body. Stripping bangs closes the observed vector, but the underlying property remains: gonk hands attacker-influenced text to a component that types it into an interactive terminal, where the receiving TUI decides what is a command. Any other input-mode trigger opencode has (or grows) is the same hole. A keystroke channel cannot be made safe by escaping at the sender.

The durable fix is to stop delivering prompts as keystrokes: give the agent its prompt out-of-band and have gonk-agent-entrypoint hand it to opencode directly. That is the same channel gonk-u1p.8 needs for attribution, so the two should be designed together.

UPSTREAM: worth reporting to Gas City that Nudge/SendKeys are a text-injection boundary for any TUI-backed provider, and to opencode that shell mode triggers on a bang anywhere in programmatically-delivered input. DRAFT BOTH, DO NOT POST -- owner reviews and posts (docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md).
design:
OUT-OF-BAND DELIVERY IS AVAILABLE IN THE PINNED BINARY. Probed opencode 1.18.3 inside the real gonk-agent image (v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55), in-cluster, 2026-08-11.

opencode ships four non-keystroke channels:
  opencode serve    headless HTTP server (--port/--hostname/--cors), warns loudly when OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is unset, so auth exists and is env-driven
  opencode run      --attach <url>, --session <id>, --continue, --fork, --format json, -m/--model, --agent, --title, message as ARGV
  opencode attach   attach a client to a running server
  opencode acp      ACP server (--cwd)

PROPOSED SHAPE. The agent pod's entrypoint execs 'opencode serve' instead of the TUI, and the prompt is delivered as an HTTP request body / argv -- never as keystrokes. Three properties this buys, each of which is a currently-open bead:

1. e9m itself: the prompt crosses as a JSON string or an argv element, so no TUI ever interprets it. The bang vector closes STRUCTURALLY, not by stripping -- sanitizeForKeystrokeDelivery and its lossy removal of '!' and GitLab !123 refs can be deleted.
2. --format json emits raw JSON events (type/sessionID/messageID/part). Triage stops depending on the model politely printing a GONK_BATCH_START/END fence into a scraped TUI transcript. Directly relevant to the sweep and to gonk-6a6.
3. --session/--continue/--fork is a real resume primitive, which is spec 11.4's NAMED RISK (ACP resume across pod recreation).

Attribution (gonk-u1p.8, gonk-m6t) rides the same channel, as this bead already predicted -- and note the metadata no longer has to travel as '<!-- gonk:meta:... -->' marker lines inside the prompt, which is what forced the marker hack in images/agent/entrypoint.sh in the first place.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS, not yet settled:
  a. Who calls the server? Either gonk-gate reaches the pod directly (needs pod IP discovery + a NetworkPolicy + --hostname 0.0.0.0 + OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD), or Gas City keeps owning delivery and we ask upstream for a non-keystroke carrier. The first removes Gas City from the payload path entirely and is the smaller blast radius for gonk; the second is the better ecosystem fix. These are not exclusive.
  b. Binding to 0.0.0.0 puts an agent-control API on the pod network. Password + NetworkPolicy is the mitigation and must be designed in, not bolted on.

VERIFIED, and what is NOT verified -- read this before building on it:
  VERIFIED: server boots and listens in the real image; 'run --attach' reaches it, creates a session, and emits structured JSON with real sessionID/messageID; the stream reaches the provider ('llm runtime selected llm.provider=gonk llm.model=qwen3-14b', agent=build).
  NOT VERIFIED: a completed model turn through opencode. Every attempt returned ONE step_start event and exited 0 with no assistant text and no error. That is filed separately -- it is not a property of out-of-band delivery, but it MUST be resolved before this design can be called proven, because an empty successful-looking turn is the same failure signature this bead already fought once.
notes:
END-TO-END PROOF 2026-08-11, real gonk-agent image v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55, in-cluster, live LiteLLM and live model.

The payload was the ACTUAL one that used to execute as a shell command -- a gonk marker line plus a GitLab bang reference:
    <!-- gonk:model:qwen3-14b -->
    Triage GitLab issue !18. Title: "Pipeline fails on arm64 nodes".
    Reply with ONLY a fence: GONK_BATCH_START ... GONK_BATCH_END

Delivered OUT-OF-BAND as an argv element to 'opencode run --format json'. Result:
    exit 0, reason=stop, tokens input=6676 output=24
    assistant text: GONK_BATCH_START\nUnable to fetch information from GitLab due to transport errors.\nGONK_BATCH_END
    shell executions: ZERO (no '/bin/sh: ... not found' anywhere)

So: the bang survived intact, nothing was executed, the model actually ran, and it emitted a WELL-FORMED GONK_BATCH fence. Under send-keys this exact text produced '/bin/sh: 1: ... not found' and an empty session that sat on a spinner forever.

(The model reporting it cannot reach GitLab is CORRECT, not a defect: the agent pod deliberately holds no forge credentials -- the broker reads the issue and posts on its behalf. What was being proven here is the delivery channel and the fence, both of which hold.)

WHAT THIS SETTLES:
 - Out-of-band delivery works against the pinned binary, with the real payload, end to end.
 - sanitizeForKeystrokeDelivery and its lossy stripping of '!' and GitLab !123 refs can go.
 - The '<!-- gonk:model/meta -->' marker hack can go: argv/JSON carries per-session values without smuggling them through prompt text, which is also the channel gonk-u1p.8 and gonk-m6t need.
 - --format json gives structured events (step_start/text/step_finish with token counts), so triage no longer depends on scraping a TUI transcript.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN:
 - Build on STANDALONE 'opencode run', NOT on serve + 'run --attach'. --attach silently drops the turn (gonk-2do) -- it emits step_start, exits 0, and never even reaches the provider.
 - Because --attach is out, the resident-pool-session shape needs rethinking: a per-bead 'opencode run' is a process per assignment, not a long-lived server. --session/--continue is the resume primitive to evaluate next (spec 11.4), and it has NOT been proven yet -- it was only exercised through the broken --attach path.
 - Headroom is thinner than it looks: the build-agent preamble alone is ~6.4K of qwen3-14b's 16384, leaving ~9.7K for issue text plus the model's own output. A large issue body could still overrun rung 1. Not the current fault, but worth a bound.
CORRECTION 2026-08-17 -- THE 'PROPOSED SHAPE' IN THE DESIGN FIELD ABOVE IS REFUTED. DO NOT BUILD IT.

The DESIGN section proposes that the agent pod's entrypoint exec 'opencode serve' and that the prompt arrive over HTTP. gonk-2do then proved, in-cluster and side by side in one pod, that a turn driven through that server is abandoned: 'opencode run --attach <url>' emits a single step_start, exits 0, and produces no assistant text, no tool call and no error on any stream. Not a display loss -- 'opencode export <sessionID>' against the server afterwards returns no assistant text either, and neither LiteLLM nor ollama ever saw a chat completion. The turn is dropped before any request reaches the provider.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PROVEN TO WORK, and it is not the same channel:
 - 'opencode --prompt <text>' (TUI, text as an ARGUMENT) -- plan T0, PASSED 2026-08-01. Bangs arrive intact, no composer '$' prefix, model answered, and a realistic multi-line triage prompt with 5 bangs, backticks and JSON braces produced a well-formed GONK_BATCH_START/END fence.
 - standalone 'opencode run <text>' -- proven in both T0 and again in gonk-2do (step_start, text, step_finish reason=stop).

So the distinction that matters is ARGUMENT vs KEYSTROKE, not serve vs TUI. The composer's shell-mode trigger is an interactive keystroke behaviour; text arriving as argv never passes the composer's key handling at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-implementation.md needs NO re-sequencing. T0 tested the argument path, not --attach, so its PASS still stands and T1-T6 land as written -- the channel first with opencode still in TUI mode via --prompt, then T5 deletes sanitizeForKeystrokeDelivery, then T6 proves it with a bang in a real issue body. 'opencode run' remains the later improvement it was always scheduled as, and 'serve' is now ruled out rather than preferred.

STILL UNPROVEN, and named as a risk in spec 11.4: --session/--continue for resume across pod recreation. Those were only ever exercised through the broken --attach, so treat them as untested rather than working.

title: Prompt delivery is silently dropped: deliverPrompt treats the async submit 202 as delivery
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-07-31. The gonk-u1p.1 workaround (deliver the prompt as a second signed call) DOES NOT WORK in production, for the same underlying reason as the original bug.

WHAT THE LIVE RUN SHOWED (issue !17, session gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1 / pod go-d3y):
- Full chain fired correctly: POST /order/gonk-dispatch/run 202, POST /sessions 202, POST /session/gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1/submit 202.
- opencode STILL sits at its idle splash. No message, no typed text, nothing.

WHY (gascity @ 4fda5a28, internal/runtime/k8s/provider.go:535):

    func (p *Provider) Nudge(name string, content []runtime.ContentBlock) error {
        _ = p.carrier().Nudge(context.Background(), name, content) // best-effort
        return nil
    }

The carrier's error is DISCARDED and nil is returned unconditionally. SendKeys (line 541) does the same. So when delivery into the pod's tmux session fails, the session Manager sees success, the API answers 202, and the caller is told the message landed. There is no way for gonk -- or any client -- to detect the drop.

So BOTH prompt-delivery mechanisms are broken for k8s-backed sessions, and the second one is silent BY CONSTRUCTION:
  - create-time template_overrides.initial_message -> PromptSuffix, never composed onto the command (gonk-drf / gastownhall/gascity#4891)
  - post-create submit -> Nudge, error swallowed

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHIPPED FIX: pkg/gcapi.SubmitSession and deliverPrompt are correct and well-tested against the contract, but the contract is not honoured by this backend. The code is not wrong; it cannot work here. Do not revert it -- it is the right shape and becomes correct the moment upstream delivers -- but stop treating it as the unblock.

REMAINING OPTION, now the only viable one without an upstream fix: option (c) from gonk-u1p.1 -- carry the prompt into the pod out-of-band and have gonk-agent-entrypoint feed it to opencode directly (exec opencode --prompt "$(cat /etc/gonk/prompt)" or similar). The entrypoint is OURS, so this needs nothing from Gas City. Open question is the channel: session env is exec-order-only (GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_*), so it likely means a staged file -- note internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go DOES stage files into the pod, which is worth reading before designing this.

Also worth adding to gastownhall/gascity#4891 (or a second report): the swallowed error is arguably the more serious half, because it makes the first bug undiagnosable from the outside.
design: Do NOT 'fix' this by having gonk poll the session output to confirm the prompt arrived and resubmit -- that is a retry loop around a silent failure, and it cannot distinguish 'not delivered' from 'delivered, agent still thinking'. The delivery channel has to be one gonk can actually observe.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched triage agent visibly receives its prompt in a live k8s session, by a channel whose failure is detectable.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-01 by live experiment. The gonk-u1p.7 diagnosis was WRONG on the cause. Three things proven live against ns gonk (session go-d3y / alias gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1):

1. tmux delivery WORKS. Reproducing the carrier's exact two-step by hand --
   'tmux send-keys -t main -l <text>' then 'tmux send-keys -t main Enter' --
   typed into the running opencode TUI and the model answered (PONG, 5.3s over
   LiteLLM). Provider.Nudge swallowing the carrier error is real, but it was
   NOT the failure: the carrier does not fail.

2. SubmitSession WORKS. A probe making the EXACT signed POST
   /v0/city/gonk/session/{alias}/submit that cmd/gonk-gate makes delivered the
   prompt: event request.result.session.submit ok=true session_id=go-d3y
   queued=false, and opencode answered (ALPHA, 498ms). The shipped fix is not
   merely 'correct against the contract' -- it is the unblock.

3. THE ACTUAL BUG IS GONK-SIDE. POST .../submit is fully async: the handler
   returns 202 BEFORE resolving the session, so a submit to a session that does
   not exist yet is answered 202, NOT 404. Proven: submitting to
   gonk.triage.p99.i999.a1 returned 202 and then emitted
     type=request.failed operation=session.submit error_code=resolve_failed
     error_message='session not found: gonk.triage.p99.i999.a1'
   deliverPrompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go) retries ONLY on 404. That
   route never 404s, so the very first submit 'succeeds', dispatch records
   StateRunning, and the prompt is silently dropped whenever the async create
   has not materialized the session yet (a live run took ~31s create->start).
   pkg/gcapi/gcapitest modelled a 404 window that upstream does not have, which
   is why the round-trip test could not catch this.

DETECTION EXISTS. The 202 body carries request_id + event_cursor precisely so
the caller can correlate. GET /v0/city/{city}/events (unsigned, supports
index=<cursor>&wait=30s long-poll) carries the terminal event:
  success: type=request.result.session.submit, payload.request_id
  failure: type=request.failed, payload.{request_id,operation,error_code,error_message}
So the acceptance criterion on this bead is satisfiable without option (c) and
without anything from upstream.

Option (c) (out-of-band prompt file + entrypoint) is NOT needed. Also ruled out
while investigating: session-create 'options' cannot carry the prompt --
ProviderOption is type 'select' only and ResolveExplicitOptions rejects any
value not in the declared choices; and staging (internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go)
is skipped entirely because gonk runs GC_K8S_PREBAKED=true.
close_reason: Closed

title: Declining to judge a running session must not mean waiting forever (reservation is the deadline)
description:
Regression I introduced in the gonk-u1p.2/.5 fix, found on the live cluster within minutes of deploying it.

sweepRunning returned EARLY for a still-running broker session -- before gate.Signals.ReservationExpired was even computed. So a session that never finishes is never reaped: it holds its reservation to TTL and the bead sits in StateRunning permanently with no outcome ever reported.

That is not hypothetical. Session gonk.triage.p75.i16.a2 was created by the PREVIOUS controller image (365518e, which predates the prompt-delivery fix), so its agent never got a prompt and sits at opencode's idle splash. The new sweep correctly declines to judge it -- and would have waited on it forever.

FIX: compute the reservation deadline BEFORE the still-running check. A running session inside its reservation is left alone (correct); a running session PAST its reservation is reaped -- view stays nil so no batch is read, and ReservationExpired classifies it. Covered by TestSweepBrokerReapsARunningSessionPastItsReservation.
acceptance_criteria: A broker session still running past ReservationExpiresAt is classified exactly once rather than waited on indefinitely.

title: Nothing ever stamps SessionEndedAt, so sweep skips every broker bead forever
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while fixing gonk-u1p.2. This is a HARD BLOCKER on the whole triage slice and is independent of the prompt fix.

sweepRunning (cmd/gonk-gate/sweep.go:117) opens with:
    if rec.SessionEndedAt.IsZero() { return }
and NOTHING IN THE TREE EVER SETS SessionEndedAt. grep for an assignment finds exactly one hit -- sweep.go:233, which CLEARS it to the zero value on a re-sling. The field's own doc comment in pkg/beadstore/store.go:66 says it is 'stamped by whatever observes the session finish (Gas City's tracking-id lifecycle, out of this plan's available facts)'. That observer was never built.

CONSEQUENCE: every broker bead sits in StateRunning with a zero SessionEndedAt, so sweepRunning returns on the first line, every 30s, forever. The batch is never read, no outcome is ever reported, no comment is ever posted, and the reservation is left to expire. Tests pass because their fixtures (baseRunningRecord) hand-stamp SessionEndedAt -- the one thing production never does.

This is the third defect in the same untested seam, after gonk-u1p.1 (prompt never delivered) and gonk-u1p.2 (an in-flight session judged as failed). All three are invisible to any test that stubs the session's output instead of modelling its LIFECYCLE, which is what gonk-u1p.4 is for.

FIX (proposed, unifies with gonk-u1p.2): the broker path already fetches the live SessionView, which carries Running/State. That IS the finish signal, and it is more truthful than a field we would have to remember to stamp. For a broker bead (agentForTrigger[trigger] && SessionID != ''), skip the SessionEndedAt precondition and let the live view decide: still running -> ArtifactUnknown, nothing to judge; not running -> read and judge the batch. Stamp SessionEndedAt at that moment so the existing spend-staleness logic (gatherSpend compares cost.AsOf against it) still has its timestamp.

Upstream also emits events.SessionStopped, so a push-based observer is possible later; the live-view read needs no new infrastructure and no event plumbing.
design: Do NOT fix this by stamping SessionEndedAt at dispatch time -- that would make every bead immediately eligible and re-introduce gonk-u1p.2 from the other direction. The stamp must mean 'we observed it finish'. Keep the SessionEndedAt guard for the v1/non-broker path, which has no session view to consult.
acceptance_criteria: A broker bead created by dispatch is picked up by a later sweep with no hand-stamped SessionEndedAt, judged only once its session is no longer running, and its batch applied exactly once.
close_reason: Fixed together with gonk-u1p.2, since both are the same 'is the session done' seam. The broker path no longer gates on SessionEndedAt (which nothing ever stamped); it reads the live session view instead, and stamps SessionEndedAt at the moment it OBSERVES the finish so gatherSpend's staleness comparison still works. The v1/non-broker path keeps the old guard -- it has no session view to consult. Mutation-tested: re-applying the guard to broker beads fails TestSweepBrokerJudgesABeadThatWasNeverStampedEnded.

title: sweep reads the batch without checking the session finished — an in-progress agent is classified as 'no batch' and escalated
description:
Found 2026-07-31 by the owner asking whether we test the session round trip. We do not, and this is what that gap hides.

cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go:82 calls GetSessionOutput(alias, brokerPeekLines) and goes straight to extractBatch(view.LastOutput) at line 93. It NEVER consults view.Running or view.State -- both are parsed into gcapi.SessionView and both are simply unused.

gonk-sweep is a cooldown order with interval=30s. A triage session takes minutes. So the FIRST sweep after dispatch reads a session that is still mid-inference, finds no GONK_BATCH_START/END fence (the agent has not written it yet), and returns violation='no GONK_BATCH_START/END fence in session output'. That folds into gate.Signals with ArtifactPresent=false -> a gate FAILURE -> re-sling, which re-decides and escalates to a MORE EXPENSIVE rung.

In other words: as soon as prompts actually get delivered (gonk-u1p.1, just fixed), essentially EVERY triage run would be marked failed ~30s in and escalated up the ladder while the original agent is still working. It costs money and it corrupts ladder state. We have not seen it only because no agent has ever received a prompt, so no session ever did any work.

FIX: gate the batch read on the session being finished. gcapi.SessionView already carries State and Running. An unfinished session is NOT 'no artifact' -- it is 'not yet known', which must map to signals.ArtifactUnknown (uncertainty must never escalate, AD-6), not to a gate failure.

Upstream also emits real lifecycle events (events.SessionStopped -- 'session.stopped, session.crashed', internal/api/event_payloads.go:626), so reacting to a stop signal is available as a follow-up rather than polling blind. See the sibling bead on reading the transcript.
design: Minimal fix inside applyBrokerBatch: if the view says the session is still running, return a distinct not-finished outcome that the caller maps to ArtifactUnknown rather than to violation/absent. Do NOT reuse the existing 'no fence' violation string for it -- that is the bug. A timeout still needs to exist so a wedged session eventually fails, but it must be a real deadline (e.g. reservation expiry, which sweep already computes) rather than 'the first 30s tick'.
acceptance_criteria: A sweep over a still-running broker session records ArtifactUnknown and does not re-sling; a sweep after the session finishes reads and applies the batch. Both covered by a test.
close_reason: Fixed: sweep now takes the finished/not-finished decision from the LIVE SessionView (Running/State) rather than judging blind. A still-running session returns early -- no classification, no outcome reported, no re-sling -- so a mid-flight agent can no longer be escalated onto a pricier rung. Mutation-tested: removing the running check fails TestSweepBrokerDoesNotJudgeAStillRunningSession.

title: template_overrides.initial_message never reaches opencode — agent session starts idle and never finishes
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-07-31 on the first full-stack triage run (issue !16 on project 75, session s-go-nzw, alias gonk.triage.p75.i16.a1). This is exactly the C2 risk the handoff flagged as unproven: 'that template_overrides.initial_message actually reaches opencode as its first prompt'. It does NOT.

WHAT WORKS (all verified this run):
- intake accepts the Issue Hook, project resolves state=valid, gonk_intake_dispatched_total{trigger=issue-triage}=1.
- controller runs the dispatch order: POST /v0/city/gonk/order/gonk-dispatch/run 202.
- ONE signed session create: POST /v0/city/gonk/sessions 202, session s-go-nzw, template=triage, alias gonk.triage.p75.i16.a1 (the correlation marker format from the spec), outcome=success in 31.23s.
- The agent pod runs the new multi-arch image and opencode 1.18.3 comes up healthy, provider wired: the TUI header reads 'Build - qwen3-14b gonk (LiteLLM)'. Model + provider plumbing is GOOD.

WHAT FAILS:
- gc session peek go-nzw shows opencode sitting at its IDLE SPLASH ('Ask anything...') 13+ minutes in. No user message was ever delivered.
- Consequence chain: no prompt -> agent never works -> session stays state=active forever -> gonk-sweep (cooldown 30s) only classifies FINISHED sessions, so it never acts -> no batch, no comment, no labels. Issue !16 still has user_notes_count=0 and no labels.

WHY THIS IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME: the per-issue instruction AND the entire proposed-effects protocol live in the INJECTED prompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go builds the GONK_BATCH_START/END contract and the 'do not post anything yourself' rules). The pack's static pack/agents/triage/prompt.template.md is only the standing role and still carries v1 wording (gc hook --claim, post the comment yourself) -- GONK_BATCH appears nowhere in pack/. So if initial_message does not land, the agent has neither the task nor the output contract.

WHERE TO LOOK: pkg/gcapi/session.go sets Message -> template_overrides.initial_message on the create call. Either Gas City is not applying template_overrides.initial_message for kind:agent sessions, or it applies it somewhere opencode does not read as a first prompt (the k8s session provider launches opencode under tmux, so a template override may never become a TUI message). Worth checking gascity at GASCITY_REF: humaHandleSessionCreate -> template_overrides handling, and internal/runtime/k8s/pod.go's tmux launch.

ISOLATION TEST NOT YET RUN (was blocked by tooling permissions, do this first next session):
  gc session nudge go-nzw '<the broker_inject prompt>'
If the agent then emits a GONK_BATCH fence and sweep applies the comment, EVERYTHING except inject is proven and the fix is narrowly scoped to the inject mechanism. That single test splits the remaining risk cleanly.
design: Do NOT 'fix' this by giving the agent pod forge credentials or by reverting the pack prompt to v1 -- the zero-creds posture is the point of the broker slice (gonk-1t3). If template_overrides.initial_message turns out to be unusable, the fallback is gc session nudge / SubmitSession as a SECOND call after create, which costs the 'one signed POST' property from C2 but keeps the security posture.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched triage session receives its injected prompt as its first message, produces a GONK_BATCH fence in session output, and gonk-sweep applies exactly one comment plus labels to the issue.
notes: SUPERSEDED IN PRACTICE by gonk-u1p.7. The SubmitSession workaround shipped here is correct against the documented contract and well tested, but does not work on the k8s backend: Provider.Nudge swallows the delivery error and returns nil. Keep the code -- it becomes right when upstream delivers -- and track the real unblock on gonk-u1p.7 (option c: our own entrypoint feeds opencode out-of-band).
close_reason: Root-caused, reported upstream (gastownhall/gascity#4891), and worked around as far as the backend allows. The remaining work is gonk-u1p.7, which is a different mechanism -- keeping this open would double-count the same blocker.

title: Make gonk images multi-arch (TARGETARCH fetch + per-arch checksums + CI legs)
description:
Durable fix for gonk-owi: build amd64+arm64 images so a reschedule onto any of orac's 5 arm64 nodes is survivable, instead of pinning workloads to the 2 amd64 nodes.

Unblocked by homelab/ci-templates!1 (merged, main@f3241e5), which adds .kaniko-build-amd64/.kaniko-build-arm64/.manifest-merge -- rootless native per-arch builds plus a crane manifest merge.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-07-31):
- All three base pins are multi-arch OCI indexes and need no change: golang 1.26.5, distroless static-debian12, debian trixie-slim.
- meter + intake need NO Dockerfile change: CGO_ENABLED=0, -mod=vendor, distroless runtime with zero RUN steps.
- agent + controller DO need work: they apt-get in the RUNTIME stage (so must build natively per-arch, not cross-compile) and fetch arch-specific binaries.
- Every fetched dependency has an arm64 build. arm64 sha256 computed from the real artifacts:
    opencode 1.18.3 arm64  da0a631174eba380b2a1d51f9d364fa3812da433e72743c72471d4b5da59c69d
    glab 1.108.0 arm64     681031c6477dc7eb53b07a4641e2defc6795cf7ffb18ddc6cf8bdbc1211ed782
    beads 1.1.0 arm64      e64eb6f5f998c9eae3ef9ec786f5f1c907ab3ed04fe220ebf265ca9952e21b2f
    dolt 2.1.7 arm64       3edb3e5d05889f654dca548a8b6eb367551d4418ee0be5a79d94ea1c0f40ae8d
  All four existing amd64 pins were re-downloaded and still match exactly.

TWO GOTCHAS:
- opencode names its amd64 asset 'x64', not 'amd64' -- needs a mapping, not direct interpolation of TARGETARCH.
- dolt's tarball has an ARCH-SPECIFIC top-level dir (dolt-linux-arm64/bin/dolt vs dolt-linux-amd64/bin/dolt), so the tar extract path must be parameterized too.
- kaniko does NOT auto-populate TARGETARCH the way BuildKit does, so CI must pass --build-arg TARGETARCH explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: registry.orac.local/agentic/gonk-project/{gonk-meter,gonk-intake,gonk-controller,gonk-agent}:<tag> each resolve for linux/amd64 AND linux/arm64, and gonk-meter runs on an arm64 node without exec format error.
close_reason: Done and verified in production. All five gonk images publish v0.1.0-<sha> as OCI indexes over linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 (pipelines 1795, 1816 — every *-index job green, each verifying both platforms resolve via crane digest --platform). Dockerfile.agent and Dockerfile.controller select URL, checksum and extract path from TARGETARCH and fail closed on an unknown arch. Two traps handled: opencode names its x86-64 asset 'x64', and dolt's tarball has an arch-specific top-level directory. meter/intake needed no change (CGO_ENABLED=0, distroless, no RUN in the runtime stage). arm64 checksums computed from the real artifacts; all four existing amd64 pins re-verified unchanged.

title: Homelab infra: image builds + registry push + port-forward all degraded (blocks gonk deploys)
description: Observed 2026-07-28 while deploying the triage broker (gonk-dxo/C7). FOUR failure modes, all pointing at cluster egress + networking: (1) CI kaniko image jobs hang at base-image pull from the zot mirror (zot.registry-system.svc.cluster.local:5000) -> Docker Hub egress is down/blocked; every controller/agent/etc image build is stuck. (2) Local podman build of Dockerfile.controller fails in the gc stage: proxy.golang.org connection-reset / unexpected-EOF (host outbound to Google degraded), even with --network=host. (3) podman push to registry.orac.local returns HTTP 499 (Traefik Ingress client-closed on chunked large-layer upload). (4) kubectl port-forward to svc/gitlab-registry -n gitlab won't bind (hangs with no 'Forwarding from' line) -> the port-forward/exec stream path is degraded, same class as GitLab k8s runner 'Preparation failed: starting pod watcher: not synced: *v1.Pod'. FIX at: zot registry-system egress to Docker Hub; node/CNI outbound to proxy.golang.org+Docker Hub; and the kube-apiserver SPDY/websocket stream path (port-forward). Until fixed, gonk images can't be built or pushed via the normal paths. Workaround for gonk specifically (broker slice): build gonk-gate offline (vendored) and overlay onto the existing controller base image -- recipe on gonk-dxo -- but it still needs a working registry push.
notes: Tracked in the GITOPS beads repo as gitops-6598 (that is where the fix lives: zot/registry-system egress to Docker Hub, node/CNI outbound to proxy.golang.org, Traefik registry-push timeouts, and kube-apiserver stream/port-forward health).
close_reason:
RESOLVED - verified against the live cluster 2026-07-30. All four failure modes from the report are clear:
(1) CI image builds: pipeline 1753 on main SUCCESS (2026-07-30 15:21); controller/intake/meter images built at v0.1.0-a073f0d51766.
(2) Registry push/pull: those images are being pulled from registry.orac.local by the running gonk deployment.
(3) Ingress/registry 499s: images landed, no push failures.
(4) kubectl port-forward: binds cleanly ('Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:18080 -> 8080'); gonk-meter /healthz and /readyz both return 200 through it.

Additionally Flux is reconciling the chart (HelmRelease gonk READY, release gonk.v5). The underlying fix was owned by the gitops repo (gitops-6598); closing here because it no longer blocks gonk deploys. If gitops-6598 is still open on its own terms, that is the right place to track any residual work.

title: Controller lacks GONK_GITLAB_URL + marker-free token file -> broker forge calls 401
description: cfg.gl() (cmd/gonk-gate) reads GONK_GITLAB_URL + GONK_GITLAB_TOKEN_FILE, but the controller container sets NEITHER: GONK_GITLAB_URL appears only inside the bootstrap awk (injected into AGENT configs), and the bot token is exposed as GONK_BOT_FILE (marker-free) for the old formula var, not under a name cfg.gl() reads. GONK_GITLAB_TOKEN_FILE contains 'TOKEN', which Gas City's execenv.IsSensitiveKey STRIPS from exec-order (dispatch/sweep) env -- so even if set it would arrive empty. Result: cfg.gl() builds glab.New('','') -> every broker forge call (dispatch issue-context fetch, sweep comment/label apply under the bot PAT) fails, and v1 sweep's GitLab reads too. Fix: main.go GitLabTokenFile := firstNonEmpty(GONK_GITLAB_TOKEN_FILE, GONK_BOT_FILE) (reuse the marker-free file the controller already mounts), and add GONK_GITLAB_URL (marker-free) to the controller container env. Mirrors the existing GONK_METER_TOKEN_FILE/GONK_METER_BEARER_FILE fallback. Blocks C7.
close_reason: Fixed: main.go GitLabTokenFile fallback to marker-free GONK_BOT_FILE + chart adds GONK_GITLAB_URL to controller (golden regenerated, pure addition). Tests added.

description: throwaway ns. EXIT: broker posts identical comment+labels+marker with NO PAT in pod (mount absent); out-of-shape batch posts nothing; no-batch escalates local->needs-human; cloud-default denies to needs-human. Plan Task 6.1.

title: [bug] gcapi.ParsePrivateKey TrimSpace corrupts ~4.6% of raw ed25519 keys
description: ParsePrivateKey ran bytes.TrimSpace over RAW ed25519 key material. Key bytes are uniform random, so the first or last byte is an ASCII whitespace value (6 of 256) about 4.6% of the time; those bytes were trimmed and the key then failed length validation with 'raw length 63 is neither a 32-byte seed nor a 64-byte key'. In the field this is an unreproducible ~1-in-22 controller/intake startup failure whose error message points nowhere near the cause. Found because TestParsePrivateKeyRaw64 generates a fresh key per run and so trips it roughly 1 run in 22.
design: Take exact-length (32 or 64 byte) input VERBATIM; keep bytes.TrimSpace only as the fallback for text files written with a trailing newline. Two new deterministic tests cover every whitespace byte at both ends in both key lengths, plus one proving the trailing-newline text case still parses.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./pkg/gcapi/ -count=20 passes; raw keys with leading/trailing whitespace bytes round-trip byte for byte.
close_reason: Fixed in 383ada0 on feat/gonk-712-minimal-opencode-leg: exact-length input taken verbatim, TrimSpace kept only as the text-file fallback; TestParsePrivateKeyKeepsWhitespaceBytes + TestParsePrivateKeyStillTrimsTextFiles added.
