title: Meter key-provisioning: unserialized resolveProject can split-brain the virtual key under overlapping tickers
description: Found by gonk-huy review. resolveProject/resolveKeyRef/ReconcileKeys/Reresolve take no per-project lock (keyedMutex is used only in Decide). Two ticker goroutines (ReconcileKeys main.go:134 + Reresolve main.go:147) can both enter the RotateKey (delete+generate) branch for a StateKeyMissing project before either commits Active: T2's delete destroys the key T1 just minted, the sink ends up holding T1's dead token while LiteLLM's live key is T2's -> agent 401s with NO self-heal (later reresolves take the preserve path, keeping the stale sink token). Narrow window (key-missing + overlapping tickers + both pre-commit), and the missing serialization predates the gonk-huy fix, but the new working delete+generate rotate branch is what makes it destructive. FIX: serialize resolveProject per project (reuse s.locks keyedMutex), or make rotate idempotency-safe. service.go:311-341,445,1227.

title: Report LiteLLM unbounded /spend/logs OOM DoS to upstream
description:
Found while verifying gonk's attribution chain against the live LiteLLM (v1.92.0): an unbounded GET /spend/logs (no start_date) OOM-killed the proxy (2Gi, exit 137, ~90s outage). Full write-up ready to file at docs/upstream/litellm-spend-logs-unbounded-dos.md.

Owner will file it. Decision needed before filing: public GitHub issue vs security@berri.ai. That hinges on ONE unverified question -- whether a low-privilege tenant virtual key (get_spend_routes, no internal-user role) can reach the unscoped full-table path, or only master/admin can. If a tenant key can, it's a privilege-limited DoS -> security@. If only admin, it's an ops hardening bug -> public issue. The probe to settle this was not completed (transient cluster TLS timeout; owner redirected).

Not fixed upstream: identical on v1.92.0 (latest stable) and main; a bounded /spend/logs/v2 exists but the legacy endpoint was only marked [DEPRECATED] in a docstring, not bounded. Prior art: issue #14218 (closed not-planned as a feature request, not framed as DoS).

Relevance to gonk: gonk-meter polls /spend/logs, so this is also a hard requirement on our side -- always query with a bounded window, never a naked query. Recorded in docs/environment.md and to be enforced in plan 03.

title: Agent-proposed labels bypass the configured label_prefix
description:
On issue !58 the agent proposed gonk/backend, gonk/bug and gonk/paging -- with a SLASH -- while the project's .gonk.yml sets label_prefix: 'gonk::'. The broker applied them verbatim, so a project's label namespace is in practice whatever the model types, and a filter written against the configured prefix silently misses them.

Note the contrast in the same run: the labels the BROKER authored (gonk::needs-maintainer, gonk::verdict-code-change) used the configured prefix correctly. So this is specifically the agent-proposed path.

Two defensible fixes, and they differ in spirit: NORMALISE (rewrite a proposed label onto the configured prefix before applying) or REJECT (fail the batch on a label outside the namespace, which is a shape question and therefore belongs in effect-shape.toml beside the cardinality rules). Rejecting is more in keeping with the gate's design -- the broker validates rather than repairs -- but it costs a re-sling for a cosmetic mistake, so normalising may be the kinder default. Worth deciding deliberately rather than by accident.
notes:
DECISION, owner, 2026-09-06: NORMALISE, do not reject.

The owner's reasoning, which is the better framing than the one in the original description: "applying the label is out of the model's purview anyway, it's up to us to decide how to apply that label to a particular issue storage engine (e.g. GitLab, Jira, GitHub)."

So a label's SHAPE is a property of the ISSUE STORE, not a judgement the model gets to make. GitLab wants gonk::bug; Jira or GitHub would want something else entirely. That makes the namespace ours to impose, and a model typing a slash is not a violation to punish -- it is a field the model should never have had a say in. Rejecting would have cost a re-sling onto a pricier rung for a cosmetic mistake in a field we own.

IMPLEMENTED in cmd/gonk-gate/broker_label.go, applied in the label loop of broker_apply.go, three rules in order:
  1. already in the namespace  -> unchanged (never double-prefix)
  2. stem + a separator        -> replaced with the configured prefix
                                  (gonk/bug, gonk:bug, gonk-bug, Gonk/bug -> gonk::bug)
  3. anything else             -> prefix prepended, so `bug` -> `gonk::bug`
Rule 3 is what makes the guarantee total: NOTHING an agent proposes can land outside the namespace.

The prefix comes from the project's resolved policy, falling back to the shipped "gonk::" when the meter cannot answer -- NOT to "", because an empty prefix disables normalisation and a meter blip would then silently let labels escape the namespace, which is the very defect being fixed. A project that deliberately configures no prefix still gets pass-through.

title: Bailey has no headroom: choose the next model against a 93 GiB census, and prove the current one first
description:
BAILEY MEMORY CENSUS, 2026-09-06 (121.7 GiB unified, 93.3 GiB held by GPU, ~1 GiB free):

  higgs-smoke (docker, up 7 days, healthy)   18.4 GiB   NOT OURS -- do not reclaim
  vLLM Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4                 42.5 GiB   reserved at util 0.35;
                                                        real = 23.45 model + 14.24 KV
  ollama qwen3:14b                           11.0 GiB   keep-alive FOREVER; gonk's rung 1
  ollama gemma4:26b                          18.0 GiB   expiring
  ollama nomic-embed-text                     0.3 GiB   embeddings, other work

So there is NO headroom for an additional model. Anything new has to replace
something, and the only two blocks gonk owns are the vLLM reservation (42.5) and
the pinned qwen3:14b (11.0) -- about 53 GiB between them.

THE THREE CANDIDATES, from the vLLM recipes:

  Qwen3.8-27B    Inferact/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 24.6 GiB, 262K native context,
                 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder, --reasoning-parser qwen3,
                 built-in MTP draft head for speculative decoding.
                 Fits with ~18 GiB to spare against today's reservation.

  Gemma 4 12B    Multimodal (text/image/audio), --tool-call-parser gemma4 with a
                 dedicated chat template, recipe targets 40GB+ at util 0.90.
                 CAVEAT: "requires nightly build or pinned Docker image; stable
                 release lacks encoder-free 12B support" -- a real operational
                 cost on a shared box.

  Nemotron 3.5   30B-A3B BF16. The only one with a DGX SPARK GB10 recipe:
  Lightning      7,252 prefill tok/s, 93.3 decode tok/s at --gpu-memory-
                 utilization 0.7 with --mamba-cache-mode align and DSpark
                 drafting. But BF16 at 30B is memory-hungry, and the recipe
                 gives NO tool-call-parser guidance -- which is precisely the
                 thing that has bitten us twice.

THE RECOMMENDATION, AND THE ORDER MATTERS:

1. PROVE THE CURRENT STACK FIRST. Both transport bugs are now fixed
   (openclaw-e3mb finish_reason, gonk-217 dropped function.name). Gemma 4 was
   abandoned for "tool use adherence" that turns out to have been ollama_chat
   dropping the call -- verified today: gemma4-26b now returns
   finish=tool_calls with a well-formed name. Swapping models to fix a problem
   we have already fixed would repeat that exact mistake and destroy the
   evidence. Run a real agent turn on qwen3.6-35b-vllm before touching anything.

2. THEN choose on merits -- speed and diagnosis quality -- not on tool-calling
   failures, which are now a solved transport problem rather than a model
   property.

3. If a change is still wanted, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 is the strongest fit: it is
   24.6 GiB against a 42.5 GiB reservation, so it frees ~18 GiB outright; the
   context is larger; and it stays in a family whose parser behaviour we now
   understand. Note the recipe recommends qwen3_coder where we currently run
   qwen3_xml, and the parser is the layer that has failed us twice, so that
   swap deserves its own before/after streaming probe.
notes:
PARSER SWAP EVALUATED AND NOT DONE, 2026-09-06, with the reasoning so it need not be re-derived.

Both parsers ship in this vLLM (0.19.2rc1.dev134): qwen3xml_tool_parser.py and qwen3coder_tool_parser.py. Both key on <tool_call> and <function=. The difference is the PARAMETER encoding:
  qwen3_xml    <function=name>, no <parameter= handling
  qwen3_coder  <function=...> PLUS <parameter=...> tags

qwen3_coder is therefore built for the Qwen3-Coder parameter format, and the recommendation to use it comes from the QWEN3.8-27B recipe -- a recipe pairing a parser with the model it ships for. Bailey serves Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, which is paired with qwen3_xml and is WORKING END TO END: issue !58, 10 tool calls across 8 turns, trajectory satisfied, batch applied.

So the swap is an optimisation against a component that is demonstrably correct, it costs an ~8 minute model reload on SHARED inference, and it risks mis-parsing every tool call if 3.6 does not emit <parameter= tags. Declined on those grounds.

WHEN TO REVISIT: if we move to Qwen3.8-27B (see gonk-sfn), switch the parser WITH it -- the recipe pairs them deliberately, and pairing a 3.8 parser with a 3.6 model is the mismatch being avoided here.

title: Trajectory slice 2: pkg/trace verdict engine, declarative predicates, and the fifth broker gate
description:
Second slice of trajectory evaluation (gonk-y8r). Depends on the trace ingest slice, which supplies the evidence. This slice is the classifier, the declarative predicates, and the single enforcement point.

pkg/trace -- THE VERDICT ENGINE. A new package modelled directly on pkg/verify: pure, total, no LLM, no I/O, and a CLOSED Outcome set. Trace in, Verdict out. The runner (slice 1) describes WHAT HAPPENED and can never express a verdict; all interpretation lives here, so the collector cannot be rewritten into a judge. The ordering principle is inherited verbatim from pkg/gate and pkg/verify: ANYTHING WE COULD NOT OBSERVE OUTRANKS ANYTHING WE JUDGED. An ABSENT or PARTIAL trace returns its own outcome class and is NEVER read as "the agent did nothing".

THE DECLARATIVE PREDICATES live in a [trajectory] section of pack/agents/<agent>/effect-shape.toml, beside the per-kind cardinality that file already declares. That file is already the broker's answer to "what is this agent allowed to SAY"; trajectory is "what must this agent have DONE to be allowed to say it", and the two belong together. Read from the BAKED PACK (/opt/gonk/pack/agents/<agent>/), exactly as the shape is today, and NEVER from anything the agent can write -- the same self-widening loophole pkg/verify closes by reading test declarations from the base commit.

Start with the one predicate that pays for the slice, for triage:
  a reply-only or close verdict REQUIRES at least one observed read of the session's primary target.
That is the confabulation case in gonk-y8r: an agent that reads nothing and writes a plausible diagnosis passes all four existing gates because there is no artifact to verify. Keep the predicate vocabulary small and decidable -- required-tool, forbidden-tool, minimum-count -- and resist anything that needs to understand the work. If a predicate cannot be evaluated by set arithmetic over tool names, it is a judgement and does not belong here.

ENFORCEMENT is a FIFTH GATE at cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go, after ValidatePaths (currently line 251), joining ParseBatch / Validate / ValidateTargets / ValidatePaths. One call site, in the order the others already establish, so the whole gate chain stays readable in one screen.

THE INVARIANT, which is the acceptance criterion for this slice and not a stylistic preference:
  A FAILED TRAJECTORY PREDICATE REJECTS THE BATCH. IT NEVER GRANTS, AND IT NEVER ESCALATES A RUNG.
Concretely: pkg/trace's outcomes must NOT be reachable from pkg/gate.Escalates, and no downstream policy may key off a PASSING trajectory check to unlock anything -- no auto-merge, no widened path allowlist, no skipped gate. The reason is the one gonk-066 already established for the intent phase: a process assertion becomes an incentive target the moment it has consequences. "Must have run tests" is satisfiable against an empty package; "must have read the issue" is satisfiable by a read the model never used. These predicates are worth having as a floor under confabulation and worthless as a ceiling on anything.

TESTS, in the style of pkg/verify/verdict_test.go and pkg/gate/outcome_test.go: table-driven over the closed outcome set, one case per rule, plus the two that matter most -- ABSENT trace does not reject and does not escalate, and a PASSING trace grants nothing. A contract test asserting pkg/trace outcomes are disjoint from anything gate.Escalates accepts would catch the dangerous drift MECHANICALLY rather than by comment, which is the pattern gate.MayPour and intake.MayFire already use.

SEQUENCING NOTE: ship slice 1 and observe real traces before turning any predicate on. A predicate enabled on unmeasured evidence will reject honest batches, and a rejected batch on the triage path re-slings the bead.
notes:
MEASUREMENT PASS, FIRST RESULTS, 2026-09-06. The observing-only gate found a FALSE POSITIVE before it could hurt anyone, which is exactly what the staged design was for.

ISSUE !49. Trace: completeness=complete, 7 turns, 5 calls -- all glob, ZERO reads. The gate said "verdict reply-only produces no artifact, and this session read nothing" and logged WOULD REJECT.

But the agent had not confabulated. Its comment was: "I was unable to find any relevant code files in the project. Could you please provide more information about the codebase or the specific files involved in the date sorting functionality?" It CLAIMED NOTHING. Rejecting that batch would have re-slung the bead for being honest.

THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM IS REAL THOUGH, and worth separating from the predicate: internal/paging/sort.go exists and contains SortByDate at line 29 -- precisely the code for the reported bug. The agent globbed five times with language-specific patterns and never listed the directory, so it missed Go files entirely and concluded nothing relevant existed.

TWO CHANGES, both driven by that evidence:
1. require_any_read_for narrowed from ["reply-only","close"] to ["close"]. A close verdict reached without opening a single file is indefensible whatever the wording, and the predicate holds there without needing to read the comment. reply-only includes the honest "I could not find it", which is not a confabulation and must not be rejected. The test now asserts BOTH directions, so re-widening it fails CI.
2. The triage prompt now says to list the tree before searching it, and not to guess file extensions, citing !49.

ISSUE !50, same run, a different failure worth recording: its trace was HEALTHY -- 3 greps and 2 reads of paging.go, exactly the right file -- but the batch came back "unparseable batch: unexpected EOF". A truncated emit, not a bad search. It re-slung onto qwen3-6-35b, which is the vLLM rung still broken by gonk-217. Trajectory evidence is useful here in a way the note did not anticipate: it separates "the agent did the work and the emit was cut off" from "the agent never did the work", which the four syntactic gates cannot distinguish at all.

COMPLETENESS SO FAR: 3 of 3 traces complete (!48, !49, !50). No partials yet, so the predicate is not yet at risk of being decorative -- but three sessions on one rung is not a measurement, and enforcement stays off.

title: Trajectory slice 1: collect tool-call evidence at the meter, where the agent cannot write it
description:
First slice of trajectory evaluation (gonk-y8r). Produces the Trace values a pkg/trace verdict engine will consume. IT IS DELIBERATELY EVIDENCE-COLLECTION ONLY: nothing gates on it until gonk-y8r's second slice, so this can ship, be observed on real sessions, and have its false-positive rate measured before it can reject anything.

WHY THE METER AND NOT THE SESSION. The obvious source is the session's own transcript, and it is the wrong one. pack/agents/triage/agent.toml sets OPENCODE_PERMISSION to allow-all and pins XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/gonk-home/.local/share, so opencode's session storage is in a directory the agent's own shell tools can write; gonk-e9m establishes that issue text can obtain a shell in that pod. A TRACE THE AGENT CAN EDIT IS NOT EVIDENCE -- it is a field the agent fills in, and gating on it would be strictly worse than not gating at all, because it would look like a control.

LiteLLM is on the other side of that boundary. It sees every request and response server-side, the agent cannot reach it, and pkg/atags already joins its rows to project/rig/bead/session/rung/attempt. That is the same trust argument that makes pkg/gate.Signals.ModelTokens admissible today, and it is why this slice extends an ingest path that already exists rather than opening a new one.

WHAT TO COLLECT, per (bead, attempt):
  - the ordered sequence of TOOL NAMES the model requested, from the tool_calls blocks in LiteLLM's logged responses;
  - a per-tool call count, and the total assistant turn count;
  - for the reads that matter, enough ARGUMENT SHAPE to answer "did it read the target" -- normalised, and see the redaction note below;
  - whether the trace is COMPLETE, PARTIAL or ABSENT.

THE COMPLETENESS FIELD IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING HERE. It is the direct analogue of pkg/verify.Evidence.Incomplete and pkg/gate.Signals.SpendStale: "we could not observe" must be representable and must outrank every judgement built on top of it. LiteLLM logging can be off, a row can be dropped, response bodies may not be retained. A consumer that cannot tell ABSENT from "the agent did nothing" will convert our own telemetry outage into somebody's rejected batch, and later into somebody's escalation. Model it now; it cannot be retrofitted onto a consumer written against a plain list.

WHAT NOT TO STORE. Prompt and response bodies carry untrusted issue text and, on cloud rungs, leave our premises in the first place. Store TOOL NAMES AND NORMALISED ARGUMENT SHAPE, not free text: a path or an iid, canonicalised, never a raw argument blob. pkg/spend/rows.go today holds no bodies at all and that is a property worth keeping -- this slice must not turn the ledger into a transcript store.

OPEN QUESTION, and it should be settled before implementation rather than discovered: WHETHER LITELLM'S SPEND LOG RETAINS RESPONSE BODIES IN THIS DEPLOYMENT, or whether tool-call capture needs a callback/hook on the proxy instead. If it needs a proxy-side hook, that is a real cost and it belongs in this bead's estimate, not as a surprise inside it. Check internal/meter/litellm before committing to a shape.

THE UPSTREAM ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not lost: Gas City could expose tool events on the session itself, out-of-band from the pod. pkg/gcapi/transcript.go carries TranscriptTurn{Role,Text} only and has no tool events in the contract. That route is cleaner (it sees tool calls the model made THROUGH THE HARNESS, including ones that never reach an inference request) but it is an upstream ask on a dependency gonk does not control. Do the meter route first; file the upstream ask separately if the meter route proves insufficient.

AND THE HONEST LIMIT OF THE METER ROUTE: it observes what the MODEL ASKED FOR, not what the HARNESS DID. A tool call the model requested and opencode refused, retried, or truncated looks identical to one that ran. For the triage read-predicate in slice 2 that is acceptable (a model that never even asked to read the issue is the case being caught), but it must be written down, because a predicate that assumes execution will eventually be wrong about one that was denied.
notes:
SLICE 1 PROVEN END TO END, 2026-09-03 06:07, issue !48 on v0.1.0-14d9cac3597a.

The stored trace:
  gonk-75-issue-48 | attempt 1 | completeness=complete | turns=8
  [glob, glob, glob, glob,
   read /workspace/internal/paging/paging.go,
   read /workspace/internal/paging/sort.go]

AND THE POINT OF IT: the agent's comment cited TotalPages in paging.go and named the exact defect (total / pageSize truncating). The trace, collected in the proxy where the agent cannot reach it, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS it read paging.go. That is the confabulation check the design note asked for, working on real traffic: for the first time there is evidence that a diagnosis came from the code rather than from the model's imagination.

Everything else on the same run behaved: verdict code-change, actions.features off so it routed to gonk::needs-maintainer instead of proposing an MR, the broker's own gonk::verdict-code-change audit label, the mention footer, and no mid-word wrapping (the pane fix held).

Also confirmed: append semantics work on real traffic -- 8 turns and 6 calls accumulated across several reports rather than the last one replacing the rest. Glob calls carry an empty target because they had no path-shaped argument, which is the redaction rule behaving as intended rather than a gap.

ONE THING FOR SLICE 2: the target is stored ABSOLUTE, /workspace/internal/paging/paging.go, because that is what the tool was given. A predicate matching repo-relative paths (which is how an issue or a shape file would name a target) must strip the checkout prefix, or "did it read the target" will be false for every session. Normalise on the READ side in pkg/trace rather than mutating what was collected: the collected value is what actually happened, and rewriting evidence at ingest to suit today's predicate is how evidence stops being evidence.

title: Trajectory evaluation: process evidence as a rejection-only gate, and the artifact-free triage gap it closes
description:
Raised by the owner 2026-09-02 after reading Google's "The New SDLC with Vibe Coding" whitepaper, which names TRAJECTORY EVALUATION -- checking WHICH TOOLS AND SKILLS a session actually loaded and ran, rather than only what it produced -- as a validation primitive for the agentic SDLC. The question was whether it fits gonk and where.

IT FITS, AND THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY HAS THE SHAPE TWICE. gonk has two pure, LLM-free classifiers with the same signature:
  pkg/gate/outcome.go    Signals  -> Classify -> outcome   (did the artifact land? did the model answer?)
  pkg/verify/verdict.go  Evidence -> Classify -> Verdict   (did the change pass the red-green sequence?)
A trajectory check is Trace -> Classify -> Verdict: a total function over observations of what the session DID. It sits BESIDE those two, not inside either, and honours spec 6.3 (no LLM judges) without amendment.

BUT THE WHITEPAPER'S HEADLINE EXAMPLE IS THE WRONG ONE FOR GONK, and this is the finding worth keeping. "Did the feature session actually write and run tests" is exactly what pkg/verify answers, and answers STRICTLY BETTER. A trajectory assertion says THE AGENT INVOKED THE TEST TOOL. The red-green sequence proves A NEW TEST EXISTS, IT WAS RED ON BASE, GREEN AFTER THE CODE DIFF, AND NO PREVIOUSLY-PASSING TEST WAS LOST (RuleMonotonicity). One is a proxy for diligence; the other is the thing diligence was supposed to produce. This is the same argument gonk-066's notes already make against the protected-path denylist -- outcome evidence beats process evidence wherever both exist -- and it applies verbatim. Do NOT build trajectory checking to answer that question; it would add a weaker second opinion to a settled one.

THE REAL GAP IS TRIAGE, AND gonk-066 DOES NOT COVER IT. gonk-066 is about code-writing agents, where an artifact exists to verify. A reply-only triage verdict produces NO ARTIFACT AT ALL. The entire gate is four syntactic checks at cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go:231-251 -- ParseBatch, Validate (cardinality), ValidateTargets, ValidatePaths. An agent that reads nothing, fetches no linked MR, greps no code, and confabulates a plausible diagnosis emits a batch that passes all four cleanly, and NO DOWNSTREAM EXPERIMENT WILL EVER CATCH IT, because there is no change to run a suite against. That is where a trajectory predicate earns its place: this agent must have performed at least one READ of the target before commenting on it.

Two lesser wins: NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS ("never invoked a forge write", "never read outside scope") are cheaper and more direct as trace predicates than as inferences from effects; and LOOP/THRASH FORENSICS for cost, though that is diagnosis, not gating.

THE HARD PROBLEM IS PROVENANCE, and it is the reason the first slice is what it is. ANY TRACE COLLECTED INSIDE THE AGENT POD IS ATTACKER-WRITABLE. pack/agents/triage/agent.toml sets OPENCODE_PERMISSION to allow-all and pins XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/gonk-home/.local/share, so opencode's own session storage sits in a directory the agent's shell tools can write; gonk-e9m establishes the agent can obtain a shell from issue text. A TRACE THE AGENT CAN EDIT IS NOT EVIDENCE. This is the same limit pkg/verify's header states about the test framework running in-process with the agent's code, and it must be stated as loudly here.

Only two honest collection points exist:
  (1) GAS CITY, OUT-OF-BAND -- the session provider records tool events the pod cannot reach. pkg/gcapi/transcript.go today carries TranscriptTurn{Role,Text} only; no tool events are in the contract. This is an UPSTREAM ASK.
  (2) THE METER -- LiteLLM sees every request server-side, outside the pod, and pkg/atags already joins it to bead/session/rung/attempt. pkg/spend/rows.go ingests CallID plus token counts and cost, no bodies; but the tool-call blocks ARE in those responses.
Route (2) is first because it needs nothing from upstream and inherits a trust boundary that already exists.

THE INVARIANT, and without it this feature is net-negative:
  A TRAJECTORY PREDICATE MAY ONLY REJECT. IT MAY NEVER GRANT, AND IT MUST NEVER ESCALATE A RUNG.
Same invariant gonk-066 settled for the intent phase ("a model may only NARROW the envelope, never widen it") and the same one pkg/gate.Escalates guards. Any process assertion becomes an incentive target the moment it has consequences: "must have run tests" is satisfiable by running the suite against an empty package -- the exact isomorph of gonk-066's CI-deletion example. And if a MISSING trace escalates a rung, we have bought an escalation out of our own telemetry outage, which is the precise failure gate.Classify exists to prevent.

Design note: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-trajectory-evaluation-design.md

title: Triage asks the reporter for things it could read itself
description:
On issue !45 -- gonk's first successful triage -- the comment ended by asking the reporter: 'Could you provide more details on how the sorting and paging are implemented in the application?'

The human reply was the correct critique: 'it's hosted in this project, choom, you should be able to search the codebase yourself, right?'

They are right, and the capability is already there: the agent HAS the repository checked out (pkg/rig delivers the tree, and the transcript shows it globbing and reading files), and renderTriagePrompt already tells it 'Reading files is expected'. It read README.md and RIG_PROOF.md and then asked a question it could have answered by grepping. On this particular issue the repo is a nearly-empty e2e fixture so there was genuinely nothing to find -- but the model did not say that either, and on a real repo the same behaviour would be a wasted round trip.

FIX IS PROMPT-SIDE, in renderTriagePrompt: the instruction to phrase ambiguity 'as a direct question to the reporter' currently has no counterweight, so questions are the path of least resistance. Say explicitly that the working copy is present and searchable, that a question is only appropriate for things the CODE CANNOT ANSWER -- intent, priority, expected behaviour, reproduction details -- and that anything answerable by reading the repository should be answered rather than asked.

Cheap to test now that triage works end to end: file an issue against a repo with real code and see whether the comment cites files instead of asking for them.

title: Canned zero-token replies: tell people to @-mention, and say when a real reply is deferred
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-02 by experiment: a human comment on issue !45 produced no reaction at all -- no dispatch, no session, nothing in the controller log.

THE PATH IS HALF-BUILT. Everything downstream exists: pack/formulas/gonk-mention.toml, pack/orders/gonk-mention.toml, the mention agent pool, and dispatch's closed trigger map already routes 'mention-reply' -> 'gonk-mention' (cmd/gonk-gate/dispatch.go:20-28). atags declares TriggerMentionReply and accepts it as valid.

WHAT IS MISSING is the front half: NOTHING IN PRODUCTION CODE EVER SETS IT. Grepping TriggerMentionReply outside pkg/atags finds only test fixtures, and intake has no note/comment webhook handling at all -- it acts on issue events only. dispatch.go:234 says as much in passing: 'scaffold/mention are not ported yet and fall through to the formula pour.'

So this is an UNBUILT FEATURE, not a defect: the trigger map is a closed set and an unknown trigger pours nothing, which is why the comment was silently ignored rather than mishandled.

TO BUILD IT: intake needs to accept GitLab Note Hook events, decide whether the note is an @gonk mention (and ignore gonk's OWN comments, or it will reply to itself forever), resolve the issue's bead, and dispatch with trigger=mention-reply plus the discussion_id so the reply lands IN THE THREAD rather than as a new top-level comment -- the formula already expects that. The self-reply guard is the part most likely to be got wrong, and the anchor marker gonk already writes into every comment is the obvious way to recognise its own output.

Worth doing: it is the conversational surface (spec 5.5), and triage now works end to end, so the reply path is the natural next capability.
notes:
CORRECTION, 2026-09-02: my original description was WRONG and is rewritten here. I claimed the mention-reply frontend did not exist. It does, and it is complete.

WHAT I GOT WRONG AND WHY: I grepped for TriggerMentionReply, piped through head -5, and concluded from a truncated result that only test fixtures referenced it. pkg/intake/dispatch.go:139-154 handles it properly -- case ghook.KindNote, a noteable_type==Issue check, Mentions(body, botUsername), the Gate-1 gate, cls.MayMentionReply() enforcing triage.respond_to_mentions, and dispatchDecision carrying ev.Note.DiscussionID so the reply lands in the right thread. Mentions() even skips quoted lines so a reply quoting an old mention does not re-trigger. The self-reply loop guard is at the trust boundary in pkg/ghook/receiver.go:135, and NewHandler refuses a non-positive BotUserID with "the loop guard cannot be disabled". Both project webhooks have note_events=true.

So the mention path WORKS. The experiment that appeared to disprove it -- a human comment on !45 producing no reaction -- was correct behaviour: the comment contained no at-mention, so Decide returned Reason=no_mention. The bot's username is gonk (GitLab user id 49); "@gonk please look again" would have triggered it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is what the discovery failure itself demonstrates: NOBODY CAN TELL. gonk answers an issue and then goes silent forever, and a reporter replying in the thread -- exactly what a reporter naturally does -- gets nothing back, with no indication that an at-mention is the way to continue the conversation. That is a usability defect, and this bead is now about fixing it with ZERO-TOKEN canned text.

TWO CANNED MESSAGES, both deterministic and neither costing a model call:
1. A PREAMBLE/FOOTER on gonk's own comments saying that replies need an at-mention to reach it. Cheap, and it converts a dead end into a documented affordance.
2. A DEFERRED notice for when gonk knows it must act but cannot yet -- out of token budget, LLM unavailable, rung exhausted, meter parked. Rather than silence, say so. This comment must be EDITED IN PLACE as the state changes so it always reflects the latest status rather than accumulating a pile of apologies, and when the real model response arrives and passes validation it must REPLACE the canned one, so the thread ends with the answer and not the excuse.

Design constraint carried from ADR-007: these are deterministic broker output, not model output, so they need no shape gate and no ladder -- but they DO need the same bead-anchor marker gonk already writes, both so gonk recognises its own comments and so the replace step can find the note to edit.

title: Controller liveness probe is tight enough to turn a slow gc start into a crash loop
description:
HIT 2026-09-01 deploying v0.1.0-f4958b085e63. The controller went 0/1 with exit code 137 (SIGKILL) and restarted 4 times in 9 minutes; rolling back to v0.1.0-030a6c58ee2e restored it immediately (1/1, 0 restarts).

NOT A CODE REGRESSION, and that is established rather than assumed. Only four files differ between the two tags: cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go, its test, images/agent/entrypoint.sh (AGENT image), and an image test. None touch the controller's startup path. Decisively: sha256 of the gc binary is IDENTICAL in both images (9dab87d14802e593f5d5), so gascity is reproducible and unchanged, and the pack is unchanged. The only differing artifact in the controller image is gonk-gate, which gc does not invoke to bind its API -- it runs later as a cooldown exec order.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Probes are tcpSocket on port supervisor (9443): readiness initialDelay 10s / period 10s / failureThreshold 3 / timeout 1s; liveness initialDelay 15s / period 20s / failureThreshold 3 / timeout 1s. So gc has roughly 75s to bind 9443 or kubelet SIGKILLs it. The crashed container logged exactly ONE line -- the benign 'does not import required builtin pack(s) core, bd' warning, which the WORKING controller also logs -- and then died before reaching the write-auth and bind lines. A kill during startup makes the next start no faster, so it loops.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS FIRE: the deploy rolled controller, intake and meter simultaneously while an agent session pod (s-go-59o2) was running, and intake's readiness probe was also timing out at the same moment ('context deadline exceeded' on /readyz). Contention, not a defect. Note also the PREVIOUS controller had already accumulated 2 restarts in 37 minutes on the old tag, so this fragility predates the deploy -- it was simply never fatal before.

WHAT TO DO: raise the liveness initialDelaySeconds and/or failureThreshold so a slow start is not lethal, and prefer a startupProbe (which is exactly the Kubernetes primitive for 'slow to start, then normal') over a tight liveness probe. timeoutSeconds: 1 on a tcpSocket check is also thin under node contention. NOT YET PROVEN: that a quieter deploy of the same tag succeeds. That is the cheap experiment and it should be run before concluding -- redeploy v0.1.0-f4958b085e63 with no concurrent agent session and watch whether it binds.
notes: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED 2026-09-01. Redeployed the IDENTICAL tag v0.1.0-f4958b085e63 under quiet conditions (no concurrent agent session, nothing else rolling) and the controller came up 1/1 with ZERO restarts, as did intake and meter. Same image, same probes, opposite outcome -- so the earlier crash loop was contention during a simultaneous three-pod roll with an agent session running, not a defect in the build. The probe tightness is still worth fixing (a startupProbe is the right primitive for 'slow to start, then normal', and timeoutSeconds: 1 on a tcpSocket check is thin under load), but it is now a latent fragility rather than an active blocker. Downgrading urgency accordingly; the deploy is unblocked.
close_reason: Closed

title: A bead-only commit leaves a permanently-running pipeline whose resource_group wedges all later image builds
description: HIT 2026-08-30/31 and cost a day of deploy latency. MECHANISM: the image rules (.gitlab-ci.yml, the gonk_image_rules anchor) fall through to 'when: manual' for any commit that touches none of go.mod/go.sum/vendor/cmd/internal/pkg/images/pack/.gitlab-ci.yml. That is deliberate and correct for not rebuilding images (gonk-1t4/gonk-mzm). But a manual job never runs, so the PIPELINE never reaches a terminal state -- it sits 'running' forever. Pipeline 2274 (a7112b3, a bead-only commit) was still 'running' a day later with 17 image/index jobs in 'created' and lint+test long since successful. Those image jobs carry 'resource_group: gonk-images-' (.gitlab-ci.yml:183), which GitLab serializes ACROSS pipelines, so the stuck pipeline held the group and the next pipeline could not start a single job -- pipeline 2276 sat with all 19 jobs in 'created' for ~13 hours, including lint, which has no resource_group at all. FIX: cancelling 2274 and retrying 2276 released it immediately. THIS WILL RECUR: the CI comment itself records that 61 of 87 commits in a two-week window touched none of the image paths, so roughly 70% of commits leave a wedged pipeline behind. OPTIONS: (a) give the manual image jobs 'allow_failure: true' AND make the pipeline terminal without them -- they already have allow_failure, so check why the pipeline still counts as running; (b) drop the manual escape hatch and use a pipeline variable to force a build instead; (c) leave the rules alone but add a scheduled job that cancels pipelines stuck in 'running' with only manual jobs left. SEPARATE, POSSIBLY RELATED: pushes of f4958b0 and 65af416 created NO pipeline at all -- 2276 had to be created by hand via POST /projects/69/pipeline. Worth confirming whether that is the same wedge or a second fault; a push that silently produces no pipeline is exactly this project's signature failure shape.

title: Image trailers test fails on a root-owned TempDir, not a gonk-gate defect
description: TestAgentImageGonkGateTrailersSplicesACommitMessage fails on this box with 'trailers missing from the commit message'. Root cause is NOT gonk-gate. The container runs as uid 65532 while t.TempDir() creates the host dir as drwx------ root root, so the bind-mounted write is denied. Proven directly: 'echo x > /tmp/m/f' inside the image returns Permission denied and the host file is unchanged. gonk-gate exits 0 because it never reached the write, so the test fails honestly but its message points at the wrong thing and will send the next reader hunting a trailers bug. Environment-dependent; would pass under rootless podman with userns id-mapping. FIX OPTIONS: (a) podman :U mount flag, -v dir:/tmp/msg:rw,U which chowns the volume to the container user -- cleanest; (b) --userns=keep-id; (c) chmod 0777 the TempDir before mounting. Also make the failure text distinguish 'could not write' from 'wrote the wrong thing': as written it is another check whose failure message asserts a cause it never verified, the pattern the 2026-08-19 handoff names. Found while verifying gonk-ob5, NOT caused by it -- that test overrides the entrypoint, which is all ob5 changed.

title: test/images/ has NEVER run in CI: //go:build images vs a bare go test ./...
description:
FOUND while root-causing gonk-j9z 2026-08-18, and it is the reason that bug reached production.

test/images/ exists precisely to honour the house rule 'if an app runs in a container, test it in a container' -- agent_smoke_test.go and packvalidate_test.go shell out to podman against the real built image. Every file there carries //go:build images.

.gitlab-ci.yml's test job runs:
    go vet ./...
    go test ./... -race -count=1
No -tags anywhere in the file (grep count: 0). So the ENTIRE test/images/ tree has never executed in CI, and nothing says so -- the job goes green having skipped it.

WHAT IT COST. gonk-j9z shipped , a flag that does not exist. tar exited 64 on every single session, the fetch is non-fatal by design, and the WARNING went to a tmux pane opencode redrew -- so five commits of rig-checkout work sat in production for a week with every agent running on a silently EMPTY working copy, while the grant logged success on both sides. A container test would have caught it on the first run.

OPTIONS:
 1. Add an images-tagged job to CI. It needs podman and a built image, so it belongs in the image stage after the build legs, and it costs real time on johnny -- weigh against gonk-0de's build-cost work.
 2. Keep test/images/ manual but make the gap VISIBLE: have the test job print what it is skipping, so 'green' stops implying 'container behaviour verified'.
 3. Move the cheap container-shaped assertions into untagged tests that run by default. test/entrypoint/ (added with the j9z fix) is the first example: it runs the entrypoint's REAL tar flags against a real archive on the CI host, and it fails with exactly the production error.

Option 3 is not a substitute for 1 -- it cannot see the image's own binaries or filesystem -- but it is what actually runs today, and it is where any assertion that CAN be made without podman belongs.

title: Image builds do not dedupe: 182MB of new blobs to change a 3.6MB binary
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 against the live registry, comparing gonk-agent v0.1.0-4b3c7e185b55 and v0.1.0-ef59b5b921ae (crane manifest, linux/amd64).

ONLY 1 OF 10 LAYERS IS SHARED between two consecutive builds -- the debian base. Every other layer got a fresh digest, INCLUDING layers whose content is pinned and byte-identical:
  41.0 MB  apt layer      (same package list both builds)
  65.2 MB  opencode       (pinned 1.18.3, sha256-verified in the Dockerfile)
  19.5 MB  glab           (pinned version)
  52.8 MB  bd             (pinned version)
   3.6 MB  gonk-gate      (the ONLY thing that actually changed)

So each agent build writes 182 MB of new blobs to deliver a 3.6 MB change -- about 50x amplification. This reconciles exactly with gonk-1t4's measurement: 203 agent tags x ~128 MB = 26 GB. THE REGISTRY BLOAT WAS NEVER IMAGE SIZE. It is that nothing dedupes across builds, so pruning treats a symptom.

Compressed sizes for reference: gonk-agent 210.6 MB, gonk-controller 208.5 MB, gonk-meter 16.9 MB, gonk-intake 6.2 MB. Agent+controller are 95% of the bytes; intake is 6.2 MB because it uses DISTROLESS_BASE.

FIXES, in order of value:

1. PIN THE TOOLCHAIN INTO A SEPARATE BASE IMAGE. Build gonk-agent-base (debian + apt + opencode + glab + bd) only when images/versions.env changes; per-commit agent builds become FROM gonk-agent-base + one COPY of the Go binary. Drops per-commit cost from ~182 MB to ~4 MB and does NOT depend on kaniko digest stability. Same shape for the controller, whose gc and dolt are pinned to GASCITY_REF. Across all images and both arches: roughly 800 MB -> 90 MB per commit.

2. DELETE bd AND glab FROM THE AGENT IMAGE -- 72.3 MB/arch, 34% of the image. Both are provably unused: zero references in images/agent/, pack/, or entrypoint.sh (the only mention is a comment stating there is deliberately no glab auth). Spec S0 already established the agent pod has NO working bd ('no beads database found'), and the broker design stripped forge creds so glab has nothing to authenticate with. The rig checkout uses curl+tar against gonk-intake, not glab. Also a small security win: it removes a forge client from a pod whose entire design is 'holds no forge access' (cf gonk-7oz).

3. TRY kaniko --reproducible. It zeroes timestamps, which is the likeliest reason pinned layers re-hash. One flag, might recover dedupe with no restructuring. CAVEAT: it rewrites the whole tar and is memory-hungry, and memory contention on johnny is already why builds are serialized by resource_group -- measure it, do not assume. Note this is also a real point in buildkit's favour on gonk-03f, whose case otherwise rests only on parallelism and cache.

4. STOP BUILDING THE TESTCLOCK METER ON EVERY COMMIT. chart/values.yaml says it is 'selected only by values-e2e.yaml' -- an e2e-harness-only image costing 3 job slots and ~34 MB per build. Gate it or make it manual.

5. LEAVE THE CONTROLLER'S APT LAYER. Checked whether distroless applies as it does for intake: it does not. git, jq, lsof, procps, tmux, util-linux and tini are documented hard deps of the gc supervisor (tmux runs sessions, flock guards the beads lock, tini is PID-1).
notes:
PART ONE SHIPPED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-19 (c501a24, deployed v0.1.0-030a6c58ee2e). THE BEAD STAYS OPEN -- the headline finding is NOT fixed.

WHAT IS DONE: glab and bd removed from the agent image. Measured against the registry before and after, compressed linux/amd64:
    v0.1.0-ef59b5b921ae   210.6 MB  (10 layers)
    v0.1.0-030a6c58ee2e   138.3 MB  (8 layers)
72.3 MB exactly, as predicted. Confirmed in a live session pod (s-go-6d2q, issue !29): 'glab ABSENT', 'bd ABSENT', opencode still at /usr/local/bin/opencode, and /workspace still carries the checkout -- so the slimmer image did not break the rig fetch. test/images/agent_smoke_test.go now asserts their ABSENCE rather than their presence.

WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE ACTUAL PROBLEM: layers still do not dedupe. Each agent build writes ~110 MB of fresh blobs (was ~182 MB) to deliver a 3.6 MB change, because the apt layer and opencode re-hash every build despite being pinned and byte-identical. Removing glab and bd shrank the thing being needlessly re-uploaded; it did not stop the re-uploading.

THE REMAINING FIX, unchanged in shape: a toolchain base image (debian + apt + opencode) rebuilt ONLY when images/versions.env changes, with Dockerfile.agent reduced to FROM that base plus one COPY of the Go binary. Per-commit cost then drops to roughly the binary size regardless of kaniko's digest behaviour. Same shape applies to the controller, whose gc and dolt are pinned to GASCITY_REF.

IT IS A BUILD-TOPOLOGY CHANGE AND WANTS ITS OWN SESSION: a new image and CI job, rules keyed on versions.env, and a build-ordering dependency (the base must exist before the agent builds) with a chicken-and-egg on first introduction. Getting it wrong breaks every agent build at once. Worth doing against a clean baseline rather than at the end of a long session.

ALSO STILL OPEN from the original list: kaniko --reproducible (untested; may recover dedupe with one flag, but rewrites the whole tar and is memory-hungry on johnny, where contention is already why builds are serialized), and gating the e2e-only testclock meter off normal commits (3 job slots + ~34 MB per build).

title: Broker session aliases are not unique by construction: a re-dispatch can mint a second session under the same attempt
description:
THE OTHER HALF OF gonk-u6p. u6p's stall is fixed (sweep now classifies an unreadable session past its reservation instead of retrying forever). This bead is the reason the ambiguity gets created in the first place, which the fix does NOT prevent.

EVIDENCE, measured live 2026-08-18 against the running city:
  go-93gk  alias=gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1  created 2026-08-10T23:11:07Z  running=false
  go-s4ug  alias=gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1  created 2026-08-10T23:15:36Z  running=false
Two sessions, one alias, 4m29s apart. NOT a sub-second race -- that interval is a re-dispatch, not concurrency.

MECHANISM. broker_inject.go builds the alias as gonk.<agent>.p<pid>.i<iid>.a<attempt> from dec.Attempt, and the meter assigns attempt = len(prior recorded attempts)+1. An attempt is only RECORDED when an outcome is reported. So while a reservation is open and unsettled, a second /decide returns the SAME attempt (by design -- it is idempotent, see the held-reservation path), and a second dispatch then mints a SECOND session under the identical alias.

WHY GAS CITY LETS IT. Create-time alias uniqueness appears to be scoped to ACTIVE sessions, while alias RESOLUTION is scoped to ALL sessions. gonk-zp3 recorded the create being correctly REFUSED for a2 ('session alias already exists: gonk.triage.p75.i24.a2 already belongs to go-7ira') -- that was while go-7ira was still live. Here the first a1 had already ended, so the check passed and the duplicate was created. Worth confirming against the gascity source at GASCITY_REF before treating as established, and worth an upstream note (gonk-ckb) if confirmed: uniqueness and resolution disagreeing about scope makes any alias reuse a permanent 409.

OPTIONS, in preference order:
 1. Make the alias unique BY CONSTRUCTION -- append the reservation ID or a ULID, so a re-dispatch can never collide even under an idempotent attempt number. Cheapest and closes it regardless of upstream behaviour.
 2. Make dispatch refuse to create when the record already carries a SessionID for this attempt (dispatch-side idempotency to match the meter's).
 3. Have the sweep resolve a multi-match by selecting the newest. Rejected as the primary fix: it makes the ambiguity survivable but leaves two sessions racing to be judged.

Note option 1 changes the correlation key, so check anything that PARSES the alias (the reaper matches gonk-created sessions by prefix) before changing its shape.
notes:
ONE MORE REASON THIS MATTERS, seen during gonk-u6p's live verification 2026-08-18: session TEARDOWN is also by alias. After the verdict, sweep logged

  POST /v0/city/gonk/session/gonk.triage.p75.i24.a1/close 404

Harmless in that instance -- both sessions had already ended, so there was nothing to close -- but the close path resolves the same ambiguous alias as the read did. Against an alias matching two sessions, a close cannot be trusted to have closed the RIGHT one, and if either were still running it would leak (the gonk-xkm failure mode) while reporting something that looks like completion.

So unique-by-construction aliases are not only about making the read work; they are what makes teardown addressable at all. Strengthens option 1 over option 3 in the description: resolving a multi-match by 'newest' would fix reads and leave this hole open.
FIXED 030a6c5, DEPLOYED v0.1.0-030a6c58ee2e, and exercised live 2026-08-19.

THE ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD GUESSED. The description reasoned about Gas City's create-time uniqueness scope, and that part holds -- but the actual defect is on gonk's side and simpler: runDispatch builds its beadstore.Record FRESH from the webhook args, so SessionID is ALWAYS empty at the create, even when a session for that exact bead+attempt already exists. Nothing anywhere consulted the store first. The meter is idempotent by design (an open, unsettled reservation returns the same attempt), so a re-dispatch recomputed the same alias and created a second session under it.

FIX: consult the store before creating; if a record already carries a SessionID for THIS attempt, log and return 0 without creating. Keyed on the ATTEMPT deliberately -- a re-sling is a new attempt and must still get its own session, and refusing there would strand every retried bead. On an unreadable store it proceeds loudly rather than failing closed, because since gonk-u6p a duplicate is recoverable while a dropped dispatch is not.

TESTS: TestASecondDispatchForTheSameAttemptCreatesNoSecondSession (reproduces production exactly -- with the guard disabled it creates two sessions both aliased gonk.triage.p42.i3.a1) and TestARealReSlingOnTheNextAttemptStillGetsItsOwnSession (pins .a1 and .a2 get distinct sessions).

LIVE STATE: issues !27 and !29 both dispatched normally on the deployed build -- one session each, and !27's re-sling correctly opened gonk.triage.p75.i27.a2 with its own checkout grant. So the guard does not block legitimate dispatch or re-slinging, which was the risk worth checking. The duplicate path itself cannot be forced on demand (it needs a re-dispatch inside an open reservation), so it is proven by test rather than by production repro -- stated plainly rather than claimed as a live verification.

OPTION 1 FROM THE DESCRIPTION REMAINS AVAILABLE AND UNTAKEN: unique-by-construction aliases. It would NOT have prevented this failure (both creates shared a reservation, so a reservation-derived suffix collides identically), and cmd/gonk-gate/reap.go matches gonk's own sessions with an anchored regex '^gonk\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\.p\d+(\.i\d+)?\.a\d+$' -- changing the alias shape without updating that in lockstep would stop the reaper recognising gonk sessions and convert a 409 into a leak. Worth doing as defence in depth for the case where the RECORD is lost (dispatch dies between create and store, which is exactly what the reaper exists for), but it is a separate change with a real trap in it.

CLOSING: the measured failure is fixed, tested, deployed, and does not block normal operation.
close_reason: Dispatch consults the store before creating; duplicate for one bead+attempt refused. Tested (reproduces the production duplicate), deployed, and normal dispatch + re-sling confirmed live.

title: OWNER DECISION: may a persistent arm64 buildkitd live on bailey?
description:
The question that decides the buildkit architecture (gonk-03f). Not mine to answer.

MEASURED 2026-08-18. arm64 is the binding constraint and it is a POLICY problem, not a hardware one: orac01-04 are 7.3-7.5Gi allocatable and sitting at 52/60/62/85% memory -- orac04 has ~1.1Gi free. None can host a builder. The only arm64 machine with room is bailey: 127Gi allocatable, 13% used, ~110Gi idle. johnny covers amd64 comfortably (29.2Gi, 48% used, ~15Gi headroom).

THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS, PARTLY. homelab/ci-templates /kaniko.yml ALREADY pins arm64 builds to bailey -- KUBERNETES_NODE_SELECTOR_HOSTNAME=kubernetes.io/hostname=bailey plus the orac.local/gpu-only=true:NoSchedule toleration -- with the comment that orac01-04 are too small. So arm64 CI builds are already an exception to 'bailey runs GPU workloads exclusively'.

THE DIFFERENCE THAT MAKES THIS A QUESTION: today bailey hosts EPHEMERAL job pods that tolerate the taint and leave. A persistent buildkitd is a LONG-LIVED DAEMON holding a cache PVC on a machine whose exclusivity is enforced by taint+label and treated as load-bearing. That is a materially larger claim and it also puts a CI dependency on the GPU host's availability.

NOTE THIS IS NOT BLOCKING. Architecture (B) -- ephemeral rootless buildkitd inside each job, the same lifecycle kaniko has today -- needs NO policy change, is strictly less invasive, and still delivers both benefits that justify the migration. (B) is the recommended start regardless; a persistent daemon becomes a measured optimization later, not a prerequisite. Answer this when convenient, not to unblock.

title: SPIKE: does rootless buildkitd run on Talos without a node-config change?
description:
The assumption most likely to invalidate the whole buildkit design (gonk-03f). Answer it before writing any YAML.

buildkitd rootless needs user namespaces and permissive-enough seccomp. Talos is immutable and locks much of this down. If it works as-is, the migration stays entirely inside gitops + ci-templates. IF IT NEEDS A NODE-CONFIG CHANGE, that change lives in the HARDWARE repo, not gitops -- a repo boundary crossing that materially raises the cost of the plan and should be weighed before committing.

DO: run buildkitd rootless in a throwaway pod on johnny (amd64) and on an arm64 node, build a trivial Dockerfile, and record exactly what it needed -- securityContext, seccomp profile, any sysctl. Test BOTH arches: the arm64 nodes run the same Talos but the only one with memory headroom is bailey, which carries the gpu-only taint.

RECORD THE ANSWER ON gonk-03f regardless of outcome. A negative result here is worth as much as a positive one -- it is the difference between a two-repo change and a three-repo change.

title: Rule out the cheap option first: evaluate the Chainguard kaniko fork
description:
GATES the buildkit migration (gonk-03f) and may cancel it entirely. Do this BEFORE any buildkit work.

GoogleContainerTools/kaniko was archived 2025-06-03 and is read-only -- maintainers retired, no CVE will be fixed there. Chainguard forked it within a day, with two of the original creators (Priya Wadhwa, Dan Lorenc) on staff. The fork is a drop-in replacement for gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor.

THE POINT: 'upstream is dead' is the most alarming of the three arguments for migrating to buildkit, and it is satisfiable by changing ONE image reference in homelab/ci-templates /kaniko.yml. Hours of work against weeks. If the fork is healthy, the security-maintenance argument for buildkit disappears completely and buildkit has to stand on parallelism and bounded cache alone.

DO: confirm the fork is actually maintained (release cadence, CVE response, whether it publishes multi-arch images for both amd64 and arm64 -- this cluster needs both). Check whether it still carries the flags the template depends on: --cache-repo, --compressed-caching, --custom-platform, --registry-mirror, --insecure-registry, --skip-tls-verify. Then swap the image in /kaniko.yml behind an MR (that project takes MRs, not direct commits -- its globals merge into every consuming pipeline) and confirm a gonk build still passes.

OUTCOME EITHER WAY: if the fork is healthy, adopt it and re-score gonk-03f on wall-clock and cache alone -- it may well be worth closing unbuilt. If the fork is not healthy, that materially strengthens the buildkit case and should be recorded on gonk-03f.

title: EPIC: migrate image builds from kaniko to buildkit (gonk pilot)
description:
Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-buildkit-migration-design.md. DECIDED 2026-08-18 (owner): gonk is the pilot; the rest of the fleet migrates later on evidence, and this is designed-and-filed now rather than built now -- Phase 0 of the local-parity roadmap (gonk-6sp) stays the active work.

THE CASE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS. None of the recent build failures were kaniko's: pipelines 2102/2103/2113/2123/2124/2132 were ENOSPC from the full registry volume (gonk-mzm), 2177 was a GitLab 500 on /jwt/auth plus a runner_system_failure, and 2187's skipped jobs were 10dda82's changes: rules working correctly. Buildkit would have failed identically on all of them.

WHAT KANIKO ACTUALLY COSTS, ranked: (1) serialized builds -- resource_group gonk-images-$BUILD_ARCH exists because parallel kaniko pods contend for memory on johnny, so five images build one at a time per arch; this is a WALL-CLOCK argument, not a correctness one. (2) unbounded cache -- --cache-repo reached 139GB across 1296 tags and was the largest contributor to filling a 296GB volume (gonk-1t4); buildkit's gckeepstorage bounds it structurally. (3) upstream is dead -- GoogleContainerTools/kaniko was archived 2025-06-03, read-only, no CVE fixes.

CRITICAL SEQUENCING: reason 3 is satisfiable by an IMAGE SWAP to the Chainguard fork (hours, not weeks). So buildkit must be justified on parallelism and bounded cache ALONE. The fork evaluation is filed first and deliberately gates the rest -- if it is sufficient, close this epic unbuilt.

title: DEV-ENV: pick bailey's model/server mix to suit how we develop gonk (not a gonk feature)
description: Framing correction: gonk is the primary workload on bailey, so the rung catalog is a REQUIREMENTS STATEMENT on the serving layer, not just a consumer of it. Different stages want different serving: triage = short one-shot, latency-visible, small model, either backend; implementation = long context + many tool calls + the same repo prefix resent every turn, which strongly favours vLLM for continuous batching, paged KV and especially --enable-prefix-caching; review = medium context, precision-sensitive, and should use a DIFFERENT model for diversity (ADR-007 4.3); search/classification subagent = tiny, high-frequency, cheap. Ollama's load/unload low-commitment model is the wrong shape for sustained agent load and the right shape for ad-hoc/keep-warm. CONTENTION: vLLM holds gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 while Ollama stays resident on the same box; consolidating the agent workload onto vLLM frees headroom to raise utilization and/or --max-model-len toward the stated ~250k target, which is probably the real answer to the 131072-vs-250k gap rather than drift. Also evaluate SGLang (RadixAttention gives stronger prefix reuse across branching agent turns; first-class structured output) and TensorRT-LLM (best raw perf on Grace-Blackwell, much more painful to operate). Feed the decision with measured demand: instrument requested-policy vs resolved-model vs cost per call, per Warp's routing observability schema, so the catalog is a living artifact rather than a hand-edited static config.
notes: SCOPE CORRECTED: this is a DEVELOPMENT-ENVIRONMENT / operator activity for orac, NOT a gonk product feature. gonk the software must assume nothing beyond an OpenAI-compatible endpoint -- spec goal 8 requires no deployment-specific material in the product repos, and environment.md already states the rule for exactly this class of fact (site-local model names must never appear as defaults in product code or chart). The same rule governs serving assumptions: no assumption about batching, prefix caching, resident-model behaviour, or which server is present. Outcome of this work belongs in docs/environment.md (gonk-4ck) and the gitops repo, not in the chart or pack.

The doc also documents no vLLM deployment at all, though bailey-gpu/vllm has been running. Refresh the inventory and the local-inference section; the site-local-not-defaults rule still stands and should be restated. Related: gonk-m4k, and the routing bead filed alongside this.

title: Agent image sets no PAGER: git commands will hang the agent in a pager
description: grep finds no PAGER, GIT_PAGER, or --no-pager anywhere in images/ or pack/. Warp published this as a real, common, silent production failure: an agent that runs 'git log' gets dropped into a pager and hangs until timeout, with no error. gonk's agent has shell access and will hit it. Cheapest fix: set PAGER=cat and GIT_PAGER=cat in the agent image (and/or git config core.pager cat) so no command can block on an interactive pager. Verified absent 2026-08-13.

title: The mention trigger is silently dead: it still pours a formula, and that path cannot deliver a prompt
description: cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go:41-51 -- brokerPorted maps only 'issue-triage' and 'scaffold'. Its own comment says 'Only mention still pours its formula in runDispatch until it is ported'. The formula-pour path is the one upstream Gas City drops caller vars on (see gonk-6gs, upstream #4668/#4891), so a mention-triggered session cannot receive its prompt. Net effect: spec section 5.5's conversational @-mention surface is dead code that fails silently rather than erroring. Either port mention onto the broker path like triage/scaffold, or make the formula path fail loudly so a dead trigger cannot masquerade as a working one. Found by the Fable second-opinion review, 2026-08-13.

title: Phase 5: harden -- run states, agent metrics, cost visibility, model routing, then widen intake
description: (5.1) run state machine INPROGRESS/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/BLOCKED/ERROR/CANCELLED + error taxonomy (environment_setup_failed, agent_process_failed incl OOM non-retryable, infrastructure_timeout as stale-task reaper = the whole runaway backstop); run-state transitions and messages share a global sequence number; parent success is NOT transitive. (5.2) agent-run OTel metrics, all series pre-seeded at startup. (5.3) cost where the work is seen: per-run footer on the MR + budget approach-alert comment at ~80%. (5.4) model routing by complexity (small local model for search/classify, larger for implementation); store requested policy AND resolved model separately per message with cost. (5.5) cross-MODEL failover chain across local models -- retrying the same model reproduces the failure; this is the correct fix for gonk-ob5's fail-open. (5.6) multi-harness rung by adopting the .agents/skills format rather than inventing a protocol. (5.7) close egress gap (gonk-7oz, Cilium). (5.8) ONLY NOW widen intake: unblock gonk-6po source beads, gonk-icj, gonk-8s0, and add scheduled triggers as first-class.
notes: ADDED per second-opinion review (roadmap 11b): delete the formula / [steps.check] machinery entirely once mention is ported to the broker (gonk-ecn). Carrying two orchestration idioms is what produced the silently-dead mention trigger and three zombie carry-forwards in PLAN.md. Also: adopt Warp's fault-split error taxonomy (FAILED = caller's fault, ERROR = platform's fault, retryable on the wire).

title: Phase 4: feedback loop + the runtime work that enables it
description: Runtime prerequisites: (4.1) research/search subagent with its OWN context window on a smaller local model -- Warp measured tool defs at up to 50k tokens unused in ~90% of conversations, -26% tokens when moved to a subagent; with qwen3-14b at num_ctx 16384 this is structural not optional. (4.2) NO embeddings -- their 75.8% SWE-bench agent uses grep/find/cat with capped output. (4.3) edit ladder exact->indentation-agnostic->Jaro-Winkler, return failure reasons, return only the changed hunk +/- k lines. (4.4) context-dependent tool availability; fix the pager hang (PAGER=cat). (4.5) environment as one declarative fail-closed object. (4.6) sidecar-merge harness tooling (serves gonk-e0o). (4.7) warm cache volume. Loop: (4.8) versioned hidden marker in every agent comment = join key to skill revision. (4.9) DETERMINISTIC feedback collection from structural GitLab signals (relabels are ground truth, thread resolution, patch applied verbatim) -- no model in the classification path. (4.10) bounded write surface: '## Learned guidelines' capped at 15 bullets, explicit never-touch contract list, 'no change' is a valid outcome, MR-only never direct commit. (4.11) teach generalization explicitly or you get a rule factory. (4.12) evals gate -- CLOSE WARP'S GAP: they publish no accuracy metric and concede local maxima. Use test/stubmodel cassettes.
notes: REVISED per second-opinion review (roadmap 11b): SUBSTANTIALLY CUT. Runtime items 4.1-4.4 move to Phase 1 (gonk-3so). The SELF-IMPROVEMENT LOOP (4.9-4.12) is CUT: Warp never validated theirs even with a team producing hundreds of runs weekly -- no accuracy metric, no eval, published concession that it finds local maxima. A solo operator's correction corpus is statistically empty and a loop learning from a handful of relabels overfits faster than it improves. KEEP only the versioned marker (4.8, now in Phase 1). What remains here: environments as one declarative object, sidecar-merged harness tooling, warm cache volume. Revisit the loop when there is a corpus worth mining.

title: Phase 3: review + verify -- annotated-diff coordinates, artifact-backed status
description: (a) Annotated diff as an ADDRESSING scheme, not presentation: rewrite the diff so every line carries [OLD:n]/[NEW:n]/[OLD:n,NEW:m]; declare it the ONLY location source; validator cross-checks every cited coordinate against the diff map. This is what gonk-3jm's split red/green diff should be FOR -- it eliminates hallucinated line numbers, which matters far more with a 14B model. (b) Validator with closed enums + hard caps the agent iterates against until green. (c) Reviewer runs read-only and non-blocking; never executes changed code; only write is the structured artifact. (d) Two verification modes reproduce/verify -- pre-state failure + post-state pass is the behavioral red/green. (e) STATUS FROM ARTIFACT EXISTENCE, NOT AGENT ASSERTION; 'blocked' first-class and distinct from failure; no artifact means a quoted failure string. (f) CLOSE WARP'S GAP: explicit max-attempts and deterministic give-up (theirs is unbounded, cost-warning only) -- also a budget-safety requirement since each attempt is a reservation. (g) three-stage privilege split resolve/work/apply with SHA re-validation. Builds on gonk-qhe, gonk-3jm.
