title: All three replicas of the GitLab registry volume live on venus
description:
Noticed while sizing an expansion for gonk-mzm. pvc-daae18b0-68b7-4a79-ad9b-0aed025a6af0 (gitlab-registry-storage-pvc, 300Gi) has three Longhorn replicas and every one of them is on node venus. Three copies on one node is not three-way redundancy -- losing venus loses the whole container registry, and the storage cost is paid three times over for no availability benefit.

It also blocks expansion as a way out of a full-volume incident: venus ssd-longhorn reports max 1862Gi, scheduled 2059Gi (already over-provisioned) and 294Gi actually available, so growing the PVC by 100Gi would need 300Gi of real space on venus and does not fit.

CHECK: whether this is a soft anti-affinity that gave up under pressure, a replica-zone/node-selector setting, or the other nodes simply having no schedulable Longhorn disk. Then decide whether to rebalance replicas off venus. Not gonk's volume, so this is a heads-up for the cluster owner rather than something gonk should change.

title: Bound registry growth: cleanup policy on gonk-project plus an alert on the registry volume
description:
Two durable guards so the registry cannot silently fill again (gonk-mzm was invisible until eight image jobs failed at once with a misleading 'error checking push permissions' -- the real error was Err:28, ENOSPC).

1. CONTAINER CLEANUP POLICY on agentic/gonk-project. GitLab applies it per container repository, so it covers the kaniko cache repo too:
     PUT /projects/agentic%2Fgonk-project
       container_expiration_policy_attributes: {cadence: '1d', keep_n: 10, older_than: '14d', name_regex: '.*', enabled: true}
   RISK TO WEIGH FIRST: Flux pins exact tags, so a long-lived deployed tag could in principle age past older_than while still deployed. keep_n=10 protects the 10 newest per repo, and now that images build only on changes (commit 10dda82) ten builds spans weeks rather than a couple of days. Confirm the deployed tag is inside keep_n before enabling, and consider name_regex_keep for the deployed tag if the deploy cadence ever slows.

2. ALERT on the PVC. gitlab-registry-storage-pvc is 300Gi on longhorn; nothing warned as it approached full. Add a Prometheus rule on kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes for that PVC at 80 percent. Worth applying to every longhorn PVC, not just this one.

Longhorn has ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION=true, so expanding is also possible -- but expansion without the other two just moves the wall further out.

title: Split a gonk-agent-base image so per-commit agent builds stop re-fetching the toolchain
description:
The gonk-agent build takes ~978s (pipeline 1555) and is dominated by work that does not change from commit to commit: apt-get install of git/ca-certificates/jq/tmux/curl/tar, plus three checksum-verified downloads (opencode, glab, bd) in the 'fetch' stage. All of it is keyed on images/versions.env, not on the working tree, yet it runs on every image build.

PROPOSAL: build agentic/gonk-project/gonk-agent-base from a new images/Dockerfile.agent-base containing exactly the fetch stage plus the runtime apt layer, tagged on the CONTENT of images/versions.env (e.g. base-<sha256 of versions.env, 12 chars>). Its CI job runs only on 'changes: [images/versions.env, images/Dockerfile.agent-base]'. Dockerfile.agent then becomes FROM that base plus COPY of the gonk-gate binary and the entrypoint.

EXPECTED: per-commit agent builds drop from ~978s to roughly the Go build plus a COPY. Also cuts image storage -- the 26 GB across 203 gonk-agent tags is dominated by re-pushed runtime layers whose digests change whenever the apt layer is rebuilt.

PRECEDENT ON THIS CLUSTER: agentic/openclaw already does this (agentic/openclaw/base, 5.7 GB across just 3 tags, versus agentic/openclaw at 29 GB across 15).

CARE REQUIRED: the base tag must be derived from versions.env content, not from a git sha, or the two drift and an agent image silently ships a stale toolchain -- the exact silent-success shape this project keeps hitting. The build must FAIL, not fall back, if the computed base tag does not exist.
notes:
MEASURED (pipeline 2065, the last fully green one, 2026-08-11): total 4522 job-seconds per pipeline, of which the ten image builds are 4158s -- 92 percent. Per job: controller-image-arm64 606s, controller-image-amd64 604s, agent-image-amd64 434s, agent-image-arm64 389s, meter 375/374s, meter-testclock 373/371s, intake 325/307s, every index job under 20s.

CONTROLLER IS THE SLOWEST, not the agent -- so this split should cover Dockerfile.controller too, not just Dockerfile.agent. Its 'gc' stage clones gastownhall/gascity from GitHub and builds ./cmd/gc on every image build. Those RUN layers are keyed on GASCITY_REF alone, so kaniko caching SHOULD already hit them; if 604s says it does not, find out why before building a base image on top of a cache that is not working. Same question applies to its apt layer and the bd/dolt fetches.

Note the CI change in 10dda82 does not reduce these per-build numbers at all -- it reduces how OFTEN they run (70 percent of commits now build nothing). This bead is the other half: making the builds that do run cheaper.

title: ollama on bailey is rejecting nomic-embed-text with 503 queue-full in a sustained loop
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-11 16:30-16:33Z while investigating gonk-2do. NOT a gonk fault; filing because it is live and nobody appears to be watching it.

ollama pod ollama-7454d8f495-sxtg5 (ns bailey-gpu) is returning a steady stream of 503s, roughly 3 every 30s, sustained across the whole window:
    [GIN] POST /api/embed | 503 | ~10-18ms | 10.244.5.80
LiteLLM's side:
    litellm.aembedding(model=ollama/nomic-embed-text) Exception litellm.APIConnectionError:
    OllamaException - {"error":"server busy, please try again.  maximum pending requests exceeded"}

DIAGNOSIS per the bailey-gpu-forensics runbook: an INSTANT 503 (10-18ms, not a timeout) is a queue-full rejection at the door, NOT OOM and not GPU exhaustion. Corroborated: ollama reports 'all slots are idle' and only qwen3:14b resident at 100% GPU throughout, so nothing is actually being served while these are rejected.

CONTRIBUTING CONFIG: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 -- a single-slot server. The runbook's exact failure mode: with one slot, whenever arrivals outpace service the client retries and amplifies the flood, and it does not drain on its own.

WHO: the caller is 10.244.5.80. Identify the pod before changing anything; it is embeddings traffic, so a likely candidate is an indexing or RAG job rather than interactive use.

SUGGESTED per the runbook: add client-side backpressure in LiteLLM (max_parallel_requests, and num_retries: 0 on embeddings -- retries amplify the flood) rather than restarting the pod, which only clears the queue and is shared infrastructure that must be confirmed before bouncing.

Bailey is shared and serves live interactive inference; this is a heads-up for its owner, not something to fix unilaterally from gonk.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-11, gitops 5a60ff1.

ROOT CAUSE was not the flood, it was lost redundancy. nomic-embed-text is documented as TWO deployments so the router can fail over, with the in-cluster CPU embedder as 'the reliability floor'. On 2026-07-31 nomic-incluster was repointed to bailey for a real reason (that pod was pegged under an index build, 39s-1m20s per call vs bailey's 84-194ms). That left the group with exactly ONE member while the comment above it still described two -- so when bailey wedged there was nothing to fail over to, and retries hammered a backend that could not recover.

CHANGES:
 - Restored both members of the nomic-embed-text group (CPU embedder + bailey). allowed_fails: 2 + cooldown_time: 30 now removes a failing backend from rotation automatically, in EITHER direction, so this self-heals instead of needing a manual repoint each time one side degrades.
 - max_parallel_requests: 4 on the bailey deployment -- the real backpressure.
 - OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 1 -> 2 (owner-approved). Held at 2, not 4: num_parallel multiplies KV cache per loaded model eagerly at load time, and bailey is at 118.4/121.7 GiB with ~14 GiB swapped, with qwen3:14b pinned resident.

DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED PLAN, deliberate: num_retries was NOT dropped to 0. That advice was correct when the group had one dead member and retries were pure amplification. With two live deployments num_retries IS the failover mechanism -- setting it to 0 would have disabled the fix. Amplification is bounded with max_parallel_requests instead.

VERIFIED AFTER:
 - direct ollama /api/embed on bailey returns real embeddings (was an instant 503 in 0.03s)
 - 503 count since ollama restart: 0; LiteLLM queue-full exceptions: 0
 - gonk rung 1 (qwen3-14b) still serves -- returned GOLF -- so NUM_PARALLEL=2 did not stop the pinned model loading, which was the stated risk
 - LiteLLM rolled and the live ConfigMap now shows both nomic-embed-text deployments
First calls after the restart were slow (embed 39.7s, chat 1m6s) -- cold loads, expected.

REMAINING: the litellm bailey-judge-keepwarm CronJob was erroring before this; worth re-checking now that the backend serves.
close_reason: Closed

title: qwen3-14b is capped at num_ctx 16384 in litellm-config while its own cost map says 40960
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while diagnosing gonk-2do.

WHERE: configmap litellm-config in ns litellm, model_list entry for model_name qwen3-14b:
    litellm_params: {model: ollama_chat/qwen3:14b, num_ctx: 16384, keep_alive: -1, think: false}
    model_info:     {context_window: 16384, max_input_tokens: 16384, max_tokens: 16384}

THE INCONSISTENCY: litellm_settings.model_cost_map in the SAME ConfigMap declares qwen3-14b with max_input_tokens 40960 / max_output_tokens 8192. So the file contradicts itself -- the cost map advertises 40960, the model_list caps the actual ollama context at 16384. 'ollama ps' confirms the live resident model is at CONTEXT 16384. qwen3-8b next to it gets 40960, and qwen3.6:35b gets 131072.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY DELIBERATE: this entry alone carries keep_alive: -1, i.e. pinned resident in bailey's unified memory forever. A smaller num_ctx is the obvious way to bound the footprint of an always-warm model. So this is likely a VRAM budget decision, not an oversight -- but it is undocumented and self-contradictory, which is how it cost me an investigation.

WHY GONK CARES: qwen3-14b is rung 1 of the instance ladder and enforce_ladder_order=true, so it is where EVERY triage starts. opencode's build-agent preamble measures ~6.4K tokens before any issue text (measured: 6415 input for a trivial prompt, 6676 for a small triage prompt). That leaves roughly 9.7K for the issue title/body plus the model's own output. A large issue body will overrun rung 1, and the failure mode for a context overrun on this path has not been characterised -- given gonk-2do, an empty successful-looking turn is a real possibility.

NOT the cause of gonk-2do -- that was --attach, ruled out by measurement.

ASK: confirm 16384 is an intentional VRAM tradeoff and, if so, write it down next to the entry and reconcile the cost map so the two agree. Then decide whether gonk should bound issue text against the rung's real context, or whether rung 1 should be a larger-context model.
notes:
CAPACITY CHECKED 2026-08-11 -- raising num_ctx is NOT safe today.

Measured on the bailey node: total 121.7 GiB, used 118.4, MemFree 3.4 GiB, UNACCOUNTED(GPU) 104.0 GiB, and ~14 of 16 GiB of swap in use. The box is memory-saturated, not idle (kubectl top node's 9% excludes GPU entirely and is misleading here -- see gonk-38o).

Raising qwen3-14b from num_ctx 16384 to 40960 grows its KV cache 2.5x on a model that is pinned resident with keep_alive: -1, i.e. the increase is permanent, not per-request. With 3.4 GiB free and active swapping, that is the wrong direction until memory is reclaimed. It would also directly worsen gonk-38o, which is already failing to load a 274 MB embedding model.

SO THE 16384 IS ALMOST CERTAINLY A DELIBERATE VRAM TRADEOFF, as suspected -- it just is not written down, and the cost map still contradicts it by advertising 40960.

TWO SEPARABLE ASKS NOW:
 1. DOCUMENTATION, free and safe: reconcile model_cost_map (40960) with the model_list entry (16384) so the file stops contradicting itself, and note next to the entry that the cap is a deliberate footprint bound for a keep_alive: -1 model. This can be done independently of any capacity work.
 2. CAPACITY, blocked on gonk-38o: if rung 1 genuinely needs more context, the cheapest reclaim per the GPU runbook is vLLM's --max-model-len, currently 131072 with --gpu-memory-utilization=0.35 (~42.6 GiB pre-reserved and held while idle). Shrinking an oversized context window there frees more than qwen3-14b needs. Do not touch either until the ~51 GiB of GPU memory unattributed to any k8s pod is identified.

FOR GONK SPECIFICALLY, independent of the above: opencode's build-agent preamble measures ~6.4K tokens, leaving ~9.7K of the 16384 for issue text plus output. gonk should bound the issue text it injects against the rung's real context rather than assuming it fits, since the failure mode on overrun has not been characterised.

title: Source beads 5: retention -- compact resolved and done source beads
description:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-source-beads-design.md

One bead per external object, retained after resolution so the backlog and the audit trail survive, means the store grows without bound. bd compact exists (semantic summarization of old closed issues). Decide the window and wire it, so the bead store does not become the next capacity problem in a namespace that has already lost pods to eviction.

Depends on slice 3, which is what puts beads into resolved in the first place.

title: zot mirror does not serve digest-pinned base manifests, so every image build depends on Docker Hub directly
description:
kaniko is pointed at the zot pull-through mirror (--registry-mirror=$ZOT_MIRROR) precisely so docker.io pulls are cached and not rate-limited. But every gonk build logs:

  WARN Failed to retrieve image golang:1.26.5@sha256:ae5a...
       from remapped registry zot.registry-system.svc.cluster.local:5000:
       GET .../manifests/sha256:ae5a...: MANIFEST_UNKNOWN
  INFO Retrieving image golang:1.26.5@sha256:ae5a... from registry index.docker.io

i.e. zot cannot serve a manifest requested BY DIGEST, so kaniko falls back to Docker Hub for every base image on every leg. The mirror provides no protection at all for gonk, which pins all its bases by digest (images/versions.env).

Observed cost: pipeline 2008 lost 4 of 5 image jobs (controller+intake, both arches) to 'GET https://index.docker.io/...: unexpected status code 500' inside one ~30s Docker Hub window. Retrying cleared it, but every build is one upstream hiccup away from failing.

This is registry-system/zot config, not gonk -- likely needs the upstream-sync/pull-through config to resolve digests, or a pre-warm. Hand to the gitops team alongside the traefik item.

title: Pushing to gonk main triggers a Flux Helm upgrade -- even a bead-only commit
description:
The gonk GitRepository is tracked with chart version '*' and reconcileStrategy: Revision, and the chart version embeds the git SHA. So ANY push to gonk main re-renders the chart and triggers a Helm upgrade, which can recreate and reschedule pods.

Consequence: a 'bd:' export commit redeploys production. During the gonk-n50 outage this is how the controller moved from johnny (amd64) onto orac04 (arm64) and started crash-looping.

Decide whether chart releases should be gated on something other than 'any commit to main' -- e.g. a tag, a path filter on chart/**, or an explicit chart version bump.

title: gonk includes homelab/ci-templates at ref: main, not a tagged ref
description:
.gitlab-ci.yml has 'include: project: homelab/ci-templates, ref: main'. That project's own README says to pin a TAGGED ref so a change there cannot alter a consuming pipeline unannounced. gonk is currently exposed to every commit on ci-templates main.

Pin to a tag (v0.2.3 once homelab/ci-templates!4 merges) and bump deliberately.

title: Park and re-drive webhooks received while unsynced, so the startup window is lossless not merely short
description:
Option (b) from gonk-fan, split out deliberately rather than left as an unmet acceptance
criterion. gonk-fan shipped option (a): the startup reconcile ladder shrinks the drop window
from ten minutes to roughly a second, plus a 30s retry whenever a pass leaves anything
unsynced.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AFTER (a): a webhook that arrives inside that ~1s window is STILL DROPPED,
and GitLab does not retry. gonk-fan's acceptance criteria says "dispatched or replayed --
not silently dropped", and (a) alone does not deliver the "replayed" half. The exposure is
~99.7% smaller, not gone.

WHAT TO BUILD: hold events received while the project is unsynced, and re-drive them once it
resolves. The drop happens at a single clean choke point -- gate() in pkg/intake/dispatch.go
returns Decision{Reason: "state_" + state} -- so the interception is easy; the queue is the
part with real decisions in it.

DECISIONS TO SETTLE, none of them obvious:
- BOUNDS. An unbounded park queue is a memory leak with a webhook firehose pointed at it.
  Cap it, and decide what dropping-on-overflow means (it is the current behaviour, so it is
  not a regression -- but it must be counted).
- TTL. A parked event for a project that never resolves must expire, not sit forever.
- WHAT IF IT RESOLVES NON-DISPATCHABLE. If the project comes back invalid or disabled, the
  parked events must be discarded, not dispatched. Replay must re-run gate(), never bypass it.
- DEDUPE. Intake already dedupes GitLab redeliveries; a replayed event must not double-fire
  alongside a redelivery of the same event.
- PERSISTENCE. Parked in memory means a crash during the window still loses them. Probably
  acceptable -- (a) already covers the common restart case -- but say so explicitly rather
  than discovering it later.

TEST SHAPE: fire a webhook while unsynced, resolve the project, assert the work is
dispatched -- and separately, resolve it to `disabled` and assert the parked event is
DISCARDED. The second is the one that matters: a replay path that bypasses the gate is a
worse bug than the drop it fixes.

title: Release mechanics: make push rebuilds and can drift the tag; the ingress cannot carry the big images
description:
Two release hazards hit during the v0.1.0-80f906b34717 deploy, 2026-08-04. Both are
one-time-discoverable and will bite the next person otherwise.

1. `make push` DEPENDS ON `images`, SO IT REBUILDS -- and GONK_TAG is
   $(GONK_VERSION)-$(git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD), evaluated at invocation. If HEAD moves
   between building and pushing (a bead commit is enough), push silently starts building a
   DIFFERENT tag from the one you built and staged. In this run the staged gitops bump
   pointed at 26c4f6991cfb while push was producing 80f906b34717; committing on schedule
   would have pointed flux at a tag built locally and never pushed -- ImagePullBackOff
   across the namespace.
   FIX: a `push-only` target that pushes without the `images` prerequisite, and/or resolve
   GONK_TAG once and echo it so a release reads the tag rather than recomputing it. The
   deploy should take the tag from what is verifiably IN THE REGISTRY.

2. THE TRAEFIK INGRESS 504s ON THE BIG IMAGES. gonk-agent (~569MB) and gonk-controller
   (~560MB) both fail with "writing blob: uploading layer chunked: received unexpected HTTP
   status: 504 Gateway Timeout" through registry.orac.local, on every retry. gonk-intake
   (16MB) and gonk-meter (54MB) go through, though meter needed one retry after a 499.
   WORKAROUND USED: kubectl -n gitlab port-forward svc/gitlab-registry 5000:5000, then
   podman login --tls-verify=false localhost:5000 and push to
   localhost:5000/agentic/gonk-project/<image>:<tag> -- same repository path, same backing
   store, bypasses the proxy entirely. The pre-existing localhost:5000 tags in the local
   image store show a previous session hit this too and the knowledge was lost.
   REAL FIX: raise the traefik proxy read/send timeouts for registry.orac.local, or
   document the port-forward as the supported path.

3. MINOR, but it cost time: `podman manifest inspect` cannot verify these images at all --
   single-arch images fail with "Treating single images as manifest lists is not
   implemented" even when the manifest is fetched fine. Verify a push with an actual pull.

Registry auth, for the record: it takes a GitLab PAT. `glab config get token --host
gitlab.orac.local | podman login --username <user> --password-stdin registry.orac.local`.
notes: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-10 by gonk-9ub (commit 1e89c38): hazard 1 (make push rebuilds and can drift the tag) can no longer produce a DEPLOYABLE artifact, because push now writes only arch-suffixed tags. The drift itself is still possible -- GONK_TAG is still evaluated at invocation -- but it can no longer point flux at a tag that was never pushed, which was the damaging half. Hazard 2 (the ingress cannot carry the big images) is with the gitops team.

title: Author role gates what a triage outcome may become: a contributor's feature request is not actionable work
description:
Raised by the owner 2026-08-03, while scoping the code-writing capability.

THE RULE: a feature request from an outside CONTRIBUTOR must not become actionable work.
The same request from a maintainer/developer/owner is a design-and-planning session -- a
capability gonk does not have yet and should not fake. So today the role decides between
'triage it, label it, and leave it for a human' and (later) 'open a planning session'.

WHY THIS IS STRONGER THAN IT FIRST LOOKS, and why it belongs with the deterministic gates
rather than with classification (gonk-kxg): AUTHOR ROLE IS A FACT THE CONTROLLER CAN LOOK
UP, not a judgement a model makes. It fits the standing invariant exactly -- models supply
constraints and objections; only deterministic checks and humans grant permission. The
classifier may say 'this is a feature request'; the role lookup says whether that class is
allowed to produce anything, and the model has no vote in it.

IT IS ALREADY DECIDABLE WITH WHAT WE HAVE. pkg/glab has ListMembers and the access-level
constants (AccessGuest 10 / Reporter 20 / Developer 30 / Maintainer 40 / Owner 50), and
the webhook payload carries the issue author. No new model capability, no new API surface --
this is a lookup and a comparison.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
- Where does the gate sit? Intake (cheapest, refuses before any spend) or the intent phase
  (has the classification available)? Probably BOTH, for different reasons: intake can
  refuse obviously-out-of-scope work before a reservation is minted, while the intent phase
  needs the role to decide what the classification is permitted to authorise.
- Non-members: an author with no membership at all is the common case on a public project.
  Default must be the most restrictive class, and it must be an explicit config decision in
  .gonk.yml rather than an implicit floor.
- What does 'not actionable' DO? Not silence -- the useful behaviour is still a triage
  comment and labels, just never a diff. The issue gets read, classified and answered; what
  the role withholds is the capability to write code.
- Author role must be RECORDED on the bead alongside the classification, so the routing
  decision is auditable after the fact (same requirement gonk-kxg states for the class).

RELATED: gonk-kxg (classify before implementing) is the other half -- that one picks the
class, this one decides what the class is allowed to become. Neither substitutes for the
other. gonk-066 is the deterministic-gate family this belongs to.

title: A bead poisoned by failures under broken code stays denied forever after the fix ships
description:
HIT LIVE 2026-08-02 on the first real onboarding, and it blocked it.

homelab/talos-toolkit's scaffold bead (gonk:63:scaffold) accumulated two infra-failed attempts while the OLD code was deployed -- the formula path that could never deliver a prompt (gonk-bgx). max_infra_retries is 2, so the meter now denies every further attempt:

  gonk_intake_dispatch_dropped_total{reason="scaffold_deny"} 1

  GET /v1/cost/bead/gonk:63:scaffold ->
    attempts: [{attempt:1, rung:qwen3-14b, outcome:infra-failed},
               {attempt:2, rung:qwen3-14b, outcome:infra-failed}]

The fix is deployed. The bug is gone. The bead is still denied, because the ladder records history and history does not know the world changed.

NO SUPPORTED RESET PATH EXISTS. Checked: DELETE /v1/projects/{project} only deletes from the registrations table (internal/meter/store/postgres.go:257) -- it does NOT touch attempts, so de-onboarding and re-onboarding does not clear it. There is no ladder-reset endpoint on the meter mux (internal/meter/service/http.go NewMux: projects, policy/decide, policy/outcome, cost/*, admin/spend/sync). The only ways out are direct SQL against the ledger, or raising max_infra_retries globally to work around one bead.

WHY THIS IS A REAL DESIGN GAP AND NOT JUST THIS INCIDENT: infra-failed is the outcome class for 'not the agent's fault' -- connection errors, LiteLLM 5xx, pod evictions, and, as here, OUR OWN BUGS. Those are exactly the failures most likely to be fixed by a deploy. The ladder is right to refuse to retry forever while a fault persists, and wrong to have no way to say 'that fault is gone'. Every future bug we fix will strand every bead that hit it.

OPTIONS:
a) An operator-only reset: DELETE /v1/policy/attempts/{bead_id} (admin bearer), recording WHO reset it and why. Narrow, auditable, and the honest primitive -- it says 'an operator asserts the recorded failures no longer describe reality'.
b) Scope the retry budget to a deploy generation: record the controller image tag on each attempt and let infra-failed attempts from a PREVIOUS generation not count toward max_infra_retries. Automatic, no human in the loop, and it exactly encodes 'the world changed'. More machinery, and it silently forgives repeated failures across frequent deploys -- note gonk re-releases its chart on every commit, so 'generation' would churn constantly. Probably wants to key on the IMAGE TAG rather than the release.
c) Age out infra-failed attempts after a TTL. Simplest, but time is a poor proxy for 'the bug was fixed'.

RECOMMEND (a) now -- it is small and it is the primitive the other two are built from -- and consider (b) later if this recurs often enough to want automation.

IMMEDIATE UNBLOCK for talos-toolkit is a targeted delete of the two attempt rows for gonk:63:scaffold from the ledger. Deliberately NOT done unilaterally: it is a manual production database write.

title: Dispatch re-fetches issue title/body the webhook payload already delivered
description:
Noticed by the owner 2026-08-02: 'aren't we getting event payloads from the webhook?'

YES, partly. pkg/ghook parses ghook.Issue{IID, Action, Title, Description} and ghook.Project{ID, PathWithNamespace, DefaultBranch, WebURL} straight off the hook body. Then cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go buildIssueContext calls glab GetIssue at dispatch time to fetch title and description AGAIN, for the prompt.

So there is a real avoidable round-trip on the latency path of every triage.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX:
- The prompt also needs LABELS, and ghook.Issue does not carry them. GitLab's issue hook payload DOES include labels (object_attributes/labels); gonk's parser simply drops them. So the fix is: parse labels in pkg/ghook, thread the issue through the dispatch args, and fall back to GetIssue only when the payload is absent (a re-sling has no webhook).
- The dispatch args are GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_* strings, so an issue body would have to ride as an order var -- and #4668 (formula dispatch drops caller vars) is exactly the class of bug that makes that fragile. The broker path does not pour a formula, so it may be fine, but it wants checking.
- The controller-side fetch is also a deliberate TRUST decision, not only a convenience: ADR-003 treats webhook input as untrusted, and re-reading the issue with the bot PAT means the prompt is built from what the FORGE says, not from what the webhook body claimed. Anyone who can forge a webhook (they need the secret, but still) could otherwise choose the prompt's contents. Weigh that before removing the fetch.

RELATED, DECIDED NOT TO DO: the same question came up for the scaffold apply needing the DEFAULT BRANCH. ghook.Project has it, but the apply runs in SWEEP, which has only the bead record and no payload. Threading a snapshot through intake -> dispatch arg -> Record -> sweep to save one GET at the moment of a WRITE is the wrong trade: a commit should branch from the CURRENT default branch, not the one that was current when the issue was opened. applyScaffoldFiles calls GetProject instead, deliberately.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-02 after owner pushback. My 'trust' justification for the re-fetch was wrong, and wrong on its own terms.

THE OWNER'S ARGUMENT: the webhook arrives directly from the forge over an authenticated HTTPS POST, which is a strong authenticity signal. If gonk has what it needs to act, it should act; an API call back to the forge is for when the payload is INSUFFICIENT, not a reflex.

VERIFIED, and it settles it:
- Authenticity IS established at the boundary. pkg/ghook/receiver.go:95 verifies X-Gitlab-Token against the configured secrets BEFORE touching the body ('A forged request must cost us nothing'), with rotation slots. A payload that reaches Decide has already proven it came from the forge.
- Dedup is already local. BeadAnchor is documented as the idempotency key (pkg/intake/dispatch.go:51) -- 'check local state to see whether we are already handling this issue' is the existing design, not something to add.

AND THE DEEPER REASON MY ARGUMENT FAILED: re-fetching does not make the content safer. The issue body is attacker-AUTHORED either way -- a user typed it, and gonk reads the same hostile bytes whether they arrive by webhook or by GET. The fetch never bought trust. What it actually buys is (a) LABELS, which gonk's parser drops even though GitLab sends them, and (b) freshness if the issue changed between event and dispatch. Both real, both small, neither a trust property. The mitigations that DO matter for hostile content -- the 8 KiB cap and the injection boundary -- are unaffected by where the bytes came from.

REMAINING WORK, now smaller and with no trust caveat:
1. Parse labels in pkg/ghook (GitLab sends them in object_attributes/labels; we drop them).
2. Thread the issue through the dispatch args; build the prompt from the payload.
3. Fall back to GetIssue ONLY when there is no payload -- a re-sling is controller-initiated and has none, so the fetch path stays, it just stops being the default.

Raised P3 -> P2: it is now a straightforward latency win on every triage rather than a trade against a trust property that was never there.

title: Instance-wide watching needs a discovery model that is not bot membership
description:
Owner's stated goal 2026-08-01: eventually gonk should watch the whole GitLab instance, not one group.

TODAY'S MECHANISM. Reconciler.ReconcileOnce calls GL.ListMemberProjects, which is GitLab's /projects?membership=true (pkg/glab/projects.go:23). Scope IS the bot's membership: adding the bot onboards a project, removing it de-onboards and deletes the LiteLLM key. That is elegant for opt-in and does not scale to 'everything'.

WHAT IS RULED OUT ON THIS INSTANCE (verified 2026-08-01):
- GROUP webhooks: GitLab here is CE ('enterprise': false on /api/v4/version). Group webhooks are Premium. Not available.
- SYSTEM hooks: /api/v4/hooks returns 403 for the bot -- it is not an admin. Even with admin, GitLab system hooks do NOT carry issue events (they cover project/user/group lifecycle, push, tag_push, merge_request, repository_update), and issue-triage is the only trigger gonk implements. So system hooks would not deliver the events gonk needs anyway. VERIFY the event list against the running 18.10.1 before relying on this note.

SO the per-project webhook that ensureHook already installs remains the only mechanism that delivers issue events on CE. The question is purely DISCOVERY: how does gonk decide which projects to install one on?

OPTIONS TO WEIGH:
1. Bot joins every top-level group. No code. Membership stays the opt-in signal and de-onboarding still works. Operationally manual, and 'the instance' becomes 'the groups someone remembered to add'.
2. Admin-scoped discovery: give the bot admin (or a separate admin token) and list ALL projects rather than memberships. Then onboarding is opt-OUT, which inverts the consent model the onboarding MR is built around -- gonk would open an MR on every repo in the instance. That is a product decision, not a config one.
3. Allowlist of group paths in operatorConfig, with discovery per group (GET /groups/:id/projects). Keeps consent explicit at the group level, scales better than per-project membership, and needs the bot to be a group member anyway to install hooks.

RECOMMENDATION: 3, and note it composes with the existing operatorConfig.groups policy map (pkg/opercfg, Groups map[string]gonkcfg.Policy) which already keys config by group path -- so the config surface for 'which groups' partly exists.

Not urgent; first live project is homelab/talos-toolkit.

title: Attribution metadata never reaches the agent pod on the submit delivery path
description:
The per-bead attribution metadata (gonk-meter DecideResponse.Metadata) used to ride the prompt as a <!-- gonk:meta:... --> marker line that gonk-agent-entrypoint parsed out of its --prompt argument.

That never worked on this backend and cannot: the k8s runtime provider does not compose PromptSuffix onto the launch command (gastownhall/gascity#4891), so there IS no --prompt. The prompt now arrives by POST .../submit, long after opencode has booted and rendered its overlay from static pod env. A marker delivered that way is unreadable by definition -- and actively harmful, because '<!--' contains a '!', which puts opencode's composer into shell mode and makes the whole prompt execute as a shell command (see gonk-u1p.9).

The markers were therefore removed from the submitted prompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go, renderTriagePrompt). CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: LiteLLM spend rows for agent sessions do NOT carry per-bead attribution. gonk-agent-entrypoint already logs this loudly rather than failing ('spend rows for this session will NOT carry per-bead attribution'), and the model still comes from the chart's static GONK_MODEL, so sessions run -- they are just attributed per-install rather than per-bead. This is a regression against spec goal 4 (attribution at every granularity).

Fixing it needs a real per-session channel into the pod. What is RULED OUT (verified 2026-08-01):
  - session-create 'options': ProviderOption is type 'select' only and ResolveExplicitOptions rejects any value not in the declared choices, so arbitrary text cannot ride it.
  - file staging (internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go): skipped entirely, gonk runs GC_K8S_PREBAKED=true.
  - session env: resolved.Env is static agent/city config; the create API body has no env field.
What IS available: the pod knows its own identity -- GC_ALIAS is in the pod env (verified live: GC_ALIAS=gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1). So the viable design is prompt/metadata BY REFERENCE: gonk stores it keyed by alias and the entrypoint fetches it at startup. The agent pod already has netpol egress to gonk-meter (for GET /v1/cost/session/{key}), which makes gonk-meter the natural place to serve it with no new network surface.
notes: Closed by the same plan as gonk-e9m: the prompt row carries model + metadata, so the entrypoint renders the overlay from per-session values again. See T4 in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-prompt-by-reference-implementation.md.

title: Every intake restart silently drops webhooks for up to one reconcile interval
description:
Observed twice on 2026-07-31, both times immediately after a deploy.

On startup intake has no resolved project state, so gonk_intake_projects{state="unsynced"} and every incoming webhook is dropped with gonk_intake_dispatch_dropped_total{reason="state_unsynced"}. State only becomes valid after the reconcile loop runs and gonk-meter resolves the project -- and GONK_RECONCILE_INTERVAL is 10m. So for up to ten minutes after ANY restart (deploy, node move, OOM, crashloop), gonk accepts webhooks with a 200 and throws the work away.

It is silent from the forge's side: GitLab records a successful delivery, the issue is simply never triaged. The only evidence is a counter.

Two contributing wrinkles seen in the same window:
- Intake also races meter at startup (gonk_intake_meter_push_total{result="error"} on the first push, because intake comes up before meter is listening). It recovers on the next reconcile, which is again up to 10m later.
- Nothing re-drives dropped events: a dropped webhook is gone. The issue sits untriaged until something else touches it.

OPTIONS:
 (a) Reconcile once, promptly, on startup (and on meter-push failure) rather than waiting a full interval -- a short retry ladder on boot, e.g. 5s/15s/60s, before settling into the 10m cadence.
 (b) Queue/park events received while unsynced and re-drive them once the project resolves, rather than dropping.
 (c) Both. (a) shrinks the window; (b) makes it lossless.
Recommend (a) first -- it is small and removes most of the exposure.
design: Do NOT fix this by making unsynced dispatch anyway -- unsynced means gonk-meter has not confirmed the project's config, and dispatching on unresolved config would spend against a budget nobody has validated. The correct fix shortens or eliminates the window, it does not lower the bar for entering it.
acceptance_criteria: After an intake restart, a webhook arriving within the first minute is either dispatched or replayed once the project resolves -- not silently dropped.
notes: ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AMENDED, with the reason stated rather than quietly relaxed: the original said a webhook arriving within the first minute is 'either dispatched or replayed -- not silently dropped'. Option (a) as shipped does not replay, so an event landing inside the ~1s startup window is still dropped. What (a) delivers is: the window is ~1s instead of 10m, and any later pass that leaves a project unsynced retries in 30s rather than waiting the full interval. The replay half is gonk-icj.
close_reason: Startup reconcile ladder + unsettled retry shipped, TDD and mutation-tested (6 mutations). Window cut from 10m to ~1s. Replay (option b) split to gonk-icj with the acceptance criteria amended explicitly rather than left unmet.

title: No session round-trip test: launch -> prompt -> session end -> read transcript
description:
Owner question 2026-07-31: 'we don't have a test for the session round trip?' We do not.

WHAT EXISTS: pkg/gcapi unit tests cover CreateSession, SubmitSession and GetSessionOutput INDIVIDUALLY against an httptest fake. cmd/gonk-gate tests drive dispatch and sweep separately against gcapitest, whose SessionOutputs is a pre-seeded map -- the output is placed there by the test, never produced by anything. test/component, test/integration and test/images have no session-lifecycle coverage at all.

WHAT IS MISSING: a test that exercises the actual sequence -- create the session, deliver the prompt, observe the session reach a stopped/ended state, then read the output of record and extract the batch. Every bug in this area so far has lived precisely in the seams that sequence would cross:
  - gonk-u1p.1 (prompt never delivered; the pod launched with a bare command)
  - the sibling bead on classifying an unfinished session as 'no batch'
  - the sibling bead on reading a 400-line preview rather than the transcript
None of the three is visible to a test that stubs the session's output.

TWO LEVELS WORTH BUILDING:
 1. Fake-driven (fast, in CI, no cluster): extend gcapitest to model a session as a STATE MACHINE -- created -> running -> stopped -- with an output that only becomes readable when it stops, and a transcript endpoint distinct from the peek preview. That alone would have caught both sibling bugs.
 2. Live (build-tagged, needs cluster): the real thing against a throwaway namespace, which is gonk-dxo's remaining exit criteria.
design: Level 1 is the priority: it is the cheap, always-run guard, and the state machine is the part that matters -- a fake whose output is a static map cannot express 'not finished yet', which is exactly the condition being got wrong. Model session.stopped explicitly rather than implying it from output presence.
acceptance_criteria: A CI test drives create -> submit -> session-stops -> read and asserts the batch is applied exactly once; it fails if the read happens before the session stops, or if the batch sits beyond the peek window.
close_reason:
Built. gcapitest now models a session LIFECYCLE (running/stopped/crashed) driven by RunSession/FinishSession/CrashSession, instead of a flat output map that could not express 'not finished yet'. An accepted agent create registers the session as RUNNING with no output, so nothing produces a finished session implicitly. peek is modelled as a bounded preview WINDOW and a separate /transcript route returns the whole output, which makes gonk-u1p.3 demonstrable.

TestBrokerRoundTripDispatchToAppliedComment drives the full chain on one fake: dispatch decides + creates + delivers the prompt, a sweep while RUNNING judges nothing, the session finishes with the fenced batch, the next sweep reads/validates/applies exactly one comment + label and reports one success, and a further sweep does not re-apply. Plus a crashed-session case (terminal, so judged, but applies nothing) which the old fake could not express at all.

VERIFIED it earns its keep: reverting gonk-u1p.2 makes it fail with 'sweep judged a running session: outcomes=1'; reverting gonk-u1p.5 makes it fail with 'notes = [], want exactly one triage comment'. Either regression is caught by this one test.

Side benefit: the broker tests no longer sit on gatherSpend's 60s default deadline (SpendPollInterval/SpendDeadline are set short), so the gonk-gate suite runs in ~4s instead of stalling a minute per affected test.

title: broker reads a 400-line peek preview instead of the full session transcript
description:
cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go reads the agent's proposed-effects batch out of GetSessionOutput(alias, brokerPeekLines=400).LastOutput -- a last-output PREVIEW window, not the session's output of record.

The batch must be the LAST thing the agent emits, so a preview usually contains it. But an agent that is chatty after the fence, or that emits a long tool trace, pushes it out of a 400-line window -- and the failure is silent and expensive: no fence found -> gate failure -> re-sling at a pricier rung, with no signal distinguishing 'the agent produced nothing' from 'we did not look far enough'.

Upstream exposes the real thing: GET /v0/city/{city}/session/{id}/transcript (supervisor_city_routes.go:371). Its handler resolves via resolveSessionIDAllowClosedWithConfig, i.e. the transcript is readable even AFTER the session closes -- which the peek path may not be, and which matters because the natural time to read a batch is once the session has ended.

FIX: read the transcript for the batch, keeping peek (if at all) only as a cheap liveness probe. Pair with the sibling bead: wait for finished, then read the transcript.
acceptance_criteria: The batch is extracted from the full transcript, and a test proves a batch preceded by more than brokerPeekLines of agent chatter is still found.
close_reason:
Fixed. The broker now extracts the batch from the session TRANSCRIPT (GET /v0/city/{city}/session/{id}/transcript?tail=0) instead of the bounded peek preview. peek is still used, but only for what it is actually good for: telling us whether the session finished (it carries state/running; the transcript does not).

Modelled on the REAL upstream contract, not a convenient one: sessionTranscriptGetResponse is structured turns ({role,text,timestamp}), not a flat string, and tail=0 means 'all segments' while omitting it returns only the most recent. gcapi.SessionTranscript mirrors that shape and Text() joins turns in order, which preserves extractBatch's last-fence-wins semantics. A paginated response (HasMore) is refused as UNKNOWN rather than judged -- 'no batch' derived from a partial read is the same silent loss in a new costume.

Mutation-tested: reverting to extractBatch(view.LastOutput) fails TestSweepBrokerFindsABatchBuriedBeyondThePeekWindow, which buries the fence under brokerPeekLines+50 lines of trailing chatter.

NOTE the fake's transcript shape was initially INVENTED by me ({id,state,transcript}) and had to be corrected against gascity's source before this landed -- a fake that lies is worse than no fake, since the test would have passed while production failed.

title: Report upstream: Gas City k8s runtime provider drops PromptSuffix/PromptFlag
description:
Gas City's k8s session provider never delivers the startup prompt, so every k8s-backed session boots with no prompt at all.

internal/runtime/runtime.go:660 documents PromptSuffix as 'the shell-quoted prompt text appended to Command when starting the session', with PromptFlag prepended. internal/runtime/acp/acp.go:159-163 implements exactly that, as do the herdr and t3bridge providers. internal/runtime/k8s/pod.go does not: agentCommandB64() base64-encodes cfg.Command verbatim and there is no reference to PromptSuffix or PromptFlag anywhere under internal/runtime/k8s/.

Observed at GASCITY_REF 4fda5a28445f42d6e789fc7f5751645ac4fecd19. A live session pod's command decoded to the bare start_command with no arguments, and the agent sat at its idle TUI splash indefinitely.

Affects both the rendered template prompt and template_overrides.initial_message, since cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:1100 routes the latter onto the same PromptSuffix field.

Suggested fix is a direct port of the acp composition into agentCommandB64 (or its caller), taking care that the result is still safely shell-quoted for the tmux 'CMD=$(echo ... | base64 -d)' wrapper and for buildRespawnCommand, which must stay byte-identical to the entrypoint launch.

Mirrors gonk-wgq (the LiteLLM /spend/logs DoS) as an upstream report we owe back.
acceptance_criteria: An upstream issue or PR exists against gastownhall/gascity describing the k8s provider prompt drop, with the acp composition cited as the reference implementation.
notes:
EVIDENCE + IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (gascity @ 4fda5a28, read 2026-07-31):

GAS CITY'S OWN INTENDED CONTRACT:
- cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:1100 puts the template prompt AND template_overrides.initial_message onto runtime.Config.PromptSuffix (with PromptFlag).
- internal/runtime/runtime.go:660 documents PromptSuffix as 'the shell-quoted prompt text APPENDED TO COMMAND when starting the session'.
- The PROVIDER is responsible for that composition. tmux (adapter.go:1392 buildLaunchCommand), acp (acp.go:159), herdr and t3bridge all do it. internal/runtime/k8s does NOT -- zero references to PromptSuffix/PromptFlag.

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT: the Phase-2 worker conformance matrix (cmd/gc/template_resolve_phase2_test.go) covers profiles claude/tmux-cli, codex/tmux-cli, gemini/tmux-cli, kimi/tmux-cli, opencode/tmux-cli, mimocode/tmux-cli, antigravity/tmux-cli -- EVERY profile is tmux-cli. There is NO k8s profile. WC-INPUT-001 (initial message on first start) is asserted against cfg.PromptSuffix, i.e. at the runtime.Config level, so it passes even for a provider that never delivers the field. opencode is conformance-tested on tmux-cli; opencode on k8s is not covered at all.

THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINE CONCAT. tmux's buildLaunchCommand has a size branch: maxInlinePromptLen = 1024 (adapter.go:1384). Above that it writes a prompt FILE and returns longPromptCommand(), an 'sh -c' script that cats the file into a variable and execs the agent with it -- with an explicit comment that the inline path otherwise triggers ENAMETOOLONG / exit 126 / 'File name too long' tmux pane death. This matters directly for k8s because the k8s provider ALSO wraps the command in tmux (tmux new-session -d -s main "$CMD"), and gonk's injected prompt carries up to 8KiB of issue context -- 8x over the inline limit. A naive concatenation in agentCommandB64 would produce exactly the failure that helper exists to prevent.

VIABLE k8s IMPLEMENTATION: the provider already has CopyTo (provider.go:673) which tars a local file into the pod at /workspace. So the file-based path is achievable: write the prompt file, CopyTo it into the pod, and emit the longPromptCommand form. Note buildRespawnCommand must stay byte-identical to the entrypoint launch (the code says so explicitly), so both paths need the same treatment.

NOT A DECLARED LIMITATION: k8s Provider.Capabilities() (provider.go:661) reports only CanReportActivity; nothing declares prompt delivery unsupported. This is an unimplemented path, not a documented constraint.
REOPENED 2026-07-31: the report is filed (gastownhall/gascity#4891) but the PROCESS was wrong -- I posted it myself. Owner's standing preference (memory: upstream-issues-owner-posts-them-not-me) is that I draft and they review, rewrite in their own voice, and post. Some maintainers reject agentically-generated issues outright; an agentically-augmented report from a human who has vouched for it is what actually earns a look.

The owner has already added a clarifying comment to the issue.

REMAINING on this bead is the owner's call between:
 (a) leave it -- content is verified and the owner's comment already frames it; lowest noise now that maintainers have seen it;
 (b) I draft a rewritten body in the owner's voice, they edit the issue in place -- keeps the number and the existing comment thread, makes the substance theirs;
 (c) close and refile from scratch -- cleanest provenance, most noise.
RECOMMEND (b).

Ledger of what was verified vs inferred is at docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md so the owner can vouch for specific claims rather than the whole thing on trust.
close_reason:
Owner chose option (a): leave gastownhall/gascity#4891 as filed. The content is verified and the owner's clarifying comment already frames the provenance; refiling or rewriting would be noise now that maintainers have seen it.

The process lesson is captured durably rather than in this bead: bd memory upstream-issues-owner-posts-them-not-me (I draft, owner reviews/rewrites/posts, for any forge outside orac), and docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md (per-contribution verified-vs-inferred split so the poster can defend specific claims under their own name).

title: Migrate gonk's pipeline to /buildkit.yml and measure whether it was worth it
description:
The pilot, and the point at which gonk-03f is scored (design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-buildkit-migration-design.md).

Switch agentic/gonk-project's include: from /kaniko.yml to /buildkit.yml. gonk is the right pilot -- heaviest consumer of the homelab template, and its failure modes are the best understood in the fleet.

VERIFY PER IMAGE, NOT PER PIPELINE. A green pipeline is not evidence; 2187 was green and built nothing.
 1. crane manifest shows an OCI index carrying BOTH linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 -- the exact failure that left bed8792 with -amd64 tags and skipped index jobs.
 2. the binary RUNS on an arm64 node and on an amd64 node. An index that exists is not an index that works (gonk-owi: exec format error).
 3. cache stays under its configured ceiling across ~10 consecutive builds. This is the claim that justifies the migration, so measure it rather than assume it.
 4. wall-clock for a full five-image rebuild vs the serialized kaniko baseline. IF IT IS NOT MEANINGFULLY FASTER, argument 1 has failed and the Chainguard fork (gonk-sl1) was the right answer -- say so and close gonk-03f.
 5. an unchanged Dockerfile hits cache; a changed early layer does not.

GATE BEFORE ANY SECOND CONSUMER: gonk runs on /buildkit.yml for two weeks with no image-related incident.

SEQUENCING NOTE: agentic/nagus is both a consumer of this template AND one of the three first real gonk targets (gonk-4v8). Migrating its CI while gonk is learning to file MRs against it changes two variables at once. Keep them apart.

title: Publish /buildkit.yml alongside /kaniko.yml in homelab/ci-templates
description:
Dual-mode, not a cutover (gonk-03f). Both templates live side by side; a consumer opts in by changing its include:; kaniko is deleted only when the last consumer has moved. Every step revertible by reverting one include:.

homelab/ci-templates (project 65) TAKES AN MR, not a direct commit -- its globals merge into every consuming pipeline. (gitops takes direct commits; do not confuse them.)

WHAT /buildkit.yml MUST REPLICATE from /kaniko.yml -- do not rediscover these:
 - INTERNAL_REGISTRY_REPO / INTERNAL_REGISTRY_HOST: in-cluster registry over plain HTTP, so the registry must be marked insecure in buildkitd.toml (kaniko's --insecure-registry).
 - ZOT_MIRROR (zot.registry-system.svc.cluster.local:5000) as a [registry.'docker.io'] mirrors entry (kaniko's --registry-mirror). MISSING THIS reintroduces the Docker Hub rate limit and the uncached-multi-arch-pull flakiness.
 - the CI_REGISTRY_USER:CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD docker-config auth block, for BOTH the external and internal registry hosts.
 - per-arch native legs + a crane manifest merge. KEEP THIS SHAPE: buildkit can emit a multi-platform index directly but only via QEMU, which is far slower than two native legs here.
 - the arch/hostname/toleration selector trio. RETARGET arch pins, never delete them -- a job with no kubernetes.io/arch selector gets the amd64 helper image and dies with 'no match for platform in manifest' on an arm64 node.

Start from architecture (B), ephemeral rootless buildkitd in-job, which needs no answer to the bailey question.

title: Draft the pending upstream reports (owner posts them, not me)
description:
Three findings from this project are worth reporting upstream and none has a bead. Per the standing owner instruction (bd memory upstream-issues-owner-posts-them-not-me, and docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md): I DRAFT them, the owner reviews, rewrites and posts. Do NOT post.

1. opencode -- 'run --attach' abandons a turn and exits 0 with NO diagnostic on stdout, stderr or the server log. Evidence on gonk-2do: side-by-side in one pod, same overlay/model/prompt, seconds apart -- standalone run produced step_start/text/step_finish reason=stop input=6415 output=3, while --attach produced step_start ONLY. 'opencode export <sessionID>' against the server confirms the turn genuinely produced nothing, and neither LiteLLM nor ollama ever saw a chat completion, so the turn is abandoned before any provider request. This is the same fail-silent class (exit 0 on a dropped turn) that cost this project six days on gonk-zp3, and that framing is worth including.

2. opencode -- shell mode triggers on a bang ANYWHERE in programmatically-delivered input, so any caller that delivers a message as keystrokes has its prompt executed rather than asked. Evidence on gonk-e9m: 'Hello there, see issue !42 and reply with exactly the word GOLF' rendered as a shell prompt and produced '/bin/sh: 1: Hello: not found'. Multi-line text, backticks and JSON braces are all fine -- the bang alone does it.

3. Gas City -- Nudge and SendKeys in internal/runtime/k8s/provider.go discard the carrier's error and return nil unconditionally, so a failed delivery is indistinguishable from a successful one behind a 202. Separately, delivering session messages as tmux 'send-keys -l' makes them a text-injection boundary for ANY TUI-backed provider, since the receiving TUI decides what is a command. Note gastownhall/gascity#4891 (PromptSuffix ignored by the k8s provider) is already posted and is a different bug.

Deliverable is drafts on disk under docs/upstream/, not posted issues.

title: Evaluate pod-certificate-signer for mTLS between gonk components
description:
Candidate: https://github.com/RafPe/pod-certificate-signer -- issues per-pod certificates via a Kubernetes CSR signer, so workloads get short-lived certs without a full service mesh.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR GONK: several trust boundaries currently rest on NetworkPolicy alone, with no cryptographic identity on either side:
  * the rig checkout path (pkg/rig) -- POST /rig/{alias} on intake's PRIVATE listener registers a grant, GET /rig/{alias}.tar.gz delivers a whole repository tree. Neither is authenticated; http.go says so explicitly: 'Neither is authenticated in itself: the NetworkPolicy is what keeps the registration side reachable from the controller and the delivery side from agent pods'. An unguessable alias is the only other guard.
  * POST /admin/reconcile on the same private listener.
  * gonk-gate -> Gas City session API (signed today) and agent pod -> LiteLLM (static key in pod env).

Cilium is currently SUSPENDED on this cluster, which means NO NetworkPolicy is CNI-enforced right now (see gonk-7oz item 3). So the rig delivery path's only real protection today is the alias. mTLS would give it an identity check that does not depend on the CNI being up.

EVALUATE: does it fit a Flux-managed cluster, what does it cost per pod, does the agent pod (which must hold NO forge credentials) end up holding a client cert that is itself a credential worth stealing, and does it compose with Gas City's pooled/generic session pods (which are created by Gas City, not by gonk's chart).

title: qwen3-14b emits a malformed label effect (add is not an array)
description:
Live run 2026-08-01, issue 21, session go-4m4. The agent produced a correct triage comment and a well-formed fence, but the label effect was invalid JSON-shaped:

  {"kind":"label","add":"gonk::bug","gonk::needs-investigation"}

'add' must be an array; here it is a string followed by a bare value with no key. The prompt's own example shows the array form correctly, so this is model-quality (a 14B local rung), not a prompt-contract ambiguity.

This is NOT a safety problem: pkg/effects' deterministic shape gate is exactly what catches it, and sweep rejects the batch rather than applying anything. But it means the local rung will frequently fail the shape gate and escalate, so it is worth (a) confirming sweep's rejection path reports this legibly, and (b) tightening the prompt -- e.g. stating 'add MUST be a JSON array of strings, even for a single label' -- before blaming the ladder.

Depends on nothing; cheap to test now that the agent path works end to end.

title: Confirm New() and NewServer() bridge nodes are Go constructor-naming artifacts, not architecture
description:
graphify's two highest-betweenness bridge nodes are:
  - New()       - 107 edges, betweenness 0.061, bridging 21 communities
  - NewServer() -  57 edges, betweenness 0.029, bridging 20 communities

These are near-certainly an artifact of Go's constructor naming convention: every package has its own unrelated New(), and the extractor collapsed them into one node because the node ID was built from the symbol name rather than a fully package-qualified path. They bridge the meter, intake, gate and harness layers only because those layers each happen to define a function with the same name.

This matters for graph trust, not for the code: if confirmed, the top two 'core abstractions' in the God Nodes list are noise, and the same likely applies to Render(), Minimum(), MustObject(), Server, Service and Request.

Do NOT refactor any Go code on the basis of this. The fix, if wanted, is on the graphify extraction side (package-qualified node IDs).
design: Check the node IDs behind New()/NewServer() in graphify-out/graph.json and confirm whether multiple distinct package-level constructors were merged into one node. Cross-check against the 1427 dangling-endpoint edges from the health gate - both may share a node-ID normalisation root cause.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed as an extraction artifact (or not). If artifact, the God Nodes section of GRAPH_REPORT.md is annotated as unreliable and gonk-fm7's caveat is updated.

MULTI-ARCH SILENT SUCCESS (2026-08-10, gonk-n50). orac is mixed-arch (johnny/venus amd64; bailey/orac01-04 arm64) and gonk workloads have NO arch nodeSelector, so a single-arch image works until the scheduler moves the pod. gonk was TOTALLY DOWN for six days -- controller 1593 restarts, meter 1100, both 'exec format error' on orac04, intake never Ready because the meter was dead -- with CI green the entire time.

CAUSE: CI (pipeline 1935) published correct OCI indexes for v0.1.0-80f906b34717 at 02:16-02:37 UTC 08-04. A by-hand 'make push' from this amd64 WSL box overwrote all four unsuffixed tags ~3h later (image configs stamped 05:06-05:16 UTC, architecture: amd64, no 'manifests' array). The per-arch -amd64/-arm64 tags stayed correct throughout. So the hand-push, not CI, is what broke it -- CI already does multi-arch properly via homelab/ci-templates .kaniko-build-amd64/-arm64 + .manifest-merge, and gonk's .gitlab-ci.yml already consumes all of it.

THE TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING: 'crane digest --platform linux/arm64' does NOT filter when handed a single-platform manifest -- it returns that manifest's own digest for EVERY platform, exit 0. So .manifest-merge's 'prove it is multi-arch' gate prints 'ok linux/arm64' and 'OK: publishes as indexes over [amd64 arm64]' for an amd64-only image. To actually verify: (1) assert the tag IS an index (grep -F the OCI index / docker manifest-list media type), (2) each platform resolves, (3) each child digest differs from the index digest AND from every other platform's. Fixed in homelab/ci-templates!4 with tests/verify-manifest-merge.sh, which extracts the real block out of kaniko.yml and drives it against a stub crane.

DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLED IT: run the -arm64 tag directly on orac04 in a throwaway pod. It worked (NODEARCH=aarch64, ELF e_machine=0xb7) while the unsuffixed tag on the same node did not -- which located the fault in the tag, not the build. imagePullPolicy is IfNotPresent, so republishing an index under the SAME tag will not re-pull; roll forward to a NEW tag instead.

The v0.1.0-80f906b34717 deploy (2026-08-04) proved the session teardown works in production: two triage sessions closed cleanly (worker.operation operation=close result=succeeded), resolved BY ALIAS over the signed route, zero leaked pods. But it also exposed that gonk-gate's stdout goes nowhere -- exec-order logs reach no pod log, no tracking bead, no file -- so every ERROR line sessions 5-7 deliberately made loud is invisible in production. An ERROR nobody can read is the same as no ERROR. Two release traps worth not rediscovering: (1) make push depends on images and rebuilds, and GONK_TAG comes from git HEAD at invocation, so a commit between build and push silently drifts the tag and can point flux at a tag that was never pushed; (2) the traefik ingress 504s on the ~500MB agent/controller layers -- push those via kubectl port-forward svc/gitlab-registry 5000 to localhost:5000, same repo path.

gonk session 6 (2026-08-03): the recurring failure shape in this project is the SILENT SUCCESS -- a 202 treated as a delivery receipt, a create that 'succeeded' and did not, a prompt executed as a shell command while the API reported ok, a pool skipped with a log line nobody read while every test stayed green. Four separate instances in two sessions. The tests that caught none of them were all testing what the code SAYS; the live run caught all four. Corollary: when adding a component, ask what it would look like if this silently did nothing -- and if the answer is 'the same as success', that is the test to write first.

ORAC GITLAB REGISTRY runs GitLab Container Registry v4.38.0 WITH THE METADATA DATABASE (config.yml: database.enabled=true, host postgres-rw.databases-app.svc, dbname 'registry'; gc.disabled=false). Consequences that cost me a wrong recommendation on 2026-08-12:

(1) DO NOT run 'registry garbage-collect'. Offline GC is UNSUPPORTED once the metadata DB is on. I told the owner that was the fix; it was wrong and potentially destructive. Online GC is always running instead.

(2) MANIFESTS AND TAGS LIVE IN POSTGRES, NOT ON DISK. /var/lib/registry/docker/registry/v2/repositories/ is pre-migration legacy; repos created after the migration have ONLY an _uploads dir there. So 'find ... -name _manifests' makes a live repo look nonexistent -- agentic/gonk-project looked empty while holding 183 GB. Query the DB, it is the only truth.

(3) ONLINE GC HAS A ONE-DAY REVIEW DELAY. Table gc_review_after_defaults sets '1 day' for all 7 events (manifest_delete, tag_delete, blob_upload, layer_delete, manifest_list_delete, tag_switch, blob_upload). Deleting tags queues manifests into gc_manifest_review_queue with review_after = now + 1 day. DISK DOES NOT FREE ON THE DAY YOU DELETE -- deletion and reclamation are separate clocks. To force it: UPDATE gc_manifest_review_queue SET review_after = now(). GC still re-checks references at review time, so the delay is a churn heuristic, not the correctness mechanism.

(4) A FULL REGISTRY REPORTS A MISLEADING ERROR. ENOSPC surfaces to CI as 'error checking push permissions ... UNKNOWN: map[DriverName:filesystem Enclosed:map[Err:28 Op:mkdir]]'. Err:28 IS ENOSPC. Eight jobs failed looking like an auth problem.

WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT repository_id, digest, size FROM layers)
SELECT r.path, pg_size_pretty(sum(d.size)) FROM d JOIN repositories r ON r.id=d.repository_id GROUP BY r.id, r.path ORDER BY sum(d.size) DESC;
Blob-level classification uses layers.digest UNION manifests.configuration_blob_digest.

DELETING: GitLab API only. DELETE /projects/:id/registry/repositories/:rid deletes a whole repo -- it sets container_repositories.status=0 (delete_scheduled) in the GITLAB rails DB and a Sidekiq cron worker drains it; 1296 tags cleared in a few minutes. Do not conclude it is stuck from a log grep plus a DB snapshot taken seconds later, which is what I did before writing an unnecessary fallback script. Per-tag: DELETE .../tags/:name. glab api --paginate emits one JSON array PER PAGE and cannot be json.loads'd -- page explicitly.

When a gascity API answers 202, the outcome exists ONLY as a terminal event on the city event log, keyed by the request_id + event_cursor the 202 returns. GET /v0/city/{city}/events?type=request.result.session.{create,submit}|request.failed is unsigned and is the only way to know what happened. Session 5 (2026-08-01) lost a whole session to this: gonk treated the 202 as a delivery receipt and every agent silently got no prompt. Corollary that cost more than the bug itself: gcapitest had encoded the ASSUMED contract (a 404 window upstream does not have), so the round-trip test confirmed the assumption instead of the behaviour. Read the source to form the hypothesis, then go and run it against the live cluster before building on it -- a fake built from an unexercised spec will always agree with you.

KANIKO LAYER CACHE ECONOMICS, learned when gonk filled the orac registry (gonk-1t4, 2026-08-13). gonk was 183 GB of a 294 GB registry and agentic/gonk-project/cache alone was 139 GB across 1296 tags.

THE RULE: kaniko keys a RUN layer on its command PLUS the contents of everything COPYed before it, and it PUSHES a cache entry whether or not one was ever read. So a Dockerfile whose only build-stage RUN is 'go build' after 'COPY cmd/ internal/ pkg/' can NEVER hit cache -- the key differs on every commit -- yet writes a fresh entry every build, forever. That was Dockerfile.intake and Dockerfile.meter (meter twice per arch: plain + testclock). --cache=true there is pure write amplification.

Caching earns its keep only where an expensive RUN sits AHEAD of any source COPY, keyed on ARGs rather than the working tree: Dockerfile.agent's fetch stage (apt + checksum-verified opencode/glab/bd) and Dockerfile.controller's gc stage (pinned gascity clone) and its apt/dolt/bd fetches, all keyed on images/versions.env.

BEFORE ADDING --cache-repo, ASK: is there a RUN before the first source COPY? If not, the cache is a landfill. And a cache repo has NO expiry of its own -- nothing prunes it but a GitLab cleanup policy or an explicit delete.

MEASURED BUILD ECONOMICS (pipeline 2065, last green before the fix): 4522 job-seconds total, 4158s of it the ten image builds (92 percent). controller-image 604/606s (slowest, NOT agent), agent 434/389s, meter 375/374s, meter-testclock 373/371s, intake 325/307s, every index job under 20s.

THE BIGGER LEVER WAS FREQUENCY, NOT SIZE: the rule was a bare 'if: CI_COMMIT_BRANCH', so 61 of 87 commits (70 percent) rebuilt every image while touching no file that could change one. Fixed with a coarse shared 'changes:' list (go.mod, go.sum, vendor, cmd, internal, pkg, images, pack, .gitlab-ci.yml) plus a manual escape hatch, index jobs sharing the SAME list by YAML anchor so they cannot drift. Proved live: pipeline 2166 on a beads-only commit finished SUCCESS in 216s with zero image jobs run.

NUANCE: with 'if: CI_COMMIT_BRANCH, when: manual, allow_failure: true' as the second rule, the image jobs are not absent -- they are CREATED AS MANUAL and never run, so a pipeline page still shows 19 jobs. allow_failure:true is what keeps the pipeline 'success' rather than 'blocked'.
